author: dosthcpp
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip companies have a human role hierarchy (viewer < operator < admin < owner) enforced by `humanRoleRank` for member management.
> - #7786: `POST /companies/:companyId/invites` only checks the `users:invite` permission and accepts any `humanRole` — so an admin can mint an **owner** invite and escalate themselves or others (verified repro in the issue).
> - The member-removal path already guards with `humanRoleRank` ("you can only remove users below your role"); the invite path simply never got the equivalent guard.
> - This PR validates the **effective** invite role (human invites default to `operator` when no role is requested) against the actor's resolved company role.
> - Non-board actors (agents) have no membership role; they are capped at the legacy default (`operator`) so ordinary agent-created invites keep working while privileged grants are blocked.
> - The benefit is the role hierarchy can no longer be bypassed via invites.

## What Changed

- `server/src/routes/access.ts` (invite creation route): compute the effective human role; resolve the actor's role via the existing `resolveActorHumanRole`; reject with **403** when `humanRoleRank[requested] > humanRoleRank[actor]` (agents capped at operator). Local-implicit/instance-admin actors resolve to owner as before.
- `server/src/__tests__/invite-create-route.test.ts`: 4 new route tests — admin→owner **403**, operator→admin **403**, admin→admin **201**, operator default-role invite **201**; the existing local-implicit test still passes.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/__tests__/invite-create-route.test.ts` → 5/5 pass.
- Server `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Risks

- Low risk: reuses the established `humanRoleRank`/`resolveActorHumanRole` primitives. Owners and local-implicit/instance-admin actors are unaffected (rank 4 grants everything). The one behavior change beyond the vuln: agents can no longer mint admin/owner invites — they keep the operator-default path, which matches the hierarchy intent. Agent-only invites (`allowedJoinTypes: "agent"`) carry no human role and are untouched.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 4.8 (`claude-opus-4-8`), extended reasoning, via Claude Code (tool use + local test execution).

Closes #7786. Related contributions: #7864 (#7840), #7865 (#7656), #7819 (#7795), #7814 (#7790), #7809 (#7685).

## Dedup search

- [x] I searched the open and recently-closed GitHub PRs for similar or duplicate PRs (invite role validation / privilege escalation) and found none addressing this.

author: jaspercurry
body:
You asked me to build PR-3b (the leader DAC-content reader). Doing so meant reading the real `jasper-outputd` `run_alsa` loop — and that surfaced a **design-level blocker** the §2 inv-2 design did not account for. So this PR corrects the design instead of shipping a known-wrong reroute.

## The blocker
`jasper-outputd/src/lib.rs`: **"Assistant/TTS ingress is owned by `jasper-fanin`."** So on the live ALSA path, TTS is mixed into the music **upstream of outputd** — it's inside the `content_buf` that `run_alsa` writes to the DAC (`write_dac_period(&content_buf)`) and taps to the snapfifo (`ref_outputs.publish(&content_buf)`). Two consequences:

1. **The naive dual-read would drop the leader's assistant audio.** Swapping the leader's DAC to the music-only buffered round-trip (`dac_content`) means the TTS fanin mixed into `content_buf` never reaches the speaker — the leader goes *silent on the assistant* mid-session. A serious regression for a voice speaker.
2. **The already-shipped `SnapfifoSink` leaks TTS to followers.** It taps `content_buf` (= music + TTS), so followers hear the leader's TTS — a **latent inv-3 violation** in the merged producer (V1 is leader-local TTS only).

## What inv-2 actually requires
TTS must be **separated**: a `jasper-fanin` music-only stream for the leader's tap (so followers get no TTS) **plus** a post-round-trip TTS re-mix onto `dac_content` (so the leader still hears the assistant). That's materially larger than "a FIFO reader" and re-opens *where TTS mixes* — so PR-3b can't be correctly built as a DAC-source swap until TTS separation lands.

## Why no code
A gated reroute that's known to break assistant audio on the leader is a landmine, not progress — shipping it even off-by-default would be dishonest. The `DacContentSource` FIFO reader (a clean mirror of `snapfifo.rs`) is the right music-half component; it lands with the corrected, TTS-aware integration, not before.

Docs only: the BLOCKER + corrected contract at the top of §2 "inv-2 realization", §0 + footer updated.

author: copilot
body:
Full-codebase review pass per the problem statement: hunt for bugs and miswired features, apply improvements, and bring the README up to date. Findings were produced by line-level review of every module and individually verified against call sites before fixing. All existing tests pass (403), plus clean code review and CodeQL runs.

## Correctness fixes

- **GPU GQA attention was silently wrong** (`backend/mod.rs`, `attention.wgsl`): the KV buffer was sized/strided by `num_heads × head_dim` while `kv_cache_insert` writes `num_kv_heads × head_dim` rows, and the shader mapped each query head 1:1 to its own KV row. For any GQA model, query heads ≥ `num_kv_heads` attended over zeros. KV stride is now `num_kv_heads × head_dim` and the shader maps query heads to their GQA group:
  ```wgsl
  let kv_dim = pc.num_kv_heads * pc.head_dim;
  let kv_h   = h * pc.num_kv_heads / pc.num_heads;
  ```
  Also fixed the `layer_offset` u64→u32 **byte**-offset truncation for deep models — it is now passed in f32 elements with an explicit range guard. `BackendBox::init`/`try_new` gain a `num_kv_heads` parameter (0 = MHA).
- **`moe_step` 2nd-order Markov prefetch never matched** (`engine.rs`): the lookup key was `(t-2, t)` but the predictor trains on consecutive `(prev, current)` pairs via `observe_step2`. Now reads `last_experts` (which holds t-1 pre-update), matching `generate`'s effective key.
- **FP8 e4m3 NaN decoded to ±448** (`mla.rs`): the `S.1111.111` NaN bit-pattern was clamped to the max finite value, injecting extreme outliers into matmuls. Now decodes to 0.0.

## Concurrency fixes

- **`ExpertCache::insert` TOCTOU** (`expert_cache.rs`): the lock was dropped between the capacity check and `push`, so a concurrent fill let `LruCache::push` silently evict a *pinned* entry. Capacity check, pre-evict, and push are now one critical section (lock order matches `evict_lru`).
- **Session `in_flight` leak on cancellation** (`session.rs`, `server.rs`): a client disconnect mid-generation dropped the task before `put()`, leaving the in-flight marker forever and permanently locking that session id. `take()` now returns an RAII `SessionCheckout` guard whose `Drop` releases the marker (token-checked via `remove_if`); `put()` consumes the guard.
- **`BufferPool` lost wakeups** (`buffer_pool.rs`): primary and shadow waiters shared one `Notify`, so a shadow-buffer drop could consume a primary waiter's wakeup (and vice versa). Each half now has its own `Notify`.
- **Speculation resumed under High pressure** (`batch_scheduler.rs`): contradicted the documented ladder (Critical→suspend, Normal→resume) and oscillated the pool back into Critical. Resumes only at Normal.
- **Tracing span held across `.await`** (`middleware.rs`): `span.enter()` guard crossed the `next.run(req).await` boundary, corrupting span nesting on the multi-threaded runtime. Switched to `Instrument::instrument`.

## Wiring / config

- `distributed.enabled = true` silently no-oped without `real_transformer.enabled = true`; `Config::validate` now rejects this (noted in `docs/distributed.md`).
- `affinity_neighbors_k` TOML default (2) aligned with the CLI/README default (4).
- `expert_0000.bin` filename mismatches: the engine writes `expert_<id>.bin` unpadded, so the io_uring integration test always panicked and `quickstart.sh`/`bench_turbo10.sh` regenerated the dataset on every run.
- Minor: removed provably-unreachable `% 2` length check in `grpc.rs`, TUI URL without a port now defaults to `:8080` (engine default) instead of `:80`, removed dead `last_used` write in `take()`.

## README / docs

- `mer-cli` → actual binary name `micro-expert-router` throughout.
- "Two built-in math backends" → three (`ScalarBackend`, `GpuBackend`, `CandleBackend`), with a note on the now-GQA-aware GPU attention.
- Corrected pressure-ladder description (resume only at Normal) and `affinity_neighbors_k` default.

body:
## Summary

The walker detected `Fusion.CreateSummonEff` (binding and inline `c:RegisterEffect(...)` forms) but not `Fusion.RegisterSummonEff` — the self-registering variant that forwards to CreateSummonEff and registers the effect itself (proc_fusion_spell.lua). Four corpus cards use it: c24094653, c58570206, c7614732, c89190953.

**Commit 1 — translator**
- Top-level statement `Fusion.RegisterSummonEff(c, ...)` synthesizes an anonymous registered `EffectSkeleton` with `fusion_summon_spec` + `SummonHelperOp` decoded via `FUSION_CREATE_SUMMON_EFF_PARAMS` (same wiring pattern as the `Ritual.AddProc*` branch from #108).
- Binding form `local e1=Fusion.RegisterSummonEff{...}` marks `registered` at creation (no `c:RegisterEffect(e1)` follows).
- **Latent mis-emit fix**: `plain_helper_op_from_call` treated a parenthesized named-args table (`Fusion.CreateSummonEff({handler=c, fusfilter=..., stage2=...})`) as positional and skipped the table as the "handler" arg — decoding zero params and emitting an over-permissive bare line. Exposed by the new pass on Spiral Fusion (c38590361) / Dark Fusion (c94820406); now decodes via `named_table_params`, so both correctly skip on `stage2`.
- **apply Pass A3**: lone-summon-helper cards never got skeleton `effect` blocks at corpus generation, so Pass A/A2 had nothing to fill. When the .ds has zero effect blocks and the walk yields exactly one summon-helper skeleton with a decodable line, inject the standard activation block. Idempotent via the no-effect-blocks guard.
- 6 unit tests following the `plain_helper_*` conventions.

**Commit 2 — corpus**
- c24094653 (Polymerization, `Fusion.RegisterSummonEff(c)`, no params) gains the bare `fusion_summon (1, fusion monster)` activation block.

author: sabihusman
body:
## Summary

Adds bottom-of-page **Previous / Next** topic navigation to every topic page, site-wide via the shared topics layout — no per-page hand-editing. The topic order is now a single source of truth that drives both the contents page and the prev/next buttons.

## Implementation

- **`app/topicList.js`** (new shared module): the ordered `TOPIC_ROWS`, parsed into `TOPICS` (flat, ordered, with `slug`/`href`), `SECTIONS` (grouped for contents), and `neighbors(slug) → { prev, next }`. The sequence is treated as one list that **crosses the AI/SQL section boundary**.
- **`app/page.jsx`**: now imports `SECTIONS` from the shared module — the order data is no longer duplicated. Reordering a topic in `topicList.js` updates the contents page *and* every page's nav automatically.
- **`app/topics/TopicNav.jsx`** (client): derives the current slug from `usePathname()`, looks up neighbors, and renders `← Previous / <title>` on the left and `Next → / <title>` on the right. First topic hides Previous, last hides Next (a spacer keeps the lone button aligned). Mono direction eyebrow + serif destination title, using the existing tokens.
- **`app/topics/layout.jsx`**: renders `<TopicNav />` at the bottom of the prose column, so all 16 topics get it without touching any topic page or component.

No topic content, prose, or visualization was changed.

## Behavior verified
- `usePathname` resolves at **static prerender**, so each page's static HTML already contains the correct neighbors (not just after hydration):
  - gradient-descent (first): Next → Confusion Matrix, **no Previous**
  - embeddings (middle): Previous → Tokenization, Next → Attention
  - funnel-analysis (last): Previous → Window Functions, **no Next**
- Browser: nav renders with the correct names and aesthetic; clicking navigates; no console errors.

## Tests
- New **`e2e/nav.spec.ts`**: a middle topic shows both prev and next with correct neighbor names and Next navigates; the first topic has no Previous; the last has no Next.
- Full e2e suite: **25 passed** (incl. the 3 new nav tests). The `e2e.yml` workflow is untouched, so the required check stays **`e2e / test`**.
- `npm run build` clean; `npm run lint` clean.

- `tsc` ต่อ ArticleForm สะอาด (full check ให้ CI ยืนยัน) · แก้ไฟล์เดียว ไม่มี migration

author: janwienand
body:
## Was

Reine Performance-Optimierung der Erkennungspipeline — keine Funktionalitätsänderung, identische Erkennungsergebnisse (byte-genau verglichen).

| Textlänge | Vorher | Nachher |
|---|---|---|
| 3,8k Zeichen | 0,54 s | **0,16 s** |
| 19k Zeichen (RFP-Größe) | ~3,9 s | **0,83 s** |

## Wie

- **GLiNER-Batch-Inferenz**: alle Chunks als ein Batch über `model.inference(...)` statt `predict_entities` pro Chunk (die `batch_predict_entities`-API ist deprecated und langsamer)
- **Apple-GPU (MPS)**: GLiNER läuft auf der GPU, wenn verfügbar. Erkenntnis: MPS lohnt nur mit Batching, Einzelchunks sind dort langsamer als CPU. Escape-Hatch: `ANONYMO_DEVICE=cpu`
- **Parallele Pässe**: Presidio und GLiNER laufen gleichzeitig (2-Worker-Executor)
- **Echtes Warm-up**: mehrchunkige Dummy-Inferenz beim Start — der erste Request zahlt nicht mehr ~1 s Lazy-Init von torch/MPS/spaCy
- **Wordlist-Cache**: `wordlists.json` wird nur bei geändertem mtime neu geparst

## Verifiziert

- 33/33 pytest grün, `tsc -b` grün
- Live-Smoke-Test: Server-Start mit Warm-up, `/anonymize` liefert in 0,45 s korrekte Maskierung (Person/Projekt/Firma/E-Mail/Telefon)
- Identische Entitätenzahl vor/nach jeder Optimierung (96 bzw. 480 im Benchmark)

> - `pnpm spell-check` → ✅ no issues on the changed files
> - `pnpm --filter @deepnote/cli test` → ✅ 25/25 on the touched suites (`constants`, `collect-integrations`, `analysis`), incl. the regression test for CodeRabbit's catch
> - `tsc --noEmit` (cli) → ✅ clean
>
> (The unrelated pre-existing `diff.test.ts` cwd/fixture failure is untouched by this PR.)

---

Closes #325

## The constraint

The CLI decides whether a SQL block's `sql_integration_id` refers to a **built-in** engine (no external credentials, never linted as "missing") or an **external** integration (collected as required, checked by `lint`). That decision is a case-sensitive set membership test. `BUILTIN_INTEGRATIONS` holds canonical lowercase IDs (`deepnote-dataframe-sql`, `pandas-dataframe`), and two call sites query it with raw `Set.has(integrationId)`:

- `packages/cli/src/integrations/collect-integrations.ts:17`
- `packages/cli/src/utils/analysis.ts:522`

A notebook is just data, and `sql_integration_id` is whatever the author typed. A built-in referenced as `Pandas-DataFrame` or `Deepnote-DataFrame-SQL` does not match the lowercase set, so it silently falls through the built-in filter and is treated as external. There's no crash — the block is added to the required-integration set (triggering credential fetches it doesn't need), and `deepnote lint` reports a bogus missing-integration error:

```
lint: SQL block references integration "Pandas-DataFrame" but no matching env var is configured
```

The inconsistency is local to this filter: the codebase already normalizes integration IDs to lowercase when matching elsewhere (`integrations/fetch-and-merge-integrations.ts`). The built-in check predates that convention and was never reconciled with it.

## What's now possible

A built-in integration is recognized as built-in regardless of how it was capitalized. `isBuiltinIntegration('Pandas-DataFrame')`, `'PANDAS-DATAFRAME'`, and `'pandas-dataframe'` all return `true`; a genuine external ID returns `false`. A built-in referenced in non-canonical casing is never collected as a required external integration and never flagged as missing by `lint`. Authors stop having to remember the exact canonical casing to avoid a false lint failure.

## Why this design

The minimal patch would be to drop `.toLowerCase()` at each `has()` call site. We rejected that because it duplicates the normalization rule across two files, and a third future call site would silently reintroduce the bug — the same drift that caused this issue in the first place. Instead the casing rule lives in one exported predicate, `isBuiltinIntegration()`, and both call sites route through it, so the built-in check has a single source of truth that call sites cannot diverge from. This mirrors the lowercase-normalization convention already used in `fetch-and-merge-integrations.ts`, keeping the package internally consistent. The price: one extra function-call indirection over a bare `Set.has`, and one more symbol exported from `constants.ts` — cheap relative to a correctness check that two (and growing) call sites depend on.

## What it looks like

```typescript
// packages/cli/src/constants.ts
/** Built-in integrations that don't require external configuration. Canonical IDs are lowercase. */
export const BUILTIN_INTEGRATIONS = new Set(['deepnote-dataframe-sql', 'pandas-dataframe'])

/**
 * Determine whether an integration ID refers to a built-in integration.
 * The comparison is case-insensitive ... single source of truth for the
 * built-in check so call sites cannot drift.
 */
export function isBuiltinIntegration(integrationId: string): boolean {
  return BUILTIN_INTEGRATIONS.has(integrationId.toLowerCase())
}
```

Both call sites now read through the predicate instead of touching the set directly:

```diff
-        if (integrationId && !BUILTIN_INTEGRATIONS.has(integrationId)) {
+        if (integrationId && !isBuiltinIntegration(integrationId)) {
           ids.add(integrationId)
         }
```

```diff
-    if (!integrationId || BUILTIN_INTEGRATIONS.has(integrationId)) {
+    if (!integrationId || isBuiltinIntegration(integrationId)) {
       continue
     }
```

Note the collection path still adds `integrationId` (the original string) to the set — only the membership *test* is normalized, so genuine external IDs keep their original casing in the result.

## How we know it works

Developed test-first: the failing test was written and confirmed red before the predicate existed, then went green with the fix. Coverage lands at all three layers:

| Test file | What it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `constants.test.ts` (new) | `isBuiltinIntegration` returns `true` for canonical, all-upper, and mixed casing of both built-ins; `false` for a genuine external ID and for an ID that differs from a built-in only by suffix |
| `collect-integrations.test.ts` (new) | a mixed-case built-in is not collected; a genuine external ID is collected with its original casing preserved |
| `analysis.test.ts` (additions) | the missing-integration check does not flag a mixed-case built-in |

The capstone case is exercised in `collect-integrations.test.ts` — a file with one mixed-case built-in block (`Deepnote-DataFrame-SQL`) and one external block (`my-warehouse`):

```typescript
it('capstone: returns exactly the external ID when a mixed-case built-in and an external block coexist', () => {
  const file = makeFileWithSqlBlocks(['Deepnote-DataFrame-SQL', 'my-warehouse'])
  expect(collectRequiredIntegrationIds(file)).toEqual(['my-warehouse'])
})
```

The built-in is filtered out and exactly `my-warehouse` is collected / flagged.

## Validation

`pnpm --filter @deepnote/cli test run` — the integration-ID files all pass: `constants.test.ts` (4), `collect-integrations.test.ts` (3), `analysis.test.ts` (17). The wider cli suite has one **pre-existing, unrelated** failure in `src/commands/diff.test.ts` (a working-directory / fixture-path issue that calls `process.exit(2)` independent of this change) — it fails identically on the unmodified base and is not touched by this PR.

## Risks and limitations

Behavior-preserving for canonical-cased IDs: any ID already matching the lowercase set continues to match. The change only *widens* what counts as built-in (to other casings of the same IDs), so the only directional shift is that a block which previously linted as a missing external integration purely because of casing now correctly does not — the intended fix.

## Rollback

Pure, side-effect-free predicate change, no migration and no runtime state. Revert the commit to restore prior behavior.

## Scope

No `.gitban/` or `.claude/` files are included — this branch is the six-file code change under `packages/cli/` only.

## Fix PR

> **Using the wrong template?**
> — Enhancement: use enhancement template
> — Feature: use feature template

## Linked Issue

Fixes #851

> The linked issue has the `confirmed-bug` label.

## What was broken

The Codex skill adapter header (generated by `getCodexSkillAdapterHeader()` in `bin/install.js`) documented `Task(subagent_type="X", prompt="Y") → spawn_agent(agent_type="X", message="Y")` as an unconditional direct mapping for all Codex sessions. In sessions where Codex exposes only the generic `multi_agent_v1` schema — which accepts only `message`, `items`, and `fork_context` with **no `agent_type` field** — this mapping is silently invalid. The orchestrator cannot natively dispatch typed `gsd-planner`/`gsd-executor` agents and may fall back to inline execution or produce schema errors, with no guidance to the model on what to do instead.

## What this fix does

Section C of the Codex adapter now requires schema detection before spawning, clearly distinguishes between the agent_type-capable schema (typed mapping available) and the generic `multi_agent_v1` schema (no `agent_type` field), and documents an explicitly-labeled generic-agent workaround for `multi_agent_v1` sessions — marked as NOT equivalent to typed gsd-planner/gsd-executor execution.

## Root cause

The adapter was written before the `multi_agent_v1` / `multi_agent_v2` schema distinction surfaced in real Codex sessions. `spawn_agent` exists in both schemas, but only the typed schema exposes `agent_type`. The code had zero references to schema versions, so the model was given instructions that silently failed in generic-schema sessions. No runtime introspection of the tool schema from static skill text is possible, so the correct fix is adapter prose that instructs the model to detect the schema and take the appropriate path.

author: c0ze
body:
Ports the last of #23's deferred content: the two gambling Mysterious Wanderers (`events/room.js`) and the `Events.saveDelay` machinery they need. With this, **#23 is fully done** — the Room pool (10 events), all 6 Outside disasters, and the Thief/Wanderers are all in.

## The saveDelay subsystem

The JS persists a delayed action's remaining seconds in the save (`game.saveDelay.*`, ticked down every half second; `loadDelays` re-arms it on load), so a pending wanderer return survives a reload. The port keeps the same property with less machinery: each pending action's remaining seconds live in the game state under `delay.<key>` (saved like everything else), and `events.tick_delays` advances every pending countdown by one second on the model's existing 1s `CoolCheck` heartbeat — no timers to re-arm, reload just works. At zero the keyed action fires (announcing in the room) and the countdown clears. Re-gambling while a return is pending resets the countdown rather than stacking, matching the JS `$SM.set`.

A registry (`delayed_actions`) maps the four possible keys to their outcomes — only the Wanderers ever use `saveDelay` in the original, so it's exactly the four cart returns.

## The events

Both wanderer variants (wood and fur) join the Room pool between the Shady Builder and the Scout, matching the JS order. Each: available while you hold any of the store at all (`$SM.get('stores.wood')` truthiness → `> 0`); give 100 (cost 100, even odds) or 500 (longer odds, 0.3), the cart leaves; a winning roll on scene entry (the existing `on_load_rng` hook — the JS `onLoad` calling `this.action(60)`) silently starts the 60-second countdown to a 3× return ("the mysterious wanderer returns, cart piled high with wood." / "…furs."). A losing roll starts nothing, and you'll never know whether builder was right.

The two variants share one builder, differing only in pronouns (he/she), cargo wording, and store.

## Tests

423 passing (+9): availability gates per store, winning/losing rolls at the exact thresholds (0.5 / 0.3), countdown decrement, firing at zero (single-shot, right store, right message, both payout sizes), the idle no-op, and a model-level test that a due return lands on the CoolCheck heartbeat with its room notification.

Refs: `events/room.js:322-481` (both wanderers), `events.js:1468-1486` (saveDelay), `events.js loadDelays` (the reload path).

author: deblasis
body:
## Summary
The MSL backend mapped GLSL.std.450 `PackHalf2x16`(58)→`pack_float_to_half2x16` and `UnpackHalf2x16`(62)→`unpack_half2x16_to_float` — but **those MSL functions do not exist**. Metal's `pack_float_to_*`/`unpack_*_to_float` cover only unorm/snorm; half conversion goes through `half` + `as_type`. So `packHalf2x16`/`unpackHalf2x16` produced **non-compiling MSL** (silent-wrong: glslpp exits 0). Found by diffing glslpp's MSL against the `spirv-cross --msl` oracle. The unorm/snorm pack/unpack variants use real builtins and were already correct.

## Fix (`src/spirv_to_msl.zig`, `.ExtInst` arm)
Emit the spirv-cross idiom:
- `packHalf2x16(vec2)` → `as_type<uint>(half2(x))`
- `unpackHalf2x16(uint)` → `float2(as_type<half2>(x))`

GLSL fixes these types (no overloads), so the result/operand types are hardcoded. `half2(vec2)` does the f32→f16 narrowing, `as_type` the bit-reinterpret — matching GLSL semantics (NaN/inf preserved). The dead `std450ToMsl` 58/62 mappings were removed so a future bypass honest-errors rather than emitting the phantom builtin.

`tests/msl_tests.zig` T-pack.1 (asserts the half idiom + `assertNotContains` the invented names) and T-pack.2 (regression guard: the real unorm/snorm builtins stay).

**APPROVE** — confirmed the `as_type` reinterpret + `half2` narrowing semantics vs the oracle and the safe dead-mapping removal. Hardened per the review by hardcoding the declared LHS types (`uint`/`float2`) and tightening the assertions.

author: frapercan
body:
## A1: SELECT-grid 220->227 KNN scoring chain

Adds `scripts/farm-exp-A1-select-220-227.sh`, the unattended 24-cell (8 PLM x K{3,5,10}) KNN scoring chain over the A0-validated SELECT window (goa:220 -> goa:227).

### What it does
- For each of the 24 canonical (PLM x K) cells: reuse-or-dispatch a prediction_set on the SELECT query_set (132fdab7, 26111 targets) against the t0 reference pool (goa@220, 1559d9f7), `search_backend=numpy`.
- Score each prediction_set under the 7 canonical scoring_configs against eval_set 817c6b9f (NK=2409 / LK=2563 / PK=22308), passing the 220-corpus IA table so `f_micro_w` is SELECT-window-comparable.
- Resume-aware: skips cells whose baseline (`reranker_model_id IS NULL`) evaluation_result already exists.

### Safety
- Every job dispatch is wrapped in `dispatch_with_lock` (shared owner=export stack lock); on contention (exit 2) it waits 60s and retries instead of dispatching unguarded.
- Dispatch is API-only (POST /v1/embeddings/predict, POST /v1/annotations/evaluation-sets/{id}/run); psql is used only for status polling and resolution.
- Keeps `wait_for_predict_with_recovery` (queue-zombie guard) and the numpy backend (torch OOMs on the large KNN corpus).
- One knn-batch consumer, cells run serially (one at a time, waiting for SUCCEEDED).

### Run
```
nohup bash scripts/farm-exp-A1-select-220-227.sh > ~/Thesis2/farm-exp-A1-select.log 2>&1 &
```
The grid log lives outside the repo and stays untracked.

Second driver wiring PR. Routes the two boundaries declared last PR through their ports, so every serial/OSC edge is a contracted source/sink pair:

- **CommandSink** — the `sinew_send_*` host→dongle writers emit their 36-byte frames through `g_cmd_sink` (a faithful wrap of `serial_write_n` on the active handle) rather than calling it directly. Same `WLOCK` scope, same bytes — pure indirection. The write twin of the serial `FrameSource`.
- **TrackerSource** — `OscReceiver::run()` pulls raw `/sinew` packets from the inbound :39540 socket through a `TrackerSource` and decodes them, instead of inline `recv()`. The read twin of `TrackerSink`; socket lifetime stays with `OscReceiver`.

Verified locally: both files compile clean with `-Wall -Wextra` (the serial host's Windows path + all of `osc_receiver.cpp`); CI covers the macOS path. Completes the driver cluster's port symmetry — every boundary (serial in/out, OSC in/out) is now load-bearing.

author: fuziontech
body:
## Motivation

A customer's sqlmesh hourly jobs stalled 30+ minutes on MTCP worker bootstrap. Two structural defects in the cold-acquire path:

1. **Doomed-spawn thrash** — `spawnReservedWorker` → `spawnWorker` waited for pod-ready on the **requester's ctx** (the client's workerQueueTimeout, 5m in prod). When the wait died, the in-flight pod was **deleted**. If node provisioning reliably exceeds the client budget, every retry spawns a new pod, waits, deletes it — the org never converges on a ready worker and burns node churn.

2. **Serialized cold burst** — `OrgReservedPool.AcquireWorker`'s slow path held the per-org FIFO `orgAcquireGate` across the **entire** spawn+activate (minutes). N concurrent cold connections for one org ramped sequentially: waiter k waited behind k−1 full spawns and timed out. (The code comment at the gate documented this as a known perf follow-up.)

## Design

**Detached spawn lifetime.** The spawn (pod create → pod-ready → reserve) and tenant activation now run under `context.WithoutCancel(requestCtx)` (keeps trace/log values) with their own deadline, the new `workerSpawnActivateTimeout = workerPodReadyTimeout + 3m` (pod-ready incl. Karpenter node provision + 90s gRPC connect + activation). The requester waits for the spawn/activate result **or** its own ctx, whichever first:

- Requester abandons + spawn/activate eventually **succeeds** → the worker is parked for the org via `ReleaseWorker` → `TransitionToHotIdleIfNoSessions` (hot_idle record persisted), so the org's next connection reclaims it through the existing hot-idle claim path instead of respawning.
- Requester abandons + it eventually **fails** → retired exactly as the synchronous failure path (`retireWorkerWithReason` with the activation-failure/spawn-failure reasons, `observeActivationFailure` where applicable). No worker can leak in Reserved/Activating.

**Gate held only for the decision section.** `ReserveSharedWorker` is split into `reserveSharedWorkerDecision` (DB-only: hot-idle claim attempt → `CreateSpawningWorkerSlot`) and `completeSharedWorkerReservation` (pod I/O); `spawnReservedWorker` becomes `spawnReservedWorkerForSlot`. `OrgReservedPool.acquireDecision` holds the gate across exactly: idle-reuse re-check → `ClaimHotIdleWorker` → `CreateSpawningWorkerSlot`. Once a waiter owns a slot/claim, the gate is released and the multi-minute spawn+activate runs outside it — so a cold burst of N waiters ramps N spawns in parallel.

**Why anti-snatch still holds.** Each slow-path waiter leaves the gate 1:1 bound to the specific worker it claimed/spawned (the durable claim/slot row is already assigned to it), and the new worker's session is **pre-claimed while still Reserved** — before it ever becomes visible as Hot — so a concurrently-arriving connection's idle-reuse fast path can never grab the worker out from under the waiter that spawned it (this also closes a pre-existing tiny window between activation and session claim). Freed/parked workers re-enter circulation only via the idle-reuse re-check and hot-idle claim **inside** the gated decision section, granted in FIFO arrival order — the earliest waiter still gets the next available worker. The gate itself (`org_acquire_gate.go`) is unchanged, including cancel-safety.

**Unchanged invariants (CLAUDE.md contract):** one session per worker (no least-loaded sharing path added), destroy-before-reuse ordering in `session_mgr.go`, cap-drift recovery in `CreateSessionWithProtocol`, hot-idle claim attempted before spawning, at-cap fail-fast with `WorkerClaimMissReasonOrgCap` (in-memory `atOrgWorkerCap` pre-check kept as fast-fail; `CreateSpawningWorkerSlot` remains the authoritative cross-CP cap check), spawn-failure metrics and persisted lifecycle records on every path (a parked worker persists its `WorkerStateHotIdle` record via `TransitionToHotIdleIfNoSessions`).

## Tests

`controlplane/org_reserved_pool_test.go` (all verified to FAIL against the old implementation where applicable):

- `TestOrgReservedPoolAbandonedSpawnParksHotIdleAndIsReclaimed` — requester cancels mid-spawn → spawn completes detached → worker ends HotIdle/0-sessions with a persisted hot_idle record → next `AcquireWorker` reclaims it via hot-idle claim with **no second pod spawn**. (Fails on main: the old code cancels the spawn and the worker never exists.)
- `TestOrgReservedPoolColdBurstSpawnsInParallel` — 3 waiters, spawn seam blocks on a barrier requiring 3 **concurrent** spawns; all succeed on distinct workers. (Fails on main: serialized ramp deadlocks the barrier.)
- `TestOrgReservedPoolAbandonedSpawnActivationFailureRetiresWorker` — abandoned requester + detached activation failure → worker retired, nothing leaks in Reserved/Activating.
- `TestOrgReservedPoolAcquireFailsClearlyAtOrgCap` — pre-existing at-cap fail-fast, unchanged and still green.

`org_acquire_gate_test.go` untouched and green (gate semantics unchanged). Full `go test -tags kubernetes ./controlplane/... -race`, `go vet -tags kubernetes ./controlplane/...`, gofmt clean on touched files. Also fixed two **pre-existing** `-race` flakes in `k8s_pool_test.go` (`TestK8sPoolRetireWorkerUsesTrackedPodName`, `TestK8sPoolHealthCheckLoopCompletesSameLeaseAlreadyLost`) that asserted async pod deletes without synchronization — both reproduce on origin/main and blocked the required race run.

## Harness (tests/e2e-mw-dev)

- Confirmed `one_session_per_worker` still exercises the changed path (2 concurrent queries → 2 distinct pods through the new decision/complete acquire flow); assertion unchanged.
- New `cold_burst_parallel_spawns` (cnpg, after the sized-worker reuse asserts since it drains the org's workers first): deletes all of the org's worker pods, opens 3 concurrent connections running multi-second queries, and asserts (a) all 3 succeed with correct results, (b) the org peaks at ≥3 simultaneous worker pods (distinct workers), and (c) the burst's first 3 pods' creationTimestamps cluster within 30s — a serialized ramp separates each create by a full spawn+activate, so the spread is the parallel-vs-sequential discriminator.

CLAUDE.md's worker-session-model contract bullets updated to describe the gate-over-decision-only + detached-spawn behavior.

author: ericandrechek
body:
## Problem

Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`) and Claude Mythos 5 (`claude-mythos-5`) launched 2026-06-09 with no LiteLLM pricing entry, so Pacer priced all of their usage at **$0.00** — today's cost, projections, per-model breakdowns, and advisor hints all undercounted. The only mythos key LiteLLM carries (`anthropic.claude-mythos-preview`) is a zero-priced placeholder, which would have shadowed any fix via the substring fallback.

## Fix

- **`AnthropicFallbackPricing`** — built-in rates for `claude-fable-5` and `claude-mythos-5` ($10 in / $50 out / $12.50 5m-cache-write / $20 1h-cache-write / $1 cache-read per MTok, from [Anthropic's pricing page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing); both include 1M context at standard pricing, so no above-200k tier). Consulted **only after every LiteLLM lookup path misses**, so LiteLLM stays authoritative the moment it ships a real entry. Handles the `[1m]` suffix and provider-prefixed variants. `claude-mythos-preview` is deliberately absent: Anthropic publishes no pricing for the invite-only preview, and inventing a number would be worse than $0.
- **Zero-priced placeholders dropped at decode** — a $0 row costs the same as a missing row, but kept it would shadow the fallback and silently re-introduce this bug (e.g. if LiteLLM ships a $0 fable stub).
- **Embedded snapshot refreshed** — the shipped LiteLLM snapshot predated even `claude-opus-4-8`; fresh offline installs now price current models.
- **`costRecomputeVersion` → 3** — existing installs rebuild all aggregates on next launch so historical Fable usage picks up real pricing.
- **Advisor hint generalized** — "Heavy Opus day" is now "Heavy premium-model day" covering Opus/Fable/Mythos (Fable is 2× Opus per token, so a pure-Fable day deserves the Sonnet nudge even more). Screenshots regenerated for the new copy.
- **MARKETING_VERSION → 0.2.0** for the release that follows this merge.

## Verification

- `swift test`: **299/299 pass** (6 new tests: fallback resolution + variants, snapshot mirror, placeholder-drop, LiteLLM-wins-over-fallback precedence, premium-hint for Fable/Mythos).
- Real-data check on a live install: a Fable 5 day that showed **$0.00** prices at **$159.12** after the automatic rebuild.

body:
# Summary

Two features that build on each other:

## 1. Level creation + standalone web page export (all six games)

Every game can now create a custom level and export it as a **single self-contained HTML file** (game + CSS + JS + level baked in) that can be hosted anywhere as its own page.

- **`shared/standalone.js`** — exporter used by every editor: fetches `game.html`, inlines stylesheets, bundles classic and ES-module scripts, injects the level as `window.STANDALONE_LEVEL`, and adds an in-memory storage fallback for sandboxed hosts.
- **New editors** for the games that had none:
  - **Truck Jam** — visual yard editor with solver-backed validation and automatic par.
  - **Block Stacker** — challenge creator (goal height, speeds, perfect tolerance, skin, win message) + a new win condition in the game.
  - **Reaction Slots** — round designer (custom symbols, goal symbol, 1–6 reels, speeds, win message).
- **Wire Puzzle / Mastermind / Paper Puzzle** — existing creators gained the standalone export; all play pages boot straight into baked-in levels.

## 2. Minigame trails (stqry integration)

String games together into a **trail**: open a link → land in a specific minigame → finishing saves the score → one final overview page. Built on the STQRY storage bridge vendored from [maxdammers/cookietest](https://github.com/maxdammers/cookietest) (postMessage inside the stqry app WebView, localStorage fallback in a browser).

- **`trail/builder.html`** — pick games (built-in levels, presets, or pasted editor share-links), choose **any order** or **set order**, generate one link per game + an overview link.
- **`shared/chain.js`** — trail runtime in every game: boots the right level, shows a progress bar, saves a normalised 0–100 score + 1–3 stars on the win screen (best attempt kept), enforces locks in ordered mode, and offers Next/Overview navigation.
- **`trail/results.html`** — live overview: per-game points/stars/native stats, totals, and a final-score celebration (with `stqry.user` greeting) once everything is done, plus a trail reset.
- All six games report their result at their win point (moves vs par, guesses used, reel accuracy, blocks stacked, completion).

# Verification

- A Node harness replays the standalone exporter's exact bundling transform against all six game pages and syntax-checks the output — all pass (plus all editors/trail pages).
- Functional Node tests: truck-jam editor→game encode/solve round trip; chain.js trail decode (incl. emoji/accents), best-score retention, and graceful deactivation on malformed links.
- No browser available in this environment — worth one manual pass once Pages deploys: export a standalone page from an editor and run a 2-game trail end to end.

| [ghcr.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly) | minor | `v1.38.1` → `v1.39.0` |

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>dragonflydb/dragonfly (ghcr.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly)</summary>

### [`v1.39.0`](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/releases/tag/v1.39.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.38.1...v1.39.0)

##### Dragonfly v1.39.0

This release delivers a significant leap in full-text search capability — `FT.HYBRID` fuses vector similarity with text queries, exact phrase matching with slop arrives, Porter stemming is on by default for TEXT fields, and BM25STD/TFIDF scoring with `WITHSCORES` support rounds out a deeply improved search engine. Performance improves across the board: PubSub reply batching cuts syscalls by 24–70% and raises throughput up to +12% RPS, INFO REPLICATION becomes fully lock-free, and a new ShardedHashMap replaces the global RCU ChannelStore for pub/sub. Security is tightened with multiple Lua sandbox hardening patches, RESP injection prevention, and PII-safe error logging. Tiered hashes are now mutable. A significant sweep of zombie-key cleanup fixes closes a class of bugs where lazy field expiry across SORT, ZUNIONSTORE, ZINTERSTORE, SHRINK, and hash TTL commands left empty containers in the keyspace.

##### Highlights

- Added `FT.HYBRID` combining full-text and vector similarity search with LINEAR and RRF score fusion strategies, capping a major release cycle of search improvements ([#​7420](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7420))
- PubSub, Monitor, and Invalidation replies are now batched per wakeup, delivering up to +12% RPS and 24–70% fewer syscalls at pipeline depths 1–500 ([#​7479](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7479))
- Tagged chunk serialization splits large objects across snapshot and replication boundaries so they can be reassembled correctly even with interleaved journal entries ([#​7416](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7416), [#​7070](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7070))

##### Search

- Adds `FT.HYBRID` combining full-text and VSIM search via LINEAR (ALPHA/BETA weighted sum of normalized scores) and RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) strategies, with HNSW KNN and range-based vector queries, `YIELD_SCORE_AS` aliasing, LOAD projection, and `FT.PROFILE` support ([#​7420](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7420))
- Adds exact phrase queries (`"hello world"`) and approximate phrase matching with slop (`"..."~N`), backed by per-document token positions stored in compressed posting lists; BM25 scoring updated for phrase semantics ([#​7319](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7319))
- TEXT fields now apply Porter stemming by default via the vendored Snowball/libstemmer library; per-field `NOSTEM`, index-level `LANGUAGE` (default `english`), and per-document `LANGUAGE_FIELD` are all supported; `FT.INFO` surfaces the new flags ([#​7295](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7295))
- Adds BM25STD (Okapi BM25) relevance scoring engine with per-field TF and document-length tracking for accurate normalization; results can be ranked when a scorer is activated ([#​7101](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7101))
- Adds `TFIDF` (TF × ln(N/n)) and `TFIDF.DOCNORM` (additionally normalized by field length) as new scorer options for `FT.SEARCH`, `FT.PROFILE`, and `FT.AGGREGATE`; scorer dispatch refactored to a function-pointer table ([#​7200](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7200))
- `FT.SEARCH` now supports `WITHSCORES` and `SCORER` parameters; `FT.AGGREGATE` gains `ADDSCORES` to inject a `__score` field enabling downstream GROUPBY/SORTBY/REDUCE on relevance ([#​7181](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7181))
- HNSW vector index memory is now tracked in the `search_used` memory class and reported in `dragonfly_memory_used_bytes` via an atomic capacity-based footprint counter ([#​7205](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7205))

##### Performance

- PubSub, Monitor, and Invalidation control-path replies are now accumulated in the send buffer and flushed together per wakeup rather than one `sendmsg` per message; single-message wakeups still flush immediately \[+3% RPS at pipeline=1, +12% at pipeline=10, −24% to −70% syscalls at pipeline=1–500] ([#​7479](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7479))
- INFO REPLICATION and replica memory stats are now served lock-free via per-proactor thread-local snapshots updated on every mutation, eliminating global mutex and per-replica shared-lock fan-out ([#​7348](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7348))
- Replaced the global RCU-based ChannelStore with a `ShardedHashMap` (16 independent shard locks), removing the pool-wide broadcast on every subscribe/unsubscribe ([#​7174](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7174))
- `NotifyWatchQueue` exits in O(1) when a watched key is absent (previously O(N) over all waiters), directly benefiting BLPOP, BZPOPMIN, and XREAD workloads ([#​7225](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7225))
- Long-running container iteration commands (LRANGE, SMEMBERS, ZRANGE, HGETALL, etc.) now yield the shard fiber periodically; configurable via `--container_iteration_yield_interval_usec` (default 500 µs, 0 to disable) ([#​7391](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7391))
- Integrates OAHSet as an alternative in-memory set backend selectable via `--use_oah_set`; threaded through RDB save/load, async deletion, defragmentation, and SHRINK ([#​7246](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7246))
- Adds foundational zero-copy GET infrastructure to CompactObj and LargeString: `TryBorrow()` returns an encoded view with Copy-on-Write semantics; a thread-local pin registry defers buffer deallocation until all readers finish ([#​7412](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7412))
- Connections that occasionally receive large commands now trim parse buffers exceeding 256 KiB at more than 2× actual utilization, preventing permanent oversized memory holds ([#​7378](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7378))

##### Replication

- Adds `serialization_tagged_chunks` flag enabling the RDB serializer to split large entries into tagged chunks with envelope IDs; compression is applied per-blob; a related list-decoding crash during chunked load is also fixed ([#​7416](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7416))
- Implements tagged chunk loading in the RDB loader with per-stream continuation state, supporting interleaved chunks from different objects and cross-database-boundary reassembly ([#​7070](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7070))
- Four new Prometheus metrics are now emitted on replica instances at `/metrics`: `dragonfly_master_link_status`, `dragonfly_master_last_io_seconds_ago`, `dragonfly_sync_in_progress`, and `dragonfly_slave_repl_offset` ([#​7069](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7069))

##### Cluster

- Adds `--cluster_coordinator_connect_timeout_ms` and `--cluster_coordinator_response_timeout_ms` flags to control coordinator-to-shard timeouts (previously hard-coded at 3000 ms) ([#​7221](https://redirect.github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/issues/7221))
- Cluster config validation now rejects invalid migr

author: nathanialhenniges
body:
Adds an opt-in **Nightly** update channel so testers can ride builds straight off `main`, while Stable stays the default for everyone else. Targeted to ship with **2.0.0**.

## How it works
Sparkle **dual-feed** (not channels): `feedURLString(for:)` swaps to a separate nightly appcast when opted in, else falls back to `SUFeedURL`. Keeps the stable release pipeline untouched and fits the existing static GitHub-release hosting (avoids the `latest`-excludes-prereleases trap).

- **Stable feed:** unchanged (`releases/latest/download/appcast.xml`).
- **Nightly feed:** a single rolling `nightly` GitHub prerelease, asset re-uploaded with `--clobber` so the URL stays stable: `releases/download/nightly/appcast-nightly.xml`. Same EdDSA + Developer ID signing, so the installed app verifies it.

## Changes
- **Core:** `UpdateChannel` enum (`nonisolated`), `updateChannel` UserDefaults key (exportable), `Update.nightlyFeedURL`.
- **Service:** persisted `channel`, pure `resolveFeedURLString(channel:isDebug:…)`, rewritten `feedURLString`, `recheckAfterChannelChange()`.
- **UI:** Software Update pane gets a Stable/Nightly picker, a destructive warn-alert before switching to Nightly (Cancel auto-reverts), a persistent nightly banner. Hidden for Homebrew, disabled in DEBUG.
- **Tests:** `UpdateChannelTests` + resolver/persistence cases. Build + tests pass locally (`BUILD SUCCEEDED` / `TEST SUCCEEDED`).
- **CI:** `nightly.yml` — daily cron + manual, skip-if-no-new-commits guard, mirrors release sign/notarize, date-stamp build number (always > stable), `generate_appcast -o appcast-nightly.xml`, rolling prerelease. Reads existing repo-level secrets; no GitHub environment.
- **Docs:** new `nightly.mdx` guide, sidebar + installation cross-links, changelog entries (CHANGELOG.md + changelog.mdx) under 2.0.0, design/plan doc.

## Caveat (surfaced in UI + docs)
Sparkle never offers a *lower* version, so switching Nightly → Stable needs a one-time manual stable-DMG reinstall. Stated in the alert, the banner, and the docs page.

## One-time step before the first nightly runs
Just **Run workflow** on `nightly.yml` once (Actions → Nightly → Run workflow / `workflow_dispatch`) to seed the rolling `nightly` release so the feed URL resolves. No secrets to add (they're repo-level) and no environment to create. Until then the feature sits dormant: the channel persists, the nightly feed 404s, Sparkle simply reports no update.

## Decisions made (flag if you disagree)
- `updateChannel` classified **exportable** (real user pref, next to `updateCheckEnabled`).
- Channel switch **not** surfaced in onboarding — advanced users find it in Settings.
- Nightly job uses **no GitHub environment** (secrets are repo-level; an env would only add an approval gate that would block the unattended cron).

author: jmtrades
body:
## What

Reps could **book / confirm / remind / cancel** meetings but had no in-app place to *see and manage* them, and no way to record an **outcome** — so the analytics couldn't show a no-show rate. This adds a **Meetings** page and outcome tracking, closing the loop opened by the booking + analytics work.

## Pieces

- **Migration `0050`** — widen `bookings.status` to `confirmed | cancelled | completed | no_show`.
- **Types / store** — `BookingStatus` union; `setBookingStatus(id, status)`; `listBookingsForManagement()` (last 45 days onward, soonest first); the status read maps all four values.
- **`/meetings` page** (nav → Work group) — **Upcoming** vs **Past**, where a rep marks a past-but-confirmed meeting **Completed** or **No-show**, **cancels** an upcoming one (which frees the slot), or **Undo**es an outcome. Optimistic with refresh, deep-links to the deal.
- **`/api/meetings/status`** — **auth-gated** (lives under `/api/meetings`, *not* the public `/api/bookings` prefix), and logs a timeline note so the outcome shows on the deal.
- **Stats** — `noShow30d` + `noShowRate` (measured over recently-*occurred* meetings); the Reports "Meetings booked" card now shows **Cancel rate** + **No-show rate** with warn tones.

## Security note

The outcome mutation deliberately sits under the gated `/api/meetings/*` prefix — putting it under `/api/bookings/*` would have made it public (that prefix is allow-listed for the prospect-facing booking endpoints). A test pins this.

## Tests (+5)

- No-show rate aggregation (only recently-occurred meetings count; old ones excluded).
- Route gating: the status endpoint stays authenticated, `/meetings` is gated, and the public booking endpoints stay public.
- Status route: 400 invalid / 404 missing / 200 sets status + logs a note.

## Gate

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `next lint` — clean
- `vitest` — 1188 passed / 20 skipped (215 files)
- `next build` — `/meetings` + `/api/meetings/status` compile

## Summary
The content half of the turn-energy arc (plan 16b, on top of #54). Both potions are in 0.40's `item_table_potion` spawn table (`treasure.c` cases 4–5):

- **Potion of slowing** (`treasure_p_slowing`): cancels an active haste, **slow for 20 turns** (C `SLOW_LENGTH`) — monsters act twice between your steps. "You feel very sluggish."

- Data-only beyond that: two TOML potions (no `nospawn`), so they join floor loot and the random-appearance shuffle like every 0.40 potion; quaffing identifies the type.

- `RemoveEffect` drops only the named effect; absent kind is a no-op.
- `haste` behavior applies haste and cancels slow; `slowness` applies slow and cancels haste; both return the C messages.

author: yawamomensah
body:
Extends the Chapter 10 recursive descent front-end with a full code generation pass, transforming Jack source into stack-based VM code. The parser now drives two output streams simultaneously: XML parse tree output (retained from Chapter 10) and VM code emission.

Symbol table architecture
-------------------------
Two-scope flat array model: ClassTable (field/static) and SubTable (argument/local), each a fixed array of SymbolTableEntry structs with slice-based name and type fields (pointer + length into the source buffer — no allocation, no copy, consistent with the tokenizer's representation throughout). Separate per-kind counters assign VM segment indices at insertion time. Linear search over the flat array is justified by Jack's scope sizes — a subroutine symbol table large enough to require hashing would indicate a poorly structured subroutine.

Lookup is subroutine-scope-first, falling through to class scope on a miss. Both lookup functions iterate from the most recently inserted entry backwards — variables declared closest to the point of use are found first on average, reducing the number of comparisons in the common case. NULL return indicates an undeclared identifier; at that point in a subroutine call context, the identifier is treated as a class name by the VM calling convention rather than a variable reference.

Subroutine kind handling
------------------------
compileSubroutineDec captures the subroutine kind (constructor/method/ function) into ParserState before consuming the keyword. The subroutine table is reset at each subroutine boundary.

compileSubroutineBody defers the `function ClassName.name nLocals` emission until all varDec parsing is complete so that local_count is final. The preamble then diverges by kind:

  constructor: push field_count, call Memory.alloc 1, pop pointer 0
  method:      push argument 0, pop pointer 0
  function:    no preamble

For methods, a hidden `this` entry (type = classname, kind = T_ARG, index = 0) is inserted into the subroutine table before parameter parsing so that explicit parameters receive correct indices from 1.

Expression and statement code generation
-----------------------------------------
compileExpression holds the binary operator in a temporary after consuming it, compiles the right-hand term via compileTerm, then emits the operator — postfix ordering falls out of the recursive call structure without any explicit reordering.

compileTerm handles all term forms:
  - Integer constants:   push constant n
  - String constants:    String.new + String.appendChar loop per character
  - Keyword constants:   null/false → push constant 0
                         true → push constant 0 / not  (produces -1)
                         this → push pointer 0
  - Plain variables:     symbol table lookup → emit_push(kind, index)
  - Array access:        compile index expression, push base address, add,
                         pop pointer 1, push that 0
  - Subroutine calls:    bare name → implicit this (push pointer 0, +1 arg)
                         varName.sub → object call (push object, +1 arg)
                         ClassName.sub → plain function call
  - Unary operators:     - → neg, ~ → not (emitted after recursive compileTerm)
  - Parenthesised:       compile inner expression, no additional emission

Array assignment in compileLet uses a temp register to preserve the RHS value across the pointer 1 assignment:
  push base, compile index, add → target address on stack
  compile RHS expression
  pop temp 0, pop pointer 1, push temp 0, pop that 0

Label generation
----------------
compileIf and compileWhile each reserve two indices from a persistent label_count in ParserState at function entry — before any recursive compileStatements call. Both labels are allocated upfront so nested constructs consume indices beyond them, eliminating collisions under arbitrary nesting depth. Labels follow the pattern ClassName_N.

Void return: compileReturn pushes constant 0 before emitting return when the next token is ';'. compileDo pops the discarded return value into temp 0 after every subroutine call to keep the stack balanced.

emit_push / emit_pop centralise the T_KIND → VM segment mapping:
  T_STATIC → static, T_FIELD → this, T_ARG → argument, T_VAR → local

Driver changes
--------------
main.c opens two output file handles per source file — .xml and .vm — and assigns both to ParserState. All ParserState fields are explicitly initialised before each parse to prevent garbage values from stack-allocated structs. Class table is reset at the top of compileClass to support multi-file compilation. The output extension for VM code is .vm; XML output is retained for verification.

Tests passing: Average, Seven, ConvertToBin, ComplexArrays (single-file); Pong, Square (multi-file, verified in the VM emulator with directory load).

body:
💡 **What:** Added an `isatty(STDOUT_FILENO)` check around the screen-clearing ANSI sequence (`\x1b[2J\x1b[H`) in the `top` applet. If the output is redirected and not a TTY, it falls back to printing a simple newline (`\n`).

🎯 **Why:** When users redirect the output of a continuous applet like `top` to a log file, the raw ANSI escape sequences severely pollute the log. By replacing them with a newline, the output becomes a cleanly separated log of each iteration.

📸 **Before/After:**
*Before:* `top > log.txt` resulted in a file full of `^[[2J^[[H` escape codes interspersed with the process listing.
*After:* `top > log.txt` results in clean text output separated by blank lines.

♿ **Accessibility:** N/A (CLI logging improvement)

author: aizu-m
body:
Auditing ppdc's PPD importer. import_ppd parses every *Font attribute with an unbounded sscanf:

    sscanf(attr->value, "%s%*[^\"]\"%[^\"]\"%s%s", encoding, version, charset, status)

encoding, version, charset and status are each char[256], and none of the four conversions is width-limited.

Assumed ppd_read's 256-byte line cap bounded attr->value, but it caps each physical line only. Inside a quoted value the reader keeps appending across newlines, so a multi-line version field grows past 256 bytes. ppdOpenFile on a PPD whose Font version field spans a few lines hands back a 427-byte value with a 404-byte version token, and the %[^"] conversion then writes 404+1 bytes into version[256].

Canary placed straight after version[256], 400-byte version field:

    bare    %[^"]   : bytes written past end = 145
    capped  %255[^"]: bytes written past end = 0

Width-limiting the four fields keeps the writes inside the buffers, matching the %255s / %255[^"] forms already used in ppd.c and cups-driverd.cxx.

author: hirekarl
body:
## Context

Full CI suite runs on every PR regardless of what changed, making docs and single-layer PRs unnecessarily slow.

## Impact

Adds a `changes` job (`dorny/paths-filter`) that detects whether backend or frontend files changed:

- `docs/`-only PRs skip all validation jobs and complete in seconds
- Backend-only PRs skip the Playwright/Lighthouse jobs (~5–8 min saved)
- Frontend-only PRs skip pytest/mypy

Adds a `ci-gate` aggregator job (`if: always()`) as the single stable required status check — passes when triggered jobs pass or are skipped, fails on any failure or cancellation. `notify-slack` and `automated-release` now depend on `ci-gate` rather than individual jobs.

**Branch protection update required after merge:** swap the three individual check names for `CI — all checks passed` in the `main` branch protection settings.

## Verification

Existing CI suite passes unchanged. Path filtering only affects which jobs are triggered, not what they test.

author: kefahi
body:
## Summary

Python dmart is EOL — the C# implementation is the only one going forward. That retires the "Python parity" rationale behind two long-standing compromises, both addressed here.

### Opt-in strict token_use enforcement (security)

- New `JWT_REQUIRE_TOKEN_USE` setting (default **false**). When enabled, a JWT lacking the `token_use` claim is rejected at bearer auth, WebSocket auth, and the OAuth refresh grant — which then requires exactly `"refresh"` instead of merely "not access". This closes the remaining deliberate gap in access/refresh token separation from #98.
- New `LegacyTokenMonitor` counts every tolerated claimless token and warn-logs it, rate-limited to one line per subject per hour. Rollout is observability-driven: once a deployment logs zero legacy-token warnings for a full `JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRES` window, the flag can be flipped safely.
- `TokenUse.Read` consolidates the duplicated claim decoders in `JwtBearerSetup` and `OAuthEndpoints`.

### Batched COPY as the default import path (perf)

- The default (non `--fast`) import previously wrote one row per connection (~216 rows/sec measured on a real 133k-row import). It now uses the same binary COPY + temp-table merge batching as `--fast`, on a session that keeps FK constraints and triggers enforced: **~7,200 rows/sec** wall on a 20k-entry fixture (see `bench/REPORT-import-default-batching.md`). `--fast` now means only what is genuinely unsafe about it: replica-role FK/trigger bypass plus per-space parallelism.
- A batch that trips an integrity error (unknown owner → FK violation at the DEFERRED commit; duplicate uuid → PK violation at the merge) is replayed row-by-row so the offenders fail alone into the failure sidecar — the per-row semantics the default path always had. The fallback is deliberately not engaged under `--fast`, where a per-row replay would enforce FKs that flag promises to bypass.
- History lines now run inside per-line savepoints, fixing a pre-existing fast-path hazard where one bad history line poisoned the shard's trailing transaction and silently rolled back the whole history slice.

## Verification

- 1393/1393 tests green (13 new: strict/tolerant token_use unit + integration pairs, `TokenUse.Read`, `LegacyTokenMonitor`, and `ImportBadRowIsolationTests` — the latter written and verified against the pre-change importer first, then kept green under the batched path, proving the fallback works).
- 97/97 `curl.sh` smoke green against a live server.
- Import benchmarked default vs `--fast` on identical fixtures; results in `bench/REPORT-import-default-batching.md`.

body:
# Assessment Bug Report — Overview

Full-stack code review of the Fabbi Todo App. This document is the canonical
overview: it lists every issue identified across the backend, frontend,
database, caching, and infrastructure layers; ranks them by severity; and
points to the individual PR description for each fix that was actually
implemented.

The codebase was audited end-to-end. Out of **43 identified issues**,
**7 fixes were implemented** on dedicated branches per the assessment
requirement of "≥ 5 meaningful issues, ≥ 2 backend, ≥ 1 frontend." The
selection prioritises **correctness, security, and data isolation** over
cosmetic cleanup, as the assessment brief instructs.

> AI assistance disclosure: Claude Code (Opus 4.7) was used for codebase
> exploration, bug triage, and draft generation of fixes, tests, and PR
> descriptions. All findings and the final implementation choices were
> reviewed before commit. Full disclosure of what was used and how lives
> in [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) at the repo root.

---

## Severity scale

| Marker         | Meaning                                                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 🔴 **Critical** | Breaks security or data isolation; leaks or corrupts data across users        |
| 🟠 **High**     | Logic bug that produces wrong data, regression risk, or production-scale perf |
| 🟡 **Medium**   | Quality, UX, performance, or robustness issue                                 |
| 🟢 **Low**      | Convention or cosmetic                                                        |

---

## Bug catalogue

### 🔐 Security / Authentication (backend)

| ID  | Severity    | Issue                                                            | Location                                                                |
| --- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| S1  | 🔴 Critical | `verify_token` disables `verify_exp`; all JWTs effectively infinite | `app/core/security.py:56`                                              |
| S2  | 🔴 Critical | `get_current_user` does not check token `type` — refresh tokens accepted as access tokens | `app/api/deps.py:21-34`                                |
| S3  | 🔴 Critical | `/auth/logout` is a no-op — tokens remain valid until expiry, no JTI blocklist | `app/api/v1/auth.py:102-107`                                    |
| S4  | 🟠 High     | Email enumeration on `/login`: 404 vs 401 leaks whether the email exists | `app/api/v1/auth.py:54-66`                                          |
| S5  | 🟠 High     | Default `JWT_SECRET` hardcoded in source and `.env` committed to repo | `app/core/config.py:15`, `.env`, `.gitignore:9`                     |
| S6  | 🟠 High     | `CORS allow_origins=["*"]` combined with `allow_credentials=True` — invalid per spec, opens cross-origin attacks | `app/main.py:31`                  |
| S7  | 🟡 Medium   | No rate limit on `/login` or `/register` — brute force / abuse vector | `app/api/v1/auth.py`                                                |
| S8  | 🟡 Medium   | Refresh tokens are not rotated and have no blocklist — replayable | `app/api/v1/auth.py:77-99`                                            |
| S9  | 🟡 Medium   | `UserCreate` schema has no password complexity rules; FE enforces min 6 but BE accepts anything | `app/schemas/user.py:7-9`                          |
| S10 | 🟢 Low      | `authenticate_user` defined but unused; `/login` reimplements the same logic | `app/services/auth_service.py:33`, `app/api/v1/auth.py:60`     |

### 🔓 Authorization / Data isolation (backend)

| ID | Severity    | Issue                                                                      | Location                            |
| -- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| A1 | 🔴 Critical | `GET /todos/{id}` does not verify `todo.user_id == current_user.id` — IDOR | `app/api/v1/todos.py:88-102`        |
| A2 | 🔴 Critical | `PUT /todos/{id}` — same IDOR pattern, attacker can rewrite any todo       | `app/api/v1/todos.py:105-134`       |
| A3 | 🔴 Critical | `DELETE /todos/{id}` — same IDOR pattern, attacker can delete any todo     | `app/api/v1/todos.py:137-154`       |

### 🗄️ Database (schema / migrations / queries)

| ID | Severity    | Issue                                                                          | Location                                                                                       |
| -- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D1 | 🔴 Critical | `users.email` lacks UNIQUE constraint and index — duplicate accounts possible  | `app/models/user.py:21-24`, `alembic/versions/001_initial.py:26`                               |
| D2 | 🟠 High     | `todos.user_id` has no index — every list query full-scans                     | `app/models/todo.py:35-38`                                                                     |
| D3 | 🟠 High     | FK `todos.user_id` lacks `ON DELETE CASCADE` — orphans or delete failures      | `app/models/todo.py:36`                                                                        |
| D4 | 🟠 High     | `get_todos` has no `ORDER BY` — OFFSET/LIMIT produces non-deterministic pages  | `app/services/todo_service.py:31`                                                              |
| D5 | 🟠 High     | N+1 query in `list_todos` — per-todo `SELECT users` lookup                     | `app/api/v1/todos.py:48-50`                                                                    |
| D6 | 🟡 Medium   | Email stored case-sensitively; `DEMO@test.com` ≠ `demo@test.com`               | `app/services/auth_service.py:11-12,21-30`                                                     |
| D7 | 🟡 Medium   | `DB_ECHO=True` is the default; production logs flooded with SQL                | `app/core/config.py:9`                                                                         |
| D8 | 🟡 Medium   | No upper bound on `?size=` — `?size=10000000` is accepted, DoS surface         | `app/api/v1/todos.py:29`                                                                       |

### ⚡ Caching (Redis)

| ID | Severity    | Issue                                                                                          | Location                              |
| -- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| C1 | 🔴 Critical | Cache key `"todos:list"` is global — one user's response is served to every other user         | `app/api/v1/todos.py:37`              |
| C2 | 🔴 Critical | Cache key ignores `page`/`size` — `?page=2` returns page 1                                     | `app/api/v1/todos.py:37`              |
| C3 | 🟠 High     | Cache never invalidated on create/update/delete — stale data for up to 5 minutes               | `app/api/v1/todos.py` (mutation paths) |

### 🧩 Backend API correctness

| ID | Severity   | Issue                                                                                                      | Location                              |
| -- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| B1 | 🟠 High    | `PUT /todos/{id}` uses `if todo_data.completed:` — only truthy values are applied, so `completed=False` is silently ignored | `app/api/v1/todos.py:123-124` |
| B2 | 🟠 High    | `TodoUpdate` apply logic is inconsistent (`is not None` vs `in update_data`) and calls `update_todo(db, todo, {})` with an empty dict | `app/api/v1/todos.py:121-132`

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
EP-0003 slice 3 — the resource-owned frame work-ledger substrate (rf2-afpdkn).

## What

Adds the work ledger that records the in-flight read work the resource runtime manages.

- New `re-frame.resources.work-ledger` ns: serializable `[:rf.runtime/work-ledger]` records keyed by work-id (plain EDN, host-handle-free); the entry points at its current attempt via `:current-work`.
- Host abort handles live in a host-side side table keyed by `[frame-id work-id]` (`work-ledger/handle-table`), NOT serialized — mirrors the generation allocator + routing nav-counters/scroll caches.
- Owner release updates ledger rows; abort is OPPORTUNISTIC (best-effort `:rf.http/managed-abort` by request-id = work-id); stale suppression by work-id + generation is the MANDATORY correctness boundary.
- Refetch supersedes + best-effort aborts the prior attempt; release-owner aborts ONLY orphaned (no-owner) in-flight work; clear-scope / remove cancel + abort in-scope work.
- Terminal rows pruned on the linked entry's next successful transition (bounded per-key tail for Xray); one identity per record (work-id embeds the generation; no `:stale-key` synonym).
- Frame destroy clears the side tables via a new `:resources/on-frame-destroyed!` late-bind hook (composes work-ledger + generation host caches), wired into core `frame/destroy-frame!` + the late-bind directory.
- Two host-side side-table write fx (`:rf.resource/record-work-handle` / `:rf.resource/clear-work-handle`), mirroring `:rf.resource/commit-generation`.

## Spec

author: copilot
body:
The `build` job was failing because `joshcai/leetcode-sync@v1.7` crashed when LeetCode returned a non-iterable `submissionList.submissions` payload. This PR prevents hard failure by validating the response shape before invoking the sync action.

- **Root-cause containment**
  - Added a preflight `Validate LeetCode session` step that performs a lightweight GraphQL request and checks that `data.submissionList.submissions` is an array.
  - Exposes a step output (`valid=true|false`) for downstream gating.

- **Conditional sync execution**
  - Updated the `Sync` step to run only when preflight validation succeeds.
  - Added a fallback step that emits a warning and skips sync when auth/session payloads are invalid instead of failing the workflow.

- **Workflow impact**
  - Preserves normal sync behavior for valid sessions.
  - Converts recurring auth-shape failures from hard job failures into explicit operator-visible warnings.

```yaml
- name: Sync
  if: steps.leetcode-auth.outputs.valid == 'true'
  uses: joshcai/leetcode-sync@v1.7
  with:
    github-token: ${{ github.token }}
    leetcode-csrf-token: ${{ secrets.LEETCODE_CSRF_TOKEN }}
    leetcode-session: ${{ secrets.LEETCODE_SESSION }}
```

author: aterrylu
body:
## Problem The heavy artifact gates — universal2 DMG build + smoke + `validate-dmg` (first-run flow + the Phase-6 idle-CPU peg-detector) — ran **only on release** (`v*` tag / dispatch). So cross-arch lipo, native-module, bundling, and first-run regressions (the **#178-class bugs** — the ones that keep breaking the desktop app) surfaced only when cutting a release, not at PR time. ## Solution Run the **full universal2 DMG build + validation on every artifact-touching PR**, path-filtered. To avoid duplicating the historically-fragile build YAML, extract it into a reusable `workflow_call` workflow that both callers share: ```mermaid flowchart LR R["release.yml
(v* tag / dispatch)"] -->|"sign: true
validate_intel: true
+ secrets"| RW P["pr-artifact.yml
(PR, path-filtered)"] -->|"sign: false
validate_intel: false
no secrets"| RW RW["reusable-dmg-build.yml
build-server ×4 → build-dmg → validate-intel"] RW --> Pub["release.yml: publish
(SLSA + GH release)"] ``` | | release.yml | pr-artifact.yml | |---|---|---| | DMG | universal2, **signed + notarized** | universal2, **unsigned** | | Build (arm64+x64 lipo) | ✅ | ✅ (same — lipo path exercised) | | smoke + validate-dmg (first-run + idle-CPU) | ✅ | ✅ | | validate-intel (L6b Gatekeeper) | ✅ | ⛔ skipped | | Publish | ✅ | ⛔ | | Secrets received | yes | **none** | **Why full universal2 (not arm64-only) on PR:** the whole point of the universal build is the cross-arch lipo (`stage-universal-server.sh` + `bundle-node.sh`) — exactly where the nastiest bugs live. An arm64-only PR DMG would never exercise it. Full universal2 catches those at PR time. ## Signing safety - Driven by the `sign` input via `SECRET_`-prefixed pass-through, promoted to `CSC_LINK`/`APPLE_API_KEY` only when `sign=true` → an unsigned build **never sets an empty `CSC_LINK`** (electron-builder mis-reads `""` as a cert path — the #196 bug). - The 5 signing secrets are declared `required: false`; `pr-artifact.yml` passes **none**, so a PR build never receives the signing material (defense beyond `sign=false`; fork PRs get nothing regardless). ## Hardening (from adversarial review) - **`validate-intel` runs on `validate_intel || sign`** — a *signed* build can **never** skip the Gatekeeper/notarization gate. (A skipped job counts as success to `needs:`, so the unsafe `false` default could otherwise publish an unverified DMG, green. This `|| sign` forecloses it.) - **The spctl Gatekeeper gate now asserts the exit code** (`set -o pipefail`) instead of substring-matching `"accepted"` through a `tee` that discarded it — robust to Apple wording drift on the single most load-bearing release gate. - Signing env resolved **before** `bun run build`, restoring the original step-level `env:` timing exactly (behavior-preserving extraction). ## Testing - ✅ actionlint: **no `workflow_call` wiring errors** (only pre-existing info-level shellcheck carried verbatim from `release.yml`). - ✅ code-reviewer: extraction verified **byte-faithful** vs `main:release.yml`, no gate dropped. - ✅ **This PR self-tests `pr-artifact.yml`** — the path filter includes the workflow files it adds, so the PR's own CI builds the full unsigned universal2 DMG and runs validate-dmg end-to-end. - ⏳ I'll also fire a `workflow_dispatch` dry-run to prove the **release path** still works post-refactor (the #196/#199 pattern), before merge. ## Risk Moderate (refactors the working release pipeline) — mitigated by: faithful-extraction review, actionlint, the PR self-test of the PR path, and a dispatch dry-run of the release path before merge. Net: extraction + 3 hardening fixes; no logic dropped. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
