author: kyem
body:
## Summary

Redesigns the verbose 10-section scrolling settings modal into a **compact, theme-aware, sidebar-categorised** modal, implemented from a Claude Design handoff bundle. Full parity with the existing **25 settings fields** (plus the custom 10s–1h quote interval).

Six categories: **Timer · Sound & music · Focus mode · Home screen · Goals & alerts · Advanced**.

### What changed
- **Instant-save** — no Save/Cancel bar; every change persists immediately with a quiet "Changes save automatically" footer pulse. Sync toggle still reloads (now only when the migration actually persists), and timer changes still refresh a running Pomodoro session.
- **Denser controls** — session-recipe preset cards (Classic 25/5/15, Deep work 50/10/25, Quick sprint 15/3/12 → flips to "Custom" when fine-tuned), `−/+` steppers, segmented controls, chips, and a background **thumbnail picker**. Helper text moved inline.
- **Cross-section search** filters settings across all categories.
- **Curated** — Debug (log level) and Chrome sync demoted under Advanced; reset is a two-tap inline confirm.
- **Theme-aware** — built with the app's semantic tokens (`bg-surface`, `text-primary`, `border-border`, `bg-primary-600`…), so it adapts across all 4 themes × light/dark. The signature glass look appears automatically under the glass theme.

### Architecture
- New: `SettingsModal` shell + primitives (`SettingControls`), section registry (`SettingsSections`), `PresetGrid`, `ThumbPicker`, and three pure helpers — `settingsMatch`, `quoteIntervalToSeconds`, `planSettingsSideEffects`.
- Removed: the 11 old per-section components, the `SettingsToggle/Select/Slider/Section` primitives, and the `useSettingsForm` hook (no longer needed under instant-save). No external importers.

### Out of scope (managed elsewhere, as before)
Color theme + layout density (theme switcher); ambient sounds / music volume / playlists (sounds panel); goal view mode.

## Test plan
- `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · Biome ✅ · production build ✅
- **Vitest 352/352** (26 new unit tests for the search matcher, the interval clamp/unit/empty-guard, and every `apply` side-effect branch)
- Manually verified in-browser: all 6 sections + cross-section search render correctly in the **glass** theme, and the modal adapts cleanly to **purple light** (theme-awareness confirmed).

## Notes
Includes fixes from a multi-agent PR review: the sync-reload no longer wipes its own migration-failure toast; an empty custom-interval entry no longer silently snaps to 10s; `SelectControl` is generic (drops unsafe casts); `SectionId` is a derived union (stale ids are compile errors); preset rhythm strings are derived rather than hand-maintained.

author: thebiglabasky
body:
## What changed

- Removed the `Skip SSL Check` fixture API check, which depended on `https://self-signed.badssl.com/`.
- Added a parse/synthesize-only ApiCheck fixture and unit test that assert `skipSSL: true` is synthesized correctly, without performing a network request.
- Narrowed the GitHub reporter E2E to `secret.check.ts` so reporter assertions are not coupled to unrelated fixture checks.

## Why

The E2E suite depended on `https://self-signed.badssl.com/`, which resets connections from Checkly cloud runners. That made the broad CLI smoke test and the GitHub reporter test fail for reasons unrelated to the behavior they are intended to cover. `skipSSL` synthesis is now covered locally by a fixture that never reaches the network.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest --run ./src/constructs/__tests__/api-check.spec.ts`
- `pnpm exec eslint e2e/__tests__/test.spec.ts src/constructs/__tests__/api-check.spec.ts`
- Commit hook ran `pnpm run lint` on staged files

I did not run the remote E2E suite locally because this shell does not have `CHECKLY_API_KEY` / `CHECKLY_ACCOUNT_ID` configured.

body:
Fixes several VRC700-specific endpoint mismatches found by comparing the library against real myVaillant Android app traffic (mitmproxy capture):

1. **Zone operating mode** (`set_zone_operating_mode`): VRC700 now uses
   `PATCH system-control/v1/systems/{system_id}/zones/{index}/{operating_type}-operation-mode`
   instead of the old `vrc700/v1/.../zone/{index}/{operating_type}/operation-mode`, and uses the
   `ZoneOperatingModeVRC700` enum (DAY, AUTO, SET_BACK, OFF).

2. **Heating curve** (`set_circuit_heating_curve`): VRC700 sends `{"setPoint": ...}` instead of
   `{"heatingCurve": ...}` (URL unchanged). Determined via `get_control_identifier`.

3. **Heat demand limited by outside temperature** (`set_circuit_heat_demand_limited_by_outside_temperature`):
   VRC700 now uses `POST system-control/v1/systems/{system_id}/circuits/{index}/heat-demand-limited-by-outside-temperature`
   (plural `circuits`) with `{"setpoint": ...}`, instead of the old singular `circuit` path and
   `{"heatDemandLimitedByOutsideTemperature": ...}` body.

4. **Manual/DAY mode setpoint** (`set_manual_mode_setpoint`): VRC700 heating now uses
   `PATCH .../zone/{index}/heating/comfort-room-temperature` with `{"comfortRoomTemperature": ...}`
   instead of `manual-mode-setpoint`, which returns 404 for VRC700 (confirmed against the live API).
   VRC700 cooling now delegates to `set_cooling_setpoint`.

This branch is built on top of #155 and includes a cherry-pick of
#154 since `set_manual_mode_setpoint` reuses `set_cooling_setpoint`. Once those
two PRs are merged, this diff will shrink to just the changes described above.

All tests pass (371 passed, 17 skipped) and mypy is clean. New tests added in
`tests/test_vrc700_temperature.py` and `tests/test_api.py`.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact - A real `OPENAI_API_KEY` configured through xcconfig was merged into the app Info.plist, exposing a long-lived provider key in the shipped client bundle. - If the Realtime WebSocket receive loop failed after audio started, the UI marked the session disconnected but skipped audio teardown, leaving the microphone/input tap and audio session active until the user manually ended practice. ## Root cause - The OpenAI key flowed through `Base.xcconfig` into `RuntimeSecretsInfo.plist` and `VoiceSessionManager` read it with `Bundle.main`. - The receive-loop catch path only cleared connection/speaking flags instead of running the teardown path that stops audio and invalidates the socket/session. ## Fix - Removed the OpenAI key from build settings and the runtime Info.plist, and restricted local debugging to an `OPENAI_API_KEY` launch environment value. - Routed receive failures through teardown while suppressing a server notification on the already-failed socket. - Updated the local agent guidance so future changes do not reintroduce bundled provider secrets. ## Validation - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` - Python static validation parsed `RuntimeSecretsInfo.plist` and asserted the key is absent from plist/xcconfig, the `Bundle.main` key lookup is gone, the environment lookup remains, and receive errors call teardown. - `rg` confirmed remaining `OPENAI_API_KEY` references are only the launch-environment path and documentation warning. Note: Full `xcodebuild` validation could not run in this Linux runner because `xcodebuild` is not installed.

body:
## DEN-2316 — Worker State Timeline (Gantt Chart)

Linear: https://linear.app/bluebearsecurity/issue/DEN-2316

Implements a Gantt-style worker utilization timeline.

### Database
- New table `worker_status_transitions(id, worker_id, status, changed_at)` + drizzle migration `0001_worker_status_transitions.sql`.
- `upsertWorker` appends a transition row whenever the worker's status changes (and on first insert), using the payload's `updatedAt` as `changedAt`. No-op when status is unchanged.

### Backend
- `getWorkersTimeline(db, { now, windowMs })` in `repository.ts` reconstructs continuous per-worker segments for the window. The first segment is seeded from the most recent transition before `windowStart` (clipped to the window start) so workers with no recent changes still render a bar. Open-ended segments are clipped to `now`.
- New REST endpoint:
  - `GET /api/workers/timeline?hours=<n>` — default 24h, max 72h, rejects invalid/out-of-range values with 400.
  - Response shape: `{ hours, windowStart, windowEnd, workers: [{ workerId, workerName, segments: [{ status, startMs, endMs }] }] }`.

### UI
- `WorkerTimelineGantt` component (`src/ui/src/components/WorkerTimelineGantt.tsx`) renders a horizontal bar per worker with colored segments (busy/idle/stopped/dead), legend, and hour tick labels along the time axis.
- `WorkersPage` gained a 24h / 48h / 72h range toggle that re-queries the timeline. The existing workers table is unchanged.
- New `useWorkersTimeline` query hook + `fetchWorkersTimeline` client.

### Mock data
- `seedMockData` now seeds a handful of transitions across `wk_1..wk_3` so the chart is visible immediately after `npm run seed:mock`.

### Tests
- New `writer.test.ts` cases: first-sighting transition recorded; only status changes append a row.
- New `repository.test.ts` cases for `getWorkersTimeline`: segment reconstruction, seeded first segment from a transition before the window, empty-worker omission.
- New `routes/api.test.ts` cases for `GET /api/workers/timeline` covering defaults, custom hours, and 400s on invalid input.
- Updated `schema.test.ts` table-list assertion to include `workerStatusTransitions`.

All backend tests pass (`npx vitest run src/backend` → 45/45). Backend + UI `typecheck` both clean.

UI rendering tests (`WorkersPage.test.tsx` and friends) fail with `React.act is not a function` both before and after this PR — pre-existing testing-library/React 19 env issue, untouched here.

author: ritwiksrivastava
body: ## Problem External DM delivery URLs (delivery-p*-e*.adobeaemcloud.com) were not converted to responsive elements with srcset. They remained as plain tags , meaning: 1. No responsive image variants — browser always fetches full-size image 2. No width/height attributes — browser cannot reserve layout space → CLS ## Solution ### New pipeline step: processExternalImages Adds `process-external-images.js` which runs after `createPictures` and converts every external (non ./media_*) to a responsive mirroring what createOptimizedPicture does for media bus images: - 4 variants: webp × 2 breakpoints + native format × 2 breakpoints - Breakpoints: (min-width: 600px) → 2000px, default → 750px ### CLS prevention via intrinsic dimensions The pipeline resolves width/height from two sources in order: 1. ?originalImageWidth=N&originalImageHeight=N — no-op params set by the custom asset picker (ignored by DM delivery engine) . https://github.com/OneAdobe/aem-uix-uex-asset-picker/pull/62 2. img.properties.width/height — existing HTML attributes on the node (set by OOTB UE picker via HTL rendering, once that team makes their change)(Future Scope) Dimensions are read before being stripped from the URL so the delivery server never receives them. The resolved values are set as width/height attributes on the fallback inside . The browser uses these to reserve layout space before the image loads, preventing CLS. Please ensure your pull request adheres to the following guidelines: - [ ] make sure to link the related issues in this description - [ ] when merging / squashing, make sure the fixed issue references are visible in the commits, for easy compilation of release notes ## Related Issues Thanks for contributing!

author: dganellari
body:
- **fix(pump): revive the pressure outlet (the REAL through-flow fix). outletU was set unconditionally -> always velocity-Dirichlet outlet -> both-ends-Dirichlet admits a flat-pressure tank-recirculation div=0 solution -> NO flow through the passage (confirmed: 1e-10 pressure solve gave identical flat-p, so it's structural not convergence -- AMG would NOT help). Gate outletU on !outletDoNothing so do-nothing (default) leaves outletU<=0 -> solver masks the WHOLE outlet face p=0 + frees outlet velocity (singlePin=false, solver:4080) -> inlet flux against fixed-p outlet FORCES the outlet->suction gradient -> through-flow. The dead --outlet flag now actually works**
- **fix(pump): default outlet back to MASS-CONSERVING (the correct design). Root cause found: the divergence operator only loops interior faces (sum(div)==0 always), so the pressure solve is NEVER told mass enters at the inlet -> a velocity-inlet + free pressure-outlet is UNPROJECTABLE -> no through-flow (flow dies at inlet, pressure parks in body). The code's own comment (solver:2295) flags this. My prior do-nothing default was backwards: the mass-conserving outlet (vel outflow removes Q + single pin) BALANCES the flux so the projection builds the inlet->outlet gradient that drives flow through the passage. The dead-flag gate stays so do-nothing is still selectable (needs a boundary-flux source term to be correct -- separate work)**
- **pump through-flow: (1) default to do-nothing outlet = whole-face p=0 + FREE outlet velocity (the channel-proven pairing that builds the inlet->outlet pressure head; both-ends-velocity-Dirichlet + single pin gave a flat-pressure dead-passage solution). (2) --inlet-flux-source (GUARDED, off): add the prescribed inlet flux as a boundary divergence source -- the exterior opening flux is in no interior SCS so it's never integrated (verified not a double-count); A/B it. (3) [through-flow] Q_in/Q_out/ratio diagnostic each step so we MEASURE through-flow (ratio->1) instead of eyeballing uMax. mass-conserving still selectable. cavity/channel/TGV unaffected**
- **pump: REMOVE the broken --inlet-flux-source (double-counted the inlet flux already registered via interior SCS scatter; full-opening-area x rho/dt -> instant blowup, ratio=garbage) and revert default to MASS-CONSERVING outlet. Verified high-confidence: the inlet flux is already in the divergence for a velocity-Dirichlet inlet, so the only correct inlet boundary source is ZERO. do-nothing (whole-face p=0 + free outlet) does NOT self-drive a small interior outlet -> ratio=0 (no through-flow); the prior do-nothing-default + comments were disproven by the A/B. mass-conserving (U_out=Uin*Ain/Aout + single pin) forces Q_out=Q_in by construction. Kept the [through-flow] Q diagnostic (correct + useful)**
- **pump through-flow REWORK (verified root cause): the reference flows through the pump with ANY scheme (bj/upwind) so the dead passage is OUR bug, not Re/scheme. TWO real defects fixed: FIX1 --opening-flux-source (GUARDED off): inlet/outlet OPENING faces are exterior, in no interior SCS, so the prescribed opening flux never reaches the pressure RHS -> pressure flat -> no through-flow. Add it as a COMPATIBLE surface integral (u.n)*A_share, SAME scale as interior scatter, NOT x rho/dt (RHS does it), net~0 -- verified NOT a double-count (telescoping interior pairs never touch the opening face). FIX2 --dirichlet-lift (default ON): velocity-diffusion col-zero had no Dirichlet lift -> inlet momentum never diffused inward -> jet died at inlet. Add b-=K[row,bdry]*uTarget. FIX3: replace TAUTOLOGICAL Q_out (relocked to prescribed outletU) with an INTERIOR cut-plane flux probe at 25/50/75% -- measures SOLVED through-flow, can't be faked. old line relabeled [bc-sanity]**

author: quant-theodorefelix
body:
Progress on #14. Removes the heap-allocating `Vec<u8>` functions from the `Hash` and `MAC` traits (`hash`, `do_final`, `do_final_partial_bits`, `mac`) in favor of companion traits that return fixed-size stack arrays, following the same const generic pattern as `KEM` / `Signature`:

```rust
pub trait HashFixedOutput<const OUTPUT_LEN: usize>: Hash { .. }   // hash / do_final / do_final_partial_bits -> [u8; OUTPUT_LEN]
pub trait MACFixedOutput<const OUTPUT_LEN: usize>: MAC { .. }     // mac / do_final -> [u8; OUTPUT_LEN]

impl HashFixedOutput<{ SHA256Params::OUTPUT_LEN }> for SHA256 {}
impl<HASH: HashFixedOutput<N> + Default, const N: usize> MACFixedOutput<N> for HMAC<HASH> {}
```

- SHA2, SHA3, HMAC implement the new traits; default method bodies make each impl a one-liner.
- Factory enums keep only the `*_out` functions: their output length is a runtime property.
- XOF `hash_xof` / `squeeze` keep `Vec<u8>`: output length is inherently a runtime argument.
- `*_out` parameters stay `&mut [u8]`: the documented truncation semantics depend on slices (reasoning recorded in the release notes TODO).
- Bonus: 2 internal `vec!` allocations in hmac replaced with zeroized stack buffers (resolves an inline TODO), 4 `do_final().try_into().unwrap()` sites in mldsa / mldsa_lowmemory cleaned up.

Verification: `cargo test --workspace` 326 passed / 0 failed (doctests included), 0 build warnings, CLI output matches system `shasum` and the FIPS 202 vectors, core unwraps 422 -> 415, non-test `-> Vec<u8>` sites 23 -> 9.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact - With `VITE_DATA_BACKEND=supabase`, anonymous or not-yet-resolved auth state could use the shared `default` Supabase workspace. - Existing open RLS policies allowed any anon/authenticated client to read/write `packlog_snapshots`, creating cross-user data exposure and overwrite/data-loss risk. - `PacklogProvider` could also save stale state into a newly selected repository before that repository finished loading. ## Root cause - `createPacklogRepository` created a Supabase repository whenever Supabase env vars existed, even without a `userId`. - Snapshot RLS policies were still open from the early phase schema. - Store hydration used a single boolean and did not bind save eligibility to the currently loaded repository/auth state. ## Fix - Require an authenticated `userId` before using Supabase snapshots, and force workspace to `u:`. - Keep anonymous Supabase-configured sessions on browser localStorage. - Gate `PacklogProvider` loads/saves by auth readiness and the hydrated repo key. - Add migration `005_packlog_snapshots_rls_lockdown.sql` and update schema reference to restrict `packlog_snapshots` to authenticated users' own `u:` workspace. - Add repository isolation tests. ## Validation - `npm test -- src/lib/packlog-repository.test.ts` — 3 passed. - `npx eslint src/lib/packlog-repository.ts src/lib/packlog-store.tsx src/lib/packlog-repository.test.ts --max-warnings 0` — passed. - `npm test` — 9 files / 26 tests passed. - `npm run build` — passed.

### What this PR does / why we need it
This PR resolves an issue with the "Step #7 Server delivery" tutorial where the final code snippet was presented as a single combined block without differentiating between CommonJS and ES Modules. 

Users using CommonJS encountered a `SyntaxError: Unexpected reserved word` due to the top-level `await` because the implicit `async function main()` wrapper wasn't shown in the snippet. Additionally, the `async` keyword was added silently without any highlighting, causing confusion.

### Changes Made:
- Split the final combined code block into `<Tabs>` with `cjs` and `mjs` variants, matching the style established in previous tutorial steps.

Fixes #512

body: ## What Adds a standalone **`README.zh-CN.md`** at the repository root and points the main `README.md` language switcher at it. The new file mirrors the **full** English README structure — badges row, hero copy, all images, every section (它做什么 / 快速开始 / 界面语言 / 应用场景 / 主要功能 / 文档), license, Star History chart. Chinese-locale visitors landing on the repo now get a top-level native-language entry point instead of an embedded, condensed `## 中文` section buried below the English one. ## Why All 12 `docs/*.zh-CN.md` files plus `CONTRIBUTING.zh-CN.md` already follow the per-file zh-CN convention. The root README was the lone exception. That mismatch matters because: - A standalone `README.zh-CN.md` is the standard GitHub i18n pattern (Vue.js, Electron, pandas, pytorch, gin-gonic). Chinese-language search and the language-aware preview pickers expect a separate file. - The embedded `## 中文` section that lived inside `README.md` was a condensed translation — about 60% the depth of the English section. The new standalone file matches the English structure 1:1. - 666ghj — the most active external contributor by a wide margin (219 commits) — and recent Chinese-language coverage (btcbabycow tweet "米罗莎要来了") suggest there's a real Chinese-speaking audience already touching the project; they just didn't have a top-level entry point. - No new translation work was needed — the content is a synthesis of the existing embedded `## 中文` section and the established terminology from the zh-CN docs (CONTRIBUTING, INSTALL, etc.), expanded to match the English README's depth. ## Changes - **`README.zh-CN.md`** *(new file, 154 lines)*: full Chinese README mirroring the English structure. Badges row, hero/demo images, all 6 content sections, complete documentation table linking to every `docs/*.zh-CN.md`, license, Star History chart. Pre-flight checked all image and doc links resolve. - **`README.md`** *(−102 / +3 lines)*: - Language switcher line changed from `中文` (in-page anchor) → `中文` (cross-file link). - Removed the embedded `## 中文` section (now superseded by `README.zh-CN.md`). - Removed the no-longer-needed `` / `## English` H2 wrapper (English is now the default). - License section trimmed to English-only (bilingual line was duplicating with the Chinese file's own license section). ## Design notes - **Convention match**: each `docs/*.zh-CN.md` file opens with `[English](X.md) · 中文` — the new `README.zh-CN.md` uses the page-centered badge row pattern instead because that's the convention `README.md` uses (not `` tags). This keeps the two files visually paired. - **No backend / API changes** — pure docs PR. No new tests required; no openapi changes; no surface added to `surfaces_catalog.py`. Zero dependency additions. - **Pre-existence grep**: confirmed `README.zh-CN.md` does not already exist (only `README.md` and `README_DEPLOYMENT.md` at root). --- *Built autonomously by Aeon*

Per roadmap decision: pipelines are a big separate product surface and leave the cluster control-plane rollout. This PR encodes the descoping in the specs while pinning the **socket** they will plug into — all of which already exists and is enforced in code: 1. **Config field reservation**: `pipelines:` in `cluster.yaml` is rejected with a typed `future_phase_field` diagnostic (enforced + test-covered in `omnigraph-cluster`) — the name can never be silently squatted. 2. **Resource-model reservation**: the `pipeline.` typed address and `Pipeline` resource kind stay reserved; the state model (kind-agnostic entries, extensible sidecar kinds, dependency edges) accepts the new kind without reshaping. 3. **The contract**: axiom 13 — the pipeline *definition* is a reconciled cluster resource; its *execution* is data-plane and never reconciled; fan-out is statusful, never silently atomic. Changes: scope note atop the high-level spec's ETL section (which now stands as the requirements record for the future project), the implementation spec's Phase 7 section reframed as "separate project (socket only)", the blast-radius row annotated, and exit criterion 9 deferred to the pipelines project's own RFC. body:
Part of #226 (interactive TUI). **Task 1 of 7.**

## WHAT
Adds the Charm stack and a new `internal/cli/tui` package — the foundation for the interactive dashboard. Ships **dark**: nothing in the CLI dispatches to it yet, so there is no user-facing behavior change.

## WHY
The dashboard (and later the train-init wizard) need a real interactive terminal UI (#226). This task lands the dependency and the read-only model/view scaffold in isolation so the wiring and interactive pages can build on a reviewed base.

## CHANGES
- `go.mod`/`go.sum`: bubbletea v1.3.10, bubbles v1.0.0, lipgloss v1.1.0 (exact agent-tools versions; all pure Go — keeps gitmoot cgo-free). Charm imports confined to `internal/cli/tui`.
- `data.go`: TUI-facing `Snapshot` mirroring `dashboardSnapshot`; `Deps{Load, Answer, Dismiss, Interval}` (Answer/Dismiss are the stable surface the Attention page wires in task 3); msg types.
- `model.go`: bubbletea `Model` — sidebar pages, viewport, single in-flight refresh suppression (à la agent-tools `queueLoad`), refresh tick.
- `view.go`: sidebar, rune/ANSI-width-safe table renderer (width via `x/ansi.StringWidth`), session grouping via `style.GroupSuffix`, job/lock coloring.
- Read-only pages: **Agents, Sessions (grouped), Jobs (by-state), Locks**.
- `model_test.go`: Update/View tests with `lipgloss` color profile pinned to Ascii — page nav/wrap, refresh suppression, load-error keeps stale data, empty states, resize, tick re-arm.

## RESULTS
- `go test ./internal/cli/tui` green; `go build ./...` green; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- No existing test touched (package is not yet wired into any command).

## RISK
Low. Dependency-only blast radius is confined to the new package; ~25 indirect pure-Go modules added (no cgo, modernc sqlite stays pure-Go). No CLI surface changes yet.

## /code-review
High-effort review (correctness + cleanup finders) ran on the diff. Findings addressed in the second commit: `displayWidth` now uses `x/ansi.StringWidth` (the hand-rolled stripper only reset on `m` and was the wrong altitude); `dash` trims before the empty check (parity with `cli.emptyText`). Accepted-as-is with rationale: cross-package duplication of the ~20-line session-grouping algorithm and the small table renderer (different package/types; `style.Columns` can't pre-color cells), and the forward-declared `Deps.Answer/Dismiss` fields (wired next task, defining them now avoids churning the task-2 adapter).

…resilient start

Request timeouts on a QUIC-alive conn now evict it immediately instead of waiting for the 30s ping sweep. connFor's inbound-wait is capped at half the caller's remaining deadline so 2s discovery probes still get to dial. author: harishwaranvijayakumar
body:
<!-- Please let the below note in for people that find this PR -->
> [!NOTE]
> Are you waiting for the changes in this PR to be merged?
> It would be very helpful if you could [test the resulting artifacts](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/wiki/Testing-PR-Builds) from this PR and let us know in a comment if this change resolves your issue. Thank you!
<!--
!!!!!!! MAIN IS THE ONLY ACTIVE BRANCH. MAKE SURE THIS PR IS TARGETING MAIN. !!!!!!! 
-->



### Issue Details

- `PlatformTicker` on iOS and Windows does not respect the OS animation accessibility settings.
- On iOS, enabling **Reduce Motion** (Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Reduce Motion) has no effect — MAUI animations continue to play normally.
- On Windows, disabling **Animation effects** (Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → Animation effects) has no effect — MAUI animations continue to play normally.
- Android already honors these settings via `ValueAnimator.AreAnimatorsEnabled()` and the energy-saver / duration-scale listeners.

### Root Cause of the issue
**iOS**
- The PlatformTicker.iOS.cs never sets SystemEnabled on the base Ticker class. The SystemEnabled property defaults to true, meaning AnimationManager always allows animations to run.
- AnimationManager.Add() checks Ticker.SystemEnabled — if false, it rejects the animation.
- AnimationManager.OnFire() checks Ticker.SystemEnabled — if false, it force-finishes all running animations.

**Windows**
- PlatformTicker.Windows.cs never checked the system animation accessibility setting. Ticker.SystemEnabled defaults to true, so MAUI animations always played regardless of the "Show animations in Windows" setting (Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → Animation effects).

**Android wires this up correctly:**
- Checks ValueAnimator.AreAnimatorsEnabled() at construction
- Listens for energy-saver and duration-scale changes to update SystemEnabled at runtime
- iOS does none of this — SystemEnabled stays true forever regardless of accessibility settings.


### Description of Change

**Accessibility and Animation Behavior:**

* `PlatformTicker` now observes system accessibility settings—on Windows, it listens to the "Show animations in Windows" setting, and on iOS/MacCatalyst, it respects the "Reduce Motion" setting. The ticker automatically enables or disables animations based on these settings. 

**Resource Management and Disposal:**

* Both platform-specific `PlatformTicker` classes now implement `IDisposable` and provide `Dispose()` and `Dispose(bool disposing)` methods to clean up event handlers and observers, preventing potential memory leaks. 
* The public API surface is updated to include the new `Dispose` methods for `PlatformTicker` on all relevant platforms. 

**Robustness Improvements:**

* Added checks to prevent starting or responding to events if the ticker has already been disposed, enhancing the safety and reliability of the animation system. 

### Issues Fixed

<!-- Please make sure that there is a bug logged for the issue being fixed. The bug should describe the problem and how to reproduce it. -->

Fixes #35845

author: seer-by-sentry[bot]
body:
This PR addresses issue SOLIDINVOICE-8X, where saving an invoice could lead to a `Doctrine\DBAL\Exception\DriverException` with the message "Data too long for column 'invoice_id'".

The root cause was identified as a lack of length validation for the user-supplied `invoiceId` (invoice number) field. This allowed input exceeding the `VARCHAR(255)` limit of the `invoices.invoice_id` database column, leading to data truncation errors during `entityManager->flush()`.

To resolve this, the following changes were made:
- Added `#[Assert\Length(max: 255)]` to the `invoiceId` property in `src/InvoiceBundle/DTO/InvoiceFormDTO.php`. This ensures server-side validation prevents oversized values from reaching the database.
- Added `attr => ['maxlength' => 255]` to the `invoiceId` form field in `src/InvoiceBundle/Form/Type/InvoiceType.php`. This provides client-side feedback and prevents users from entering excessively long invoice numbers in the first place.

These changes prevent database errors, improve the user experience by providing immediate feedback on input length, and mitigate potential abuse vectors where large payloads could be injected into the invoice number field.

Fixes SOLIDINVOICE-8X

author: samm-git
body:
Thank you for your work on MCP. I did a lot of changes, so now it's a bit hard to summarize them. Let me try to do this with AI help (of course!)

# v2: Frontdoor auth, MCP resources, containers/report migration, Docker/CI

## Summary

Major overhaul of the Cloudability MCP server. Key themes: automatic token acquisition via Frontdoor API keys, new read-only MCP reference resources, migration from retired container endpoints to the v2/v3 APIs, per-vendor account tools, and full CI/Docker infrastructure.

---

## Authentication

- **Frontdoor API keys** (`CLOUDABILITY_KEY_ACCESS` / `CLOUDABILITY_KEY_SECRET`): when set in the environment, the server automatically exchanges them for an `apptio-opentoken` via the Frontdoor login endpoint. Tool calls no longer need an explicit `authorization` parameter.
- **Token caching with auto-refresh**: tokens are cached until near expiry (configurable skew). A 401 response triggers a cache invalidation and one automatic retry.
- **`_TruststoreHTTPAdapter`**: all HTTP goes through a shared `requests.Session` backed by the OS certificate store (`truststore`), so corporate CA chains work out of the box.
- **Regional Frontdoor URLs**: US/EU/AU endpoints supported via `CLOUDABILITY_FRONTDOOR_URL`.

---

## MCP Reference Resources (`cloudability_resources.py`)

New read-only resources registered on the MCP server, with short-lived in-memory caching (default 15 min, tunable via `CLOUDABILITY_RESOURCE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`):

| URI | Content |
|-----|---------|
| `cloudability://config` | Non-secret server config (API URL, auth mode, default view ID) |
| `cloudability://measures` | Cost report dimensions & metrics catalog |
| `cloudability://measures/allocated` | Measures for allocation-enabled reports |
| `cloudability://filter-operators` | Filter operator reference |
| `cloudability://saved-reports` | Saved cost report definitions |

---

## Containers API Migration

- **`containers_report`** replaces the retired `/containers/allocations` and `/containers/counts` endpoints, now calling `POST /v3/containers/report`. Parameters updated: `cost_type` values changed (`"adjusted"`, `"total_adjusted_amortized"`), grouping by `workload_name`/`workload_type` instead of `service`/`deployment`, pagination via `paginationToken`.
- **`get_clusters`** now calls `GET /containers/v2/clusters` with `viewId` and `concise` params.
- **`clusterName==` filter guard**: raises a clear `ValueError` directing users to use `cluster==<uuid>` instead.
- **`widget_type=kpi` remapping**: silently remapped to `top` since the API returns HTTP 400 for `kpi`.
- **Removed**: `get_container_allocations`, `get_container_counts`, `count_container_resources`.

---

## Vendor Accounts

`list_billing_accounts` replaced by five per-vendor tools:

| Tool | Endpoint |
|------|----------|
| `list_aws_accounts` | `GET /v3/vendors/AWS/accounts` |
| `list_azure_accounts` | `GET /v3/vendors/azure/accounts` |
| `list_gcp_accounts` | `GET /v3/vendors/gcp/accounts` |
| `list_ibm_accounts` | `GET /v3/vendors/ibm/accounts` |
| `list_oci_accounts` | `GET /v3/vendors/oci/accounts` |

---

## Infrastructure

- **`Dockerfile`**: Alpine image on Python 3.14, non-root user, SSE transport on port 8080.
- **`Makefile`**: targets for `sync`, `test`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `check`, `docker-build` (multi-arch amd64/arm64), `docker-push`, `docker-build-local`.
- **GitHub Actions CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): lint + typecheck + tests on PRs, followed by Docker build + Trivy scan for CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs.

---

## Tests

- **New**: `tests/test_cloudability_resources.py`, `tests/test_mcp_integration.py` (10 core read-only tools + 3 optional + chained `get_budget`), `tests/conftest.py`.
- **Removed**: legacy `tests/test_cloudability.py`.
- Integration tests require `.env` credentials and are skipped by default (`-m integration`).

---

## Other Changes

- Python requirement bumped to **3.14+**.
- `run_server.py` removed; entry point is now `python main.py`.
- `__init__.py` removed from project root.
- `.env` added to `.gitignore`; committed `.coverage` binary removed.
- Error messages now include the API response body on HTTP errors.

body: ## Bug and impact Commit `ba919a3` (#169) replaced the production CORS allowlist with unconditional origin reflection while `credentials: true`. In production, session cookies use `SameSite=None; Secure`, so any malicious website could make credentialed cross-origin requests to the API and **read authenticated responses** (e.g. `/auth/export-data`, task approvals, point adjustments). ## Root cause `createApp()` called `callback(null, true)` for every `Origin` header, ignoring `FRONTEND_ORIGIN`, Vercel wildcard config, and Codespaces helpers. ## Fix - Restore production allowlist behavior (configured origins + `*.vercel.app` wildcard + GitHub Codespaces hosts). - Keep origin reflection for non-production and when `CORS_REFLECT_ORIGIN=true`. - Retain explicit `OPTIONS` preflight handler from #169. - Add `backend/tests/corsPolicy.test.js` to lock in production blocking vs allowed origins. ## Validation - `npm test -- tests/corsPolicy.test.js` — 3/3 passed - Full backend suite — all tests passed

## 💡 Summary 
Fixed broken doctests in `tokmd`'s CLI argument resolution modules (`crates/tokmd/src/config/resolve/export.rs`, `crates/tokmd/src/config/resolve/lang.rs`, and `crates/tokmd/src/config/resolve/module.rs`).

## 🎯 Why 
The `Librarian` persona mandates preferring executable docs and doctests for core APIs so that documentation does not silently drift. The doctests in the argument resolution module imported `Profile` from `tokmd::cli` instead of `tokmd_settings`, which meant they either failed to compile or were silently failing when checked.

## 🔎 Evidence 
- `cargo test --doc -p tokmd` ran the doctests and encountered compilation errors when I modified the files, revealing they were broken before, or masking failures. I fixed them by properly importing `Profile` from `tokmd_settings` and removing it from the `tokmd::cli` import lists.

## 🧭 Options considered 
### Option A (recommended) 
- what it is: Update the doctests in the config resolve modules to ensure they compile and provide valid, executable examples of how configuration resolution works.
- why it fits this repo and shard: It fits the `Librarian` persona by improving factual docs quality and executable examples, reducing uncertainty around API usage. It belongs in the `interfaces` shard.
- trade-offs: Improves documentation structure and testability with negligible cost to velocity or governance.

### Option B 
- what it is: Update the `docs/reference-cli.md` with explicit doctests.
- when to choose it instead: If the priority was testing documentation generation or rendering behavior.
- trade-offs: We can't actually `cargo test --doc` a markdown file easily in the standard cargo pipeline without tools like `rustdoc` set up for standalone markdown files, so it's less guaranteed to be continuously verified.

## ✅ Decision 
Option A. The `Librarian` persona explicitly states: "Prefer doctests and example tests so docs cannot silently drift." and the `docs-executable` gate profile requires doctests to execute or compile. Fixing the failing or silently ignored doctests in the config module is the best alignment with this mandate.

## 🧱 Changes made (SRP) 
- `crates/tokmd/src/config/resolve/export.rs`
- `crates/tokmd/src/config/resolve/lang.rs`
- `crates/tokmd/src/config/resolve/module.rs`

## 🧪 Verification receipts 
```text
cargo test --doc -p tokmd
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
```

## 🧭 Telemetry 
- Change shape: Doc-test fix
- Blast radius: API docs / tests
- Risk class: Low - no logic changed, only documentation examples
- Rollback: Revert the PR
- Gates run: `cargo test --doc -p tokmd`, `cargo run -p xtask -- docs --check`, `cargo build -p tokmd`, `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`

author: nedlane
body:
Split 1/4 of the mixed `fix/organisation-tree-sync` branch (one change per PR).

A real Project.m1prj carries the component hierarchy twice inside each `<ComponentStream>`: the flat `<List>` of real components AND a nested `<Organisation>` view tree. M1 Build binds every object's Properties through `<Organisation>`, so a structural edit that touched only `<List>` left the two out of sync and M1 Build refused to load the project with "Unable to find Properties for object 'Root.X'" (fatal). The view tree had been treated as view-only and ignored.

All structural edits now keep `<Organisation>` consistent:

- `create_channel` / `create_group`: insert a `<Component Name="leaf"/>` view node under the parent's `<Organisation>` node.
- `delete_component`: remove the matching view node (nested subtree included).
- `rename_component`: rename the matching view node's short Name.

All are no-ops on projects with no `<Organisation>`, so existing behaviour on minimal/hand-written files is preserved.

Also:

- `rename_component` now rejects a dotted `--new-name` (was silently accepted and doubled the parent prefix, e.g. `Root.CAN.Root.CAN.Foo`).
- `validate()` gains a `<List>`/`<Organisation>` consistency check: a view node with no matching real component is an error; a real component absent from the view tree is a warning.

New `xml.rs` helpers (`org_locate`, `org_insert_child`, `line_extended_start`) and 8 unit tests cover create/delete/rename sync, dotted-name rejection, no-Organisation no-ops, and dangling-node detection. 77 tests pass; clippy/fmt/docs gates clean.

author: nsollazzo
body:
PR-B3: authentication for the CLI — `positronick login` (device flow), `logout`, `auth status`, and `auth token create`, with a 0600 credential cache and a credential provider wired into every command.

## What's in here

### `internal/auth`
- **`deviceflow.go`** — `Start` / `Poll` against `/api/auth/device/{code,token}` with **JSON bodies** (the verified live contract; the server 415s form encoding, and the mock now enforces that on every test). `authorization_pending` keeps polling; `slow_down` grows the interval **+5s**; `access_denied` → exit 2 ("authorization denied"); `expired_token` → exit 4 with "run positronick login again"; plus a **hard local deadline** at `expires_in`. Polling uses a plain `http.Client` (unauthenticated endpoints; its own loop, not `api.Client` retries). `sleep`/`now` are injected seams — pacing and the deadline are tested without real waiting.
- **`store.go`** — `<config dir>/credentials.json`, written 0600 via temp-file+rename; group/other-readable files are repaired to 0600 with a one-line stderr warning; **keyed to `baseUrl`** — `Load` returns nil for any other host, so a prod token is never sent to localhost. Malformed files fail loudly (fix: `positronick logout`).
- **`provider.go`** — implements `api.CredentialsProvider`: `POSITRONICK_API_KEY` (as `x-api-key`, never persisted) > cached bearer for the resolved base URL > anonymous, all read at call time. Wired into `clientFor`, so **every existing read command now authenticates too** (asserted in `TestReadCommandsUseProvider`).

### Commands
- **`login [--no-browser]`** — prints `First, copy this code: TJSP-LLAV` + `Then visit: <verification_uri>`; auto-opens `verification_uri_complete` only when interactive (TTY, no CI/agent) AND (macOS or `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) AND not `--no-browser`, failures ignored. On success: live `GET /api/me`, persist, `Logged in as <name> (<email>)`. `--json` is a documented **two-line NDJSON stream** (pending immediately, authenticated after approval).
- **`logout`** — deletes the cache; idempotent.
- **`auth status`** — live `/api/me` check; **exit 0 in every resolvable state** (logged out, device session, API key, rejected credentials — the last with a re-login hint). A success refreshes the cached user/isAdmin (the bit a later PR uses for hidden admin commands).
- **`auth token create [--name] [--expires-days]`** — requires a bearer session (env-key-only → exit 4 "log in first"; nothing → exit 4). Client caps `--expires-days` at 365; omitted = server default (90d). Human mode prints the raw key **alone on stdout** (pipe-safe for `$(...)`) with the shown-once warning + `export POSITRONICK_API_KEY=...` hint on stderr.

### Supporting changes
- `internal/api`: `do()` gains optional JSON request bodies (resent per retry attempt); typed `Me()` and `CreateAPIKey()`.
- `internal/output`: `Printer.EmitJSONLine` (compact NDJSON building block).
- `internal/mockapi`: the four auth endpoints, frozen fixtures (`TJSPLLAV`, scripted pending→success poll, 415 on non-JSON bodies).
- e2e smoke: real binary runs `login --json` against the mock — asserts the NDJSON stream, `credentials.json` mode 0600, and a follow-up `auth status` round-trip.
- README: "Authentication" section (laptop / SSH-via-phone / unattended `POSITRONICK_API_KEY`); AGENTS.md layout updated.

## Golden-file changes (public contract — AGENTS.md rule)
- **New**: `login.ndjson`, `logout.json`, `auth-status-{loggedout,device,apikey,stale}.json`, `auth-status.txt`, `auth-token-create.json`.
- **Regenerated**: `agent-docs.json` / `agent-docs.txt` — additive only (the new `login`, `logout`, `auth …` commands via the existing tree-walk; no hand-written docs).
- No existing command output changed.

## Design decisions & deviations
1. **`Poll` returns `*Token` (token + token_type + expires_in), not a bare `accessToken string`** as the brief's signature sketched: the store's `expiresAt` field needs the server-reported lifetime — fabricating it client-side would be a lie. Sole intentional deviation.
2. `/api/me` + `api-key/create` go through `api.Client` (gets auth injection, UA, envelope decoding, GET retries) rather than duplicating that in `internal/auth`; only the unauthenticated device endpoints use a plain client, per the brief.
3. `auth status` reports `method` even when credentials are rejected (shows what was tried), and adds a `hint` field; user object omitted unless the live check succeeded.
4. Mock advertises `interval: 0` so tests never really sleep — interval pacing and `slow_down` growth are unit-tested in `internal/auth` with the injected clock.
5. `--json` for `logout`/`auth status`/`token create` uses the CLI's standard indented `EmitJSON` (consistent with every existing command); only `login` streams compact NDJSON, as specced.
6. Golden tests normalize the mock server's random-port URL to `https://mock.positronick.test` before comparing, keeping the files byte-stable.
7. `.golangci.yml`: `APIKey` gets the same revive-stutter exclusion (with rationale) as the existing `APIError`.

## Gates
- `go build ./...` ✓ · `go test ./... -race` ✓ · `golangci-lint run` 0 issues ✓ · `gofmt -l .` empty ✓

author: philihp
body:
Collapses standalone config files into defaults and package.json, and updates dependencies. Net −41 lines, 5 fewer files at the repo root.

## Config simplification
- **tsup**: deleted `tsup.config.js`; the build is now just `tsup src/index.ts --format esm,cjs --dts --clean`. The glob entry was unnecessary (single source file), `splitting`/`sourcemap` were dropped, and the target is picked up from tsconfig automatically. Output files are byte-for-byte equivalent to before.
- **prettier**: `.prettierrc.json` → `"prettier"` key in package.json.
- **lint-staged**: `lint-staged.config.js` → `"lint-staged"` key in package.json.
- **tsconfig**: removed options that are defaults or implied (`moduleResolution`, `lib`, `esModuleInterop`, `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames`, `isolatedModules`). `ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` has to stay — tsup's dts build internally sets the deprecated `baseUrl` option, which TS 6 otherwise errors on (now documented with a comment).
- **eslint**: replaced the blanket `no-constant-binary-expression: off` (which existed only because eslint was linting the bundled `dist/` output) with an `ignores: ['dist/']` entry, and dropped unused browser globals.
- **npm packaging**: deleted `.npmignore` (the `files` field already scopes the tarball) and simplified `files` to `["dist"]` since the single-entry build no longer emits test files. Deleted the empty `.coveralls.yml`.
- **husky**: `prepare` now runs `husky` (the standard v9 setup) and the build moved to `prepublishOnly`; the pre-commit hook drops the deprecated `husky.sh` shim. Verified working — the hook ran on this PR's commit.

## Updates
- Removed the explicit `esbuild` pin: 0.28.0 doesn't satisfy tsup's `^0.27.0` range, so tsup was resolving its own copy anyway.
- Bumped `@types/node` (latest 22.x, matching the `engines` floor), `eslint`, `lint-staged`, `prettier`.
- `.node-version` 22.12.0 → 24.16.0 (current active LTS), GitHub Actions `checkout`/`setup-node` v4 → v5.
- `src/index.ts` reformatted by prettier (it was out of compliance with the existing config).

## Verification
`tsc --noEmit`, build, all 5 tests, `eslint`, `prettier --check .`, and `npm pack --dry-run` all pass; both the CJS and ESM dist entry points were smoke-tested with `require()`/`import()`.

author: mads-hartmann
body:
## Description

This PR configures the repository's development environment with a [Dev Container](https://containers.dev/) and [Ona tasks/services](https://ona.com/docs/ona/configuration/tasks-and-services/overview).

A Dev Container is a checked-in environment definition that describes the container image, runtimes, tools, and editor configuration needed to work in this repository. Ona tasks and services are checked-in automations in `.ona/automations.yaml`: tasks run repeatable one-shot workflows such as dependency installation, checks, and builds, while services run long-lived development processes such as app servers, preview servers, or databases.

This is useful to merge because it makes environment startup and common development workflows reproducible for contributors and agents, instead of relying on local machine state or undocumented setup steps.

Ona automated this setup while creating or tuning the project so future development starts faster and the repository is easier to work on in new environments.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Summary Deep bug scan of recent commits (Phase A/B userspace vendoring) found three critical correctness issues in early-boot daemons. ## Bugs fixed ### 1. ramfs `fchown` used scheme handle as inode (security) - **Impact:** After enough opens, scheme handle IDs diverge from filesystem inode numbers. `fchown(fd, …)` was authorized by the kernel against the opened file's inode, but ramfs mutated `files[handle]` instead of resolving the handle first — changing ownership on the wrong file. - **Root cause:** `fchown` indexed `files` directly with the scheme-internal handle; `fchmod` in the same file correctly resolves via `handles.get(fd)?.as_inode()?`. - **Fix:** Resolve handle → inode before mutating, matching `fchmod`. ### 2. ramfs `unlinkat` operator-precedence bug (breakage) - **Impact:** `!inode != ROOT` parsed as bitwise `(!inode) != ROOT`, so unlink from the scheme root always returned `EACCES` — files could not be removed on ramfs instances. - **Fix:** Remove erroneous `!` to match `openat`'s root check. ### 3. randd x86_64 ignored `rdrand` failure (security) - **Impact:** When `rdrand` failed (CF=0), randd still marked seeding successful and initialized ChaCha20 from uninitialized stack data, weakening all subsequent random output. - **Fix:** Check CF via `setc` and only accept the seed when all `rdrand` rounds succeed (AArch64 path already checked for zero). ### 4. bootstrap `spawn` used invalid FD after child failure (boot corruption) - **Impact:** If a daemon child exited or failed before readiness notification, the parent broke out of the `call_ro` loop with `new_fd == usize::MAX` and continued boot. - **Fix:** Mirror `init`'s explicit handling: panic on EOF, wrong fd count, or syscall error. ## Validation - `cargo check -p ramfs -p randd` passes - `cargo test -p randd` — pre-existing test compile issue (`open` vs `openat`), unrelated to this change ## Not fixed (reported, lower priority) - logd unbounded per-PID line buffer (memory DoS) - procmgr `/scheme/proc/ps` missing UID check (info disclosure)

`get_device_properties(x.device)` and reads CUDA-specific fields (`major`, `multi_processor_count`, `max_threads_per_multi_processor`). These attributes are not exposed on XPU device properties, so the test fails with an `AttributeError` when run on Intel GPU.

body:
## Problem

The database tables were never created automatically, causing the server to crash on login/register requests. The migration file called `pool.end()` and `process.exit()` at the end, which destroyed the connection pool and terminated the process — making it unusable as an imported module. It also self-invoked rather than exporting a callable function, so `app.js` had no way to trigger it.

## Solution

Refactored `migrate.js` to export an async function instead of self-invoking, and removed the `pool.end()` and `process.exit()` calls so the pool stays alive after migrations run. Updated `app.js` to import and call `migrate()` before `app.listen()`, so all tables and default categories are created on every deploy. If migrations fail, the error is logged and the process exits with code 1 to surface the failure clearly.

### Changes
- **Modified** `backend/API/src/config/migrate.js`
- **Modified** `backend/API/src/app.js`

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bugs fixed ### Bug 1 — Stale UTxO cache after every Quick Pay (`sendStorePayment`) **Root cause:** `sendStorePayment` never called `refreshBalancesFromChain()` after a successful transaction submit. `sendMultiTransaction` (the standard send path) has always called it; the store-payment path omitted it. **Impact:** After every Quick Pay, `currentUtxos` still holds the pre-payment UTxOs. Any subsequent fee estimate or send attempt references already-spent inputs, causing the blockchain to reject the follow-on transaction with a "UTxO not found" error. The displayed balance also stays wrong until the user manually pulls to refresh. **Fix:** Added `await refreshBalancesFromChain()` in `sendStorePayment` before returning the tx hash, mirroring the existing call in `sendMultiTransaction`. --- ### Bug 2 — Pay Now button permanently disabled for payments ≥ 100 ADA **Root cause:** `PaymentConfirmView.estimateFee()` called the generic `estimateNetworkFee()`, which internally builds a *standard* transaction where the Vendano fee is added **on top** of `sendCoin` (payer pays `base + vendanoFee + networkFee`). The actual submit path is `sendStorePayment` / `buildCandidateTransactionStore`, a different structure where the Vendano fee is deducted from the merchant output — the **payer only needs `base + tip + networkFee`**. With a 1% Vendano fee, the standard estimator over-estimates by ~1 ADA for any payment ≥ 100 ADA. If the payer's balance falls in the window `[base + networkFee, base + vendanoFee + networkFee)`, `estimateFee()` throws, `netFeeAda` stays `nil`, and the Pay Now button is permanently disabled — even though the actual payment would succeed. **Trigger example:** User has 101.5 ADA, tries to pay 101 ADA. Standard estimator needs ~102.2 ADA → throws → button locked. Actual store payment needs ~101.2 ADA → would succeed. **Fix:** Added `estimateNetworkFeeForStorePay()` in `WalletService-Send.swift` that mirrors the exact `merchantCoin`/`feeCoin` computation from `sendStorePayment` and builds via `buildCandidateTransactionStore`. `PaymentConfirmView.estimateFee()` now calls this method instead. --- **Files changed:** - `vendano/Services/WalletService-Send.swift` — added `refreshBalancesFromChain()` call + new `estimateNetworkFeeForStorePay()` function - `vendano/Views/PaymentConfirmView.swift` — updated `estimateFee()` to call `estimateNetworkFeeForStorePay()`

提高綁定完成率與首封訊息送達率。現況顧客要走「加好友」與「LIFF 授權」兩件事但 UI 混為一談；只授權沒加好友的人，推播必被 LINE 拒絕（過去會白白重試 6 次進 dead-letter），而且綁定連結把 base64 的姓名/電話塞在 URL（隱私缺陷）。

## 變更

**好友狀態閉環**
- `LineBindPage` 在 `getProfile` 後呼叫 `liff.getFriendship()`；未加好友 → POST 帶 `friendFlag:false`，UI 顯示「最後一步：加入官方帳號好友」+ 補發說明。
- 後端 `lineBind`：`friendFlag === false` → 寫 `pushBlocked:'not-friend'`、跳過首封推播；回 `needFriend:true`。
- `lineWebhook` follow 事件：清掉該使用者所有 `pushBlocked` 旗標（解除封鎖重加也適用），並對仍有效的未來訂位自動補發確認卡片（受既有防重保護）。

**URL 去個資**
- 綁定連結只帶 `bookingId + token`，不再有 payload 參數；顯示資料改由 `lineGetBooking` 回讀（含 React StrictMode 雙跑安全的 fetch 狀態機）。舊版已寄出連結的 payload 仍相容解析。
- `lineBind` POST body 瘦身為 `{ booking: {id, token}, line }`——後端本來就權威重讀。

**CTA 重設計**
- ConfirmPage / ManageBookingPage 改兩段式「① 加入好友 → ② 綁定通知」，並說明「先綁定後加好友也會自動補發」。

**Ops checklist**（functions/README.md）
- LINE console：LIFF **Add friend option 設 aggressive**（授權畫面同時勾加好友）、webhook 必開（follow 補發依賴它）。

## 測試

- 新 `tests/services/lineService.test.js`：綁定 URL 帶 id/token/useLiff、**隱私回歸（URL 不含姓名/電話）**、舊 payload 相容解碼。
- 新 `e2e/line-bind.spec.js`：LIFF stub 全流程——未加好友顯示引導、已加好友綁定成功、**POST body 不含個資**。（途中修了兩個 E2E 坑：寬鬆 regex 誤攔 Vite 模組請求、跨網域 mock 缺 CORS 標頭。）
- Vitest 706 全綠、Playwright 16 全綠、build 成功。

## 部署

functions 先（webhook/lineBind 向下相容，新前端未上前行為不變）→ LINE console 設定 → 前端。出問題關 `lineUseLiff` 即回舊行為。

author: cleverdino
body:
## Summary
Completely refactored the football statistics sync system to use openfootball's GitHub-hosted historical match data as the primary source, while retaining TheSportsDB for live current-season tables only. This enables comprehensive historical coverage back to 1888-89 with proper matchday structure and accurate points rules.

## Key Changes

- **Data source migration**: Replaced TheSportsDB `eventsseason.php` API calls with direct parsing of openfootball text files from `https://github.com/openfootball/eng-england`
  
- **Historical match parsing**: Implemented `parse_ofb_text()` function to parse openfootball's text format, supporting:
  - Matchday/Round headers
  - Standalone and inline date lines
  - Played matches (N-N format) and scheduled matches (?-? format)
  - Proper date parsing with month/day extraction and season year inference

- **Points rule accuracy**: Added `win_pts()` function to apply correct historical rules:
  - 2 points per win before 1981-82
  - 3 points per win from 1981-82 onwards

- **Competition era naming**: Implemented `era_name()` to track proper competition names across history:
  - PL: First Division → Premier League (1992)
  - ELC: Second Division → First Division → Championship (2004)
  - L1: Third Division → League One (2004)
  - L2: Fourth Division → League Two (2004)
  - Special handling for split Third Division North/South (pre-1958)

- **Schema updates**: Added `competition_name` field to matches and snapshot tables to preserve historical competition names

- **Simplified badge handling**: Removed complex badge injection logic; crests now sourced only from live TheSportsDB tables (historical data doesn't include badges)

- **Improved table reconstruction**: Refactored `sort_table()` and `apply_result()` as pure functions for cleaner matchday-by-matchday and date-ordered snapshot generation

- **League configuration**: Restructured league config to specify tier file number and start year for each competition, enabling flexible historical coverage

## Implementation Details

- Openfootball files are fetched with 20-second timeout and cached in memory to avoid redundant requests
- Historical seasons are skipped if already cached (unless current season)
- Date-ordered snapshots now built from openfootball data to handle postponed matches played out of sequence
- National League remains TheSportsDB-only (not available in openfootball)
- Set `set_time_limit(0)` to handle large historical datasets

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: glenn-jocher
body:
## QNN export and inference fixes

Three corrections to the Qualcomm QNN export/inference path, verified against the [ONNX Runtime QNN EP docs](https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/execution-providers/QNN-ExecutionProvider.html) and the [ExecuTorch Qualcomm backend schema](https://docs.pytorch.org/executorch/stable/backends-qualcomm.html):

### 1. Correct the HTP arch → Snapdragon mapping (docs + messages)

The documented mapping was off by one generation: `68` is the Snapdragon 888 (SM8350) and `69` is the 8 Gen 1 / 8+ Gen 1 (SM8450/SM8475) — not 865 and 888 as previously listed. The Snapdragon 865 has no HTP at all (HVX/HTA only, SNPE-era) and cannot be targeted by the QNN HTP backend. Also adds `81` (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, SM8850) to `QNN_HTP_ARCHS` — already referenced by ONNX Runtime 1.26 — and notes that `73` covers Snapdragon X Elite laptops.

### 2. Fix QNN backend load on monolithic ONNX Runtime builds

`QNNBackend.load_model` called `register_execution_provider_library()` unconditionally, but `qnn_library_paths()` returns `ep_library=None` when QNN is built into ONNX Runtime (no plugin registration needed), crashing at load. The backend now mirrors the handling already proven in `onnx2qnn`: plugin builds register the EP library and select devices; monolithic builds create the session directly via `providers=[...]`.

### 3. Quantize to 16-bit activations + INT8 weights (A16W8)

`get_qnn_qdq_config` was called with defaults (uint8 activations). The ONNX Runtime QNN docs recommend uint16 activations with uint8 weights as the accuracy/performance balance for the HTP backend, which matters for accuracy-sensitive tasks like semantic segmentation. Docs updated to match.

Note: this changes the exported artifact — `_qnn.onnx` files exported previously should be re-exported.

## Testing

- All edited files parse and `ultralytics` imports cleanly; `QNN_HTP_ARCHS` resolves to `{68, 69, 73, 75, 79, 81}`.
- `test_export_qnn` requires `onnxruntime-qnn` (Windows / Linux ARM64) and is unchanged.
- On-device validation on Snapdragon hardware is planned this week and will exercise both the backend fix and the A16W8 accuracy/latency tradeoff.

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary
🛠️ This PR improves Qualcomm QNN support and documentation by updating quantization behavior, expanding Snapdragon target coverage, and making QNN model loading more robust.

### 📊 Key Changes
- 🚀 **Updated QNN quantization details** across code and docs:
  - QNN export now uses **INT8 weights with 16-bit activations** instead of describing the pipeline as fully INT8.
  - Logging and docstrings were updated to reflect this recommended Hexagon NPU accuracy/performance balance.
- 📱 **Expanded Snapdragon architecture support**:
  - Added support for **HTP arch `81`**, mapped to **Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5**.
  - Updated architecture mappings for existing targets like `68`, `69`, and `73` to better reflect supported Snapdragon platforms.
- 🔌 **Improved QNN backend loading logic**:
  - The QNN runtime loader now handles both cases where the QNN Execution Provider must be manually registered and where it is already built into ONNX Runtime.
  - This makes QNN inference setup more flexible across different environments.
- 📝 **Refreshed QNN documentation**:
  - Export examples, argument tables, and precision notes were updated to match the new quantization behavior and supported hardware list.
- 🧹 **Minor custom trainer docs cleanup**:
  - Removed an unnecessary import from the custom trainer inference example to simplify the workflow.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ **More accurate QNN guidance** helps users better understand what is actually produced during export, reducing confusion around deployment.
- ⚡ **Better quantization defaults** should provide a stronger balance of speed, model size, and accuracy on Qualcomm Hexagon NPUs.
- 🌍 **Wider device support** enables deployment on newer Snapdragon hardware, including **Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5**.
- 🧩 **More reliable backend initialization** reduces the chance of QNN runtime issues caused by differences in ONNX Runtime packaging.
- 📚 **Clearer docs and examples** make QNN export and inference easier for both new users and experienced developers.

author: dxmone
body:
## Problem

Three loops in `Buffer.resize` iterate `lines.maxLength` — the scrollback **capacity** — instead of `lines.count`, the number of lines actually in the buffer. `CircularList`'s subscript materializes a `BufferLine` for every empty slot it touches (the getter calls `makeEmpty`), so each loop walks and allocates the entire scrollback capacity even for a nearly empty buffer.

With a large scrollback this makes every column-count change expensive. At `changeScrollback(50_000)`, a single resize costs **30–70 ms of main-thread time per terminal** (~200× the cost at the default 500-line scrollback), measured headless on an M-series Mac. In an app with several visible terminals, every window resize, divider drag, or layout switch multiplies that — it shows up as typing lag and slow view switching. Patched, the same resize is **~0.3 ms**.

## Fix

Iterate `0..<lines.count` in the three sites. This is safe:

- The two column-resize loops (widen at the top of `resize`, narrow after `reflow`) only need to touch lines that exist. Empty slots are materialized on demand by `makeEmpty` → `getBlankLine`, which uses the buffer's *current* `cols` and therefore already produces lines at the new width.
- The `DEBUG: Post-condition` loop would otherwise materialize blank lines for the whole capacity on every resize — and worse, they'd be created at the **old** `cols` value (`cols` is updated after the check), which trips the `abort()` when widening.

## Measurements

Headless `Terminal` with `changeScrollback(50_000)` and 1,000 lines of content, resizing between 80/120/200 columns:

| resize | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 80 → 120 cols | ~50 ms | 0.70 ms |
| 120 → 80 cols | ~40 ms | 0.32 ms |
| 80 → 200 cols | ~60 ms | 0.90 ms |
| 200 → 80 cols | ~45 ms | 0.36 ms |

## 📝 Description

**Resolves #3 ** - *GSSoC '26 Good First Issue: Backend: Add Detection Rules for Private Keys & API Tokens*

This PR implements robust regex-based scanning for various hardcoded secrets and introduces a clean unit testing suite to verify correctness, preventing developers from accidentally committing credentials.

## 🛠️ Changes Implemented

- **Modular Secrets Scanner Helper:** Extracted duplicate scanning logic from `backend/index.js` into a new, dedicated helper file (`backend/utils/secretsScanner.js`). This improves modularity and keeps the Express routes cleanly decoupled from business logic.
- **Added Secret Detection Rules:**

author: sdolidze
body:
## Description

The AI writeback sandbox previously ran with **unrestricted outbound network access**. This locks its egress to an allowlist — Anthropic for the Claude CLI and GitHub/GitLab for clone/push — and denies everything else, mirroring the data-app sandbox in `AppGenerateService`.

Applied in `AiWritebackService.createSandbox` via E2B's `network` config:

```ts
network: {
    allowOut: ['api.anthropic.com', 'github.com', 'gitlab.com'],
    denyOut: [ALL_TRAFFIC],
}
```

**Sandbox egress, before → after**

Before:
- any host — allowed

After:
- `api.anthropic.com` — allowed (Claude CLI)
- `github.com` / `gitlab.com` — allowed (clone / push)
- everything else — denied (`ALL_TRAFFIC`)

Only the *fresh* sandbox path (`Sandbox.create`) is affected. Backend-side traffic — the E2B control plane and the GitHub/GitLab PR API — does not traverse sandbox egress, so it is unaffected. `lightdash compile` runs with warehouse credentials stripped, so it needs no warehouse host on the allowlist.

## Test plan

- `pnpm -F backend typecheck:fast` passes.
- Live writeback run (sandbox create → clone → agent → PR) against a GitHub-connected project — verifying the allowlist doesn't break the happy path. (Running separately; will confirm in a comment.)

author: madgodinc
body:
**Circle 2, axis: forgetting (средне → хорошо, second half).** Decay was BINARY: cold iff `access_count==0 AND old`. A single ancient access made a memory permanently warm, no matter how stale. The `last_access` timestamp was collected in the access journal but **never read by decay** — a dead field.

## Change
`coldness_score(created, last_access, count, now)` returns "days since last relevance":
- never-accessed → scores as its age (the old signal preserved)
- accessed → cools from `last_access`, divided by a gentle `log10` frequency damp so heavy use slows cooling without making memory immortal

A memory used 5× but untouched ~516 days is now cold — which the binary model never caught. The dead `last_access` field is alive (`run` feeds it in, sorts coldest-first).

## Safety (critic blocker, fixed)
The recency model marks **more** memories cold than the binary one, so feeding it to the destructive `--prune-cold` would silently delete more than before. **Split into two sets:**
- **archive** gets the full recency-weighted `cold` (reversible — a false positive costs a `restore`)
- **prune** gets only the conservative binary subset (`count==0`), so `--prune-cold` deletes *exactly* what it did before the recency change — never more silently.

A unit test pins `cold_prune` is a subset of `cold`.

*(My first PR description claimed a PR-5 prune warning protected this; the critic caught that the warning only fires when BOTH flags are set. The two-set split is the real fix.)*

## Verified
- `coldness_is_recency_weighted_not_binary` — the discriminating case (count=5, 516 days stale → cold) + monotonicity + frequency damp.
- `prune_subset_is_conservative_binary` — the safety invariant.
- `cold_requires_age_and_zero_access` — backward compat.
- 330 unit green, clippy + fmt clean. `TODO(circle-3-calibration)` on the damp/cutoff (honest: provisional constants).

author: iocrazy
body:
## Summary

Front-end half of the mask cutout mode (Phase 3, canvas node editor). Pairs with #628 (backend derive-mask-cutout). Wiring into OutputNode lands in the follow-up PR.

The stroke model is resolution-free: normalized points + brush size as a fraction of image width. The SVG overlay previews at display size; export rasterizes at the source image's natural pixel size, so the persisted cutout is exact regardless of how small the editor rendered.

- **maskMath** — immutable helpers: `beginStroke` / `extendStroke` (with a distance floor so pointermove streams don't bloat the model), `hasMaskContent` (eraser-only masks keep nothing → commit disabled), `strokePath` (single points become zero-length segments so round caps render dots).
- **MaskBrushTool** — pointer painting over the image. Preview uses an SVG `<mask>` (brush strokes white, eraser strokes black, applied to a translucent indigo wash) so erasing visually punches holes. Reports `naturalWidth/Height` up for export.
- **maskExport.strokesToMaskPngBase64** — offscreen canvas raster: black fill, brush white / eraser black, round caps/joins matching the preview geometry. Returns raw base64 (the endpoint's `mask_png_base64` shape). Canvas usage is confined to the commit path since jsdom has no real 2D context.
- **MaskEditorModal** — Brush/Eraser toggle, S/M/L sizes, Clear, live stroke rendering, Cut Out disabled until at least one brush stroke, `committing` freezes every control including Esc/backdrop. Same cancel semantics as the crop/grid modals.

## Test Coverage

- 11 maskMath tests (immutability, distance floor, clamping, content detection, path building)
- 5 maskExport tests (base64 payload, op order black→white→black with correct line widths, empty-stroke skip, degenerate dims, missing context)
- 9 modal tests (tool/size toggles, paint→enable→commit payload with fallback raster size, eraser-only disabled, Clear, re-open reset, cancel routes, committing freeze)
- Full frontend suite: **869 passed** (was 844); tsc baseline unchanged (104)

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors

author: christianhg
body:
Precedes #2772, which makes the operation type names public via `editor.on('operation', ...)` — renaming after that ships would be a breaking change; right now it's a zero-cost internal rename.

`insert_text` → `insert.text`, `remove_text` → `remove.text`, `set_selection` → `set.selection` (`insert`/`set`/`unset` unchanged), aligning the operation vocabulary with the behavior-event naming convention — a behavior event like `insert.text` now produces an operation of the same name.

No compatibility surface: operations are never serialized (patches use their own type vocabulary; undo history is in-memory) and no other package references these literals. Mechanical rename of 118 occurrences across 38 files, with the few non-type-checked spots (the raw string array in patch generation, comments) verified by hand.

Verified: types, lint, 768 unit tests, full chromium suite (1630), mutation/undo-redo suites on all three browsers.

author: acaldas
body:
## What

Makes one Connect bundle servable under any subpath, resolved at serve time instead of build time.

- `ph connect build --dynamic-base` (new flag in `packages/shared/clis/args/connect.ts`, wired through `clis/ph-cli/src/services/connect-build.ts`) sets the Vite `base` to the placeholder token `/__PH_DYNAMIC_BASE__/`.
- New `connectDynamicBasePlugin` (`packages/builder-tools/connect-utils/vite-plugins/dynamic-base.ts`) rewrites every placeholder-prefixed string literal in emitted JS chunks to a runtime expression reading `globalThis.__PH_DYNAMIC_BASE__` (falling back to `/`). The rewrite runs in `renderChunk` as per-match MagicString edits — no AST byte-offset splicing, which corrupts Rolldown chunks — and returns a hires sourcemap per edited chunk, which the bundler composes into the chunk's map chain so the emitted `.map` files stay aligned (including the worker prelude's line shift).
- HTML keeps the literal token: the serving runtime substitutes it per-request.
- Worker chunks get a prelude that derives the global in worker scope from the worker's own script URL (`self.location.pathname` minus `assets/<file>`), since the runtime only injects the global into the main-thread document.
- `getDeployBasePath()` (`apps/connect/src/connect.config.ts`) resolves the effective base at runtime; the router base and favicon now participate in the deploy base.

## Hardening from review

- The rewrite regex anchors the opening/closing quote via a backreference, so a literal containing the other quote character (e.g. an apostrophe inside a double-quoted string) is no longer truncated/corrupted.
- `generateBundle` asserts no residual placeholder remains in JS chunks or CSS assets — the build fails loudly rather than shipping the raw token. HTML is exempt by design (serve-time substitution).
- Rewrites carry sourcemaps: each edited chunk returns a MagicString-generated hires map from `renderChunk`, so column shifts from the placeholder rewrite and the worker prelude's prepended line are reflected in the emitted maps (Sentry uploads them when configured).
- Unit tests for the plugin added (`packages/builder-tools/connect-utils/vite-plugins/dynamic-base.test.ts`), including sourcemap assertions.

## Serve-time contract

The token `/__PH_DYNAMIC_BASE__/` (in HTML) and the global `globalThis.__PH_DYNAMIC_BASE__` (set before the entry bundle loads) are consumed by ph-clint's connect-server in a companion PR. Token name and global name are the cross-repo contract.

## Merge order

This is 1 of 3 integration PRs (monorepo → ph-clint → vetra-cli). Merge this one first.

## Commits

- f1a5df342 feat(connect): runtime-dynamic deploy base for Connect builds

## Test status

- packages/builder-tools: `vitest --run` 27/27 passed (includes the dynamic-base plugin tests with sourcemap coverage); `tsc` clean.
- apps/connect: `tsc` clean.
- packages/shared: `vitest --run` 124/124 passed (no `tsc` script in that package).
- clis/ph-cli: `tsc` clean.

No pre-existing failures encountered.
