author: moqimoqidea
body:
## Problem

Gemini 3+ models return HTTP 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT: Thought signature is not valid` on multi-turn conversations that span across subtasks (e.g. after the agent loop restarts with history loaded from the DB).

### Root cause

1. When Gemini 3+ returns a response containing a function call with a "thought", the `langchain-google-genai` library serialises the thought signature as a text block in the message content:
   ```json
   {"type": "text", "text": "", "extras": {"signature": "<base64>"}}
   ```
2. `_serialize_messages_chain()` in `graph_builder.py` persists this text block (with signature) to the DB.
3. In a subsequent subtask — potentially hours later — the history is reloaded and the stale, expired signature is sent back to the Gemini API verbatim.
4. The Gemini API rejects the request with `400 Thought signature is not valid`.

The `google → google` same-provider path in `strip_foreign_reasoning_blocks()` previously had no handling for this case (complete pass-through).

## Fix

Per the [official Gemini API documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking), omitting non-function-call thought signatures is explicitly safe:

> "You won't receive a blocking error if you *omit* [non-FC signatures], though performance may degrade."

Sending an **invalid/stale** signature is strictly worse than omitting it (causes a hard 400 rejection).

This PR adds:
- **`_clear_google_thought_signatures(content)`** — a helper that strips `extras.signature` from text blocks in Google message history. Returns the original list unchanged (same reference) when no signatures are present, avoiding unnecessary copies.
- **Google branch in `strip_foreign_reasoning_blocks()`** — handles the `google → google` same-provider path by calling the helper above on each assistant message's list content.

Within-subtask signatures (managed in-memory by `langchain-google-genai` via `DUMMY_THOUGHT_SIGNATURE`) are not affected by this change.

## Tests

17 new unit tests added in two new test classes:
- `TestClearGoogleThoughtSignatures` — direct tests of the helper (8 cases)
- `TestStripForeignReasoningBlocksGoogle` — integration tests of the full pipeline for the Google path (9 cases)

All 58 tests pass.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Enhanced message filtering to properly handle Google thought signatures in text blocks and prevent replay of stale cross-subtask signatures.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive test coverage for thought signature clearing and Google provider-specific message filtering behavior.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: aliciadriani
body:
## What

Foundation slice for the new `@adobe/spacecat-shared-project-engine-client` package — the typed integration with the Semrush **Project Engine API** (`/enterprise/projects/api`).

Part of **LLMO-5459** (epic) / **LLMO-5461** (client + generated types). This PR is **foundation only**: vendor the spec and wire the conversion-and-type-generation pipeline. The client wrapper, IMS handler move, and stateful mock land in follow-up PRs.

## Scope of this PR

- **Vendored spec** — `spec/projectengine_swagger_public.yaml` (Swagger 2.0, `basePath: /enterprise/projects/api`). Manual-refresh only; Semrush provides the file, no endpoint access. Not patched/edited.
- **Generation pipeline** (npm scripts):
  - `spec:convert` — swagger2openapi `--patch` v2→3.x → `build/openapi3.json` (intermediate, gitignored). Exists **only** to feed the type generators.
  - `generate:ts` — openapi-typescript → `src/generated/types.ts`
  - `generate:pydantic` — datamodel-code-generator → `python/serenity_project_engine/` (Pydantic v2)
  - `mock` — Counterfact reads the **raw v2** spec directly (`:4010`), never the converted artifact.
- **Conventions** — follows `spacecat-shared`: JS + ESM, JSDoc-typed source, mocha + chai + c8, `@adobe/eslint-config-helix`. The scaffold's TS surface is ported to JS+JSDoc; `types.ts` is a type artifact only.
- **Smoke test** — `test/foundation.test.js` asserts the vendored spec invariants (Swagger 2.0, basePath, `Auth-Data-Jwt` header) and that generated `types.ts` carries the expected `paths` interface + known v1/v2 routes.

## Commit structure

1. `feat(...)` — vendored spec + generation pipeline + config + smoke test
2. `chore(...) [skip ci]` — generated TS + Pydantic types, committed separately and marked `linguist-generated` (collapsed in review, excluded from diff counts)

## Validation

- `npm run generate` runs end-to-end (build/openapi3.json → types.ts → python package)

author: nategeier
body:
Autopilot queue item 2. PR targets `autopilot`, not `main`. Independent of #26 (no shared code; whichever merges second can switch this route from `getSessionAddress` to the Bearer-aware `getAuthAddress` — noted inline).

## What
- **`lib/grant-typed-data.ts`** — the canonical `SpendGrant` EIP-712 struct: Base `chainId`, **sorted lowercased allowlist** (order-insensitive signatures), USD caps as **1e6 micros** (EIP-712 has no decimals; matches USDC atomic units; omitted lifetime cap signs as 0), expiry as unix seconds. Always built **from the stored row**, never client input — a signature can only attest to terms the server actually enforces.
- **`GET /api/grants/[id]/signature`** — returns the exact JSON-safe payload to sign + `signed` flag (what the wallet UI / SDK will consume).
- **`PUT /api/grants/[id]/signature`** — verifies with `publicClient.verifyTypedData` (EOAs **and** ERC-1271/6492 smart wallets — same trust path as SIWE sign-in), persists to the existing `signature` column. No schema change.
- **`signed: boolean`** on grant list, read, and PATCH responses.
- **Signature voiding** — changed terms invalidate the attestation: cap edits (PATCH) and allowlist re-derivations (`lib/approvals.ts` toggle sync, only when the host set actually changed) null the signature; re-sign restores it.

## Verification
Temp script (deleted before commit) against dev server + real Neon, throwaway keys, **12/12 green**:
- typed-data payload correct (sorted allow, `perCallUsdMicros: '50000'`, `totalUsdMicros: '10000000'`)
- owner signature → 200 + persisted; **foreign signature → 400**; malformed → 400
- cap change → `signed:false` + `signature:null`; re-sign from the GET payload → 200
- anon → 401; other wallet → 404; cleanup verified (0 rows left)

`npx tsc --noEmit` ✓ · `npm run build` ✓ (`/api/grants/[id]/signature` registered)

author: luciferyang
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds an internal config `spark.sql.codegen.compiler` that selects the compiler used to turn generated Java source into bytecode:

- `janino` (default): the current behavior. The existing compile path in `CodeGenerator.doCompile` moved to `JaninoCodeCompiler` unchanged.
- `jdk`: compiles with `javax.tools.JavaCompiler` from the running JDK.

Generators keep emitting exactly the source they emit today; the JDK backend adapts it where javac is stricter than Janino. It wraps the class body into a real compilation unit, hoists class-body `import` lines, rewrites binary inner-class names (`Outer$Inner`) to the source form, and strips the explicit `Function1` bridge that Janino needs but javac synthesizes itself. Referenced classes are resolved through the task's context classloader (the same way Janino resolves them) rather than a `-classpath`, so classes that exist only on a runtime loader still work. javac runs on a dedicated thread so task interrupts cannot break its jar reads.

A few shared codegen templates were adjusted to be legal under both compilers, e.g. explicit casts where Janino erases generics, and `catch (Throwable)` for invoked methods declaring `throws Throwable`. These are no-ops under Janino. Two changes are structural rather than template tweaks: `ColumnarIterator` now extends `scala.collection.AbstractIterator[InternalRow]` instead of mixing in the `Iterator` trait directly (javac cannot subclass a scalac-compiled class that fixes a trait's type parameter while mixing the trait in directly: the raw mixin forwarders clash with `IterableOnceOps`' generic signatures; it is still an `Iterator[InternalRow]`, so no call sites change), and the unused `BufferHolder` import was removed from `GenerateColumnAccessor`'s generated code (the JDK backend compiles generated code as a separate compilation unit and enforces access control that Janino does not; the generated code never actually referenced the package-private `BufferHolder`).

There are two kinds of code for which we have not yet found a way to use javac directly, so they are routed to Janino - decided up front, not as a fallback after a failed compile: codegen in REPL / Connect interactive sessions (javac cannot resolve REPL-generated classes), and generated code referencing a class nested in a Scala `package object` (`package` is a Java reserved word, so the reference cannot be spelled in Java source). A one-time INFO log records each routing so the choice is visible to operators.

Note: during development the default was temporarily flipped to `jdk` so that CI ran the entire test suite against the new backend (see the earlier runs on this PR's branch). The default in this PR is `janino`, i.e. the default behavior is unchanged.

### Why are the changes needed?

Whole-stage codegen depends entirely on Janino, which is unmaintained upstream (last release 3.1.12, Feb 2024). This gives Spark an alternative that is maintained on the JDK release cadence, without changing the default: Janino stays preferred since it compiles small generated units 30-300x faster, but if a Janino bug or incompatibility ever blocks Spark, users can switch with one config instead of waiting on an upstream that may never release again.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The config is internal and the default behavior is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- New `CodeCompilerSuite` with 40 tests covering backend selection and routing, the source adaptations (import hoisting, bridge stripping, inner-class-name rewriting including string/comment safety), class resolution through enumerable and non-enumerable classloaders, compile-error type parity between the backends, per-backend separation in the compile cache, and interrupt isolation.
- The full GHA matrix passes with the default flipped to `jdk`, i.e. the whole Spark test suite compiles and runs on javac-produced bytecode.
- The Janino path is a code move; it was validated unchanged with `SQLQueryTestSuite` and the codegen suites under `janino` locally.

author: charles-zablit
body:
The Windows recipes for these macros were printf "%s\n" $(1). The callers wrap content in single quotes (for the POSIX printf), but the test recipes run under cmd.exe on Windows, which keeps the single quotes literal and word-splits on spaces, and the bundled printf additionally mangles backslashes and spaces. The result is garbage generated files (e.g. a modulemap whose first line is 'module, or a truncated SDK path from a "Program Files" directory).

Write the file with cmd's echo after stripping the callers' single quotes. echo runs in the recipe shell, so unlike GNU make's $(file ...) it still works after a preceding MKDIR_P in the same recipe.

This is a reland of https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/202612 which add the changes in the wrong if/else branch.

author: aaronjmars
body:
## What
Adds a **Hyperstition-deadline tiebreaker** clause to step 2 of `skills/feature/SKILL.md`. Before finalizing the idea pick in step 2.b, the skill now reads the `Active Targets` section of `memory/MEMORY.md`, identifies any unresolved hyperstition with a deadline within the next **10 days**, and — if exactly one unbuilt candidate in the batch directly advances such a hyperstition — picks it over evergreen alternatives, even when a different idea ranks higher on raw impact. If multiple candidates match, fall back to highest-impact among the matched subset. If none match, proceed with the highest-impact pick unchanged. The step requires logging the tiebreaker decision (or its absence) in the daily log entry under `**Hyperstition tiebreaker:**`.

## Why
On **2026-06-10**, the `feature` skill picked idea #5 (Chinese README) from the Jun-08 repo-actions batch over evergreen candidates #2 (Trending Topics), #3 (MCP Tool Catalog JSON), and #4 (Pre-Run Cost Estimator) — explicitly because the **Jun-15 Chinese-locale hyperstition deadline was 5 days away**. That judgment was made by the agent in-flight; the SKILL.md said only "pick the highest-impact idea." The rule lived in operator memory + log precedent, not in the skill prompt.

This PR encodes the same kind of one-off judgment that produced PR #53 (auth-posture step 7, Jun 6) and PR #55 (push-recap noise-exclusion step 5, Jun 8). The pattern is the same each time: a judgment call that worked, encode it so the next run doesn't have to re-derive it.

## Changes
- `skills/feature/SKILL.md`: new "Hyperstition-deadline tiebreaker" paragraph inserted at the bottom of step 2, scoped to step 2.b only. Names PR #155 as the past-application reference so future runs can read the precedent.

## Impact
Future feature-skill runs will mechanically check Active Targets in MEMORY.md for ≤10-day-out hyperstition deadlines before locking in the pick. No tiebreaker fires when no hyperstition is in window or no candidate matches — the change is additive, not restrictive. The 10-day window is tight enough that the rule rarely interferes with normal "highest-impact" selection; it only fires when a deadline is genuinely close.

author: larswa
body:
## Motivating real-world repro

From the user's live log: an accidental **0.313 s** key tap on quiet input produced the classic Danish subtitle-credit hallucination:

> `Danske tekster af Jesper Buhl Scandinavian Text Service 2018`

That's 60 chars from 0.31 s ≈ **193 chars/s** — humanly impossible — with segment metrics `no_speech_prob=0.0, avg_logprob=-0.53, compression_ratio=0.91`. The existing `NO_SPEECH_DROP` gate can't catch it (no_speech_prob is 0), the exact-match `HALLUCINATIONS` blacklist can't enumerate named credits, and the hardcoded `len(pcm) < SR * 0.3` floor missed it by 13 ms.

## Three guards (all live-reloadable)

1. **Configurable minimum recording duration** — new setting `min_record_seconds` (env `VOICEPI_MIN_RECORD_SECONDS`, default `0.5`). `_should_skip_pcm` uses `max(0.3, min_record_seconds)` so 0.3 s remains the absolute misfire floor even if a user sets 0. Cached in `__init__`, refreshed in `_apply_runtime_module_config` (mirrors `parakeet_min_seconds`).

2. **Pattern-based subtitle-credit filter** — `is_hallucination` keeps the exact-match set and adds a conservative **anchored** full-text regex for credit shapes: `(danske|norske|svenske)? (under)?tekster af/by/:`, `tekstet af`, `oversat af`, `subtitles/subtitled/captions/translated by`, plus bare company credits (`scandinavian text service`, `broadcast text international`, `dansk video tekst`), each tolerating a trailing year. Anchored only — a real dictation merely *containing* "tekster af" mid-sentence is **not** dropped.

3. **Speech-rate plausibility gate** — new setting `max_chars_per_second` (env `VOICEPI_MAX_CHARS_PER_SECOND`, default `30`, `0` disables). After text assembly in `_transcribe_detail`, if `len(text)/max(duration,0.1)` exceeds the threshold the transcript is dropped (same downstream empty-result path as an `is_hallucination` match), logging:
   `[stt] dropped: {chars} chars in {dur:.1f}s = {rate:.0f} chars/s > {threshold} (hallucination guard)`. Real speech is 15-25 chars/s; the default 30 leaves headroom.

## Settings wired end-to-end

`settings_schema.json` (both `live:true`) → Rust `AppSettings` (struct + Default + load + save + `keys.rs` `SETTINGS_KEYS` + `validate.rs`) → `settings_reset_tests` exhaustive literal + Quality reset group → Quality-tab UI rows with hover help → `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (Quality table + env reference rows).

## Tests

- Repro string at 0.31 s dropped by **both** the pattern filter and the rate gate independently.
- Anchored-pattern negatives: long real sentences containing "tekster af" / "oversat af" / "subtitles by" / "scandinavian text service" mid-sentence survive; `Undertekster af Jesper Buhl` full-match dies.
- Rate gate: 60 chars / 0.31 s dies, 8 chars / 0.5 s survives, threshold `0` disables.
- `min_record_seconds`: 0.45 s clip dropped at default 0.5, passes at 0.3; floor clamps below 0.3 (0.25 s dies, 0.35 s survives even at setting 0).
- Live-reload of both settings via `_apply_runtime_module_config`.

## Verification

- Python: `584 passed, 10 subtests passed`
- Rust (dev container): `cargo fmt` clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean, `cargo test` → `271 passed; 0 failed` (+ integration/doctest buckets all green)

author: gabe3laka
body:
## Root cause (debugged from the code, matches the phone symptoms)

The fingertip label said **"pinch to grab" in every phase** — including `idle`, where **no Build region exists**. The user pinched the **detected** boxes (EdgeCrafter entities / HSE live boxes), but extraction only listened on `build.region`, which is only created via the manual Select-object drag. So the pinch worked, the hit-test worked… on nothing. Secondary bug: a fast pinch right after selection could race the async session bootstrap (`captureKeyframe` saw a null session → silent-ish failure).

## Fixes

**1. Pinch a detected box → extract (preferred behaviour, spec §2).** In Build `idle`, a pinch inside any live detection box auto-converts it to a Build region and extracts in one motion:
- `findDetectionAtPointer()` — smallest containing box wins (most specific object); candidates = `backendEntities` + `liveBoxes` (both already card-normalized, verified).
- `detectionBoxToRegion()` — clamps into the card, expands tiny boxes around their centre to a workable size.
- `lockAndExtract()` — lock → extract chained deterministically via a new `go()` phase helper that updates `phaseRef` **synchronously** with `setPhase` (the chain never reads a stale phase); the session bootstrap is held in `sessionReadyRef` and `extractBlueprint()` awaits it (race killed).
- Manual Select-object drag unchanged.

**2. Nothing fails silently (spec §1/§4).** New `extractStatus` (`idle / extract_requested / capture_failed / frame_received / placing_started`) + a TEMP debug readout on the Build panel: `phase · region/base/ghost yes/no · extract status · pinch ON/off · inside yes/no · pointer x,y`. Capture failure shows *"capture failed — try reselecting the object"* and the box stays pinchable.

**3. Visible ghost guaranteed (spec §5/§6/§8).**
- **"✓ Blueprint extracted"** flash when placing begins.
- Amber **"BLUEPRINT SHELL — waiting for frame…"** fallback whenever a ghost exists without a frame.

## Gateway isolation redesign — lean recovery (Plan B, part 2)
Replaces the reactive IB-Gateway watchdog **pile** (5-min probe + restart loop + cooldown + max-restarts + exhaustion re-arm) with **one deterministic daily restart** + an **alert-only** daily health-check. This is the "small / reliable / lean — no band-aids" half of the gateway-isolation directive; the VM tooling is in #3270.

### Changes
- **`deploy/ict-ib-gateway-reset.{service,timer}`** (new) — one `docker restart ib-gateway` per day at **05:30 UTC** (just after IBKR's overnight reset + the image's 23:59 UTC IBC auto-restart), the deterministic recovery for the single known failure (in-place re-login wedging on the reset). Gated to the gateway VM via `ConditionPathExists=/etc/ict/ib-gateway-docker.env`, so it's **inert on the trader's micro** once the gateway moves off it.
- **`ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.{service,timer}`** → **alert-only + daily** (06:00 UTC). Dropped `--auto-restart` + all restart-loop flags from `ExecStart`; cadence 5min → daily. Probes `ib_paper` across the network and Telegrams only if MES is dark — no mutation.
- **`ib-integration.md`** — new "Gateway isolation redesign" section (topology: gateway on its own 1-OCPU Ampere VM, trader reaches it over the network, thin trader-side connect breaker stays); supersedes the reactive-watchdog description (kept as history).

### Unchanged on purpose
- The trader-side connect breaker (`IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` / `IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S`) — a gateway/network blip still never blocks the BTCUSDT loop.
- `check_ib_gateway.py` keeps its restart code only as the **manual** `vm-ib-gateway-recover` path (no longer wired into a scheduled loop). A follow-up can strip the now-unused restart machinery + its test.

### Still pending (flagged, not in this PR)

- Execution: terminate candidate → provision gateway VM (#3270 tooling) → `provision-ib-gateway` (**needs your IBKR Mobile 2FA tap**) → wire `ib_paper.ib_host` to the gateway's private IP → remove gateway from micro → measure micro load.

## 问题
新建 WireGuard(oss 家族)通道卡在「待登录」、隧道延迟「—」、容器反复重启,连不通。

author: davenger
body:
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106020

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required)

Since the stateless worker endpoint and streaming exchange server were enabled in every stateless CI run, sanitizer jobs idle closer to their memory cap and OOM more often. The infrastructure retains idle threads for the server's lifetime, and under ASan each parked thread is expensive (instrumented stack pages, fake stack, allocator cache, shadow memory), none of it visible to the memory tracker.

Three sources of retained threads, addressed individually:
- `StatelessTaskExecutor` kept up to 100 idle pool threads (observed: 35 parked for the whole run at ~0.1% utilization). The pool parameters are now configurable via `stateless_worker_server.max_threads/max_free_threads/queue_size`, and idle threads are not retained by default. Since `ThreadPool` spawns threads on demand, this has no startup or steady-state cost.
- The `ExchangeServer` handshake pool kept 8 idle threads; handshakes are short-lived, so it now retains none.
- The global thread pool only trims when idle threads exceed `max_thread_pool_free_size` (default 1000). Idle counts in stateless runs peak at ~400-500, so the pool never shrank and every concurrency burst permanently ratcheted up the thread count and resident stack memory. Sanitizer test configs now set the threshold to 128.

Verified locally: after running the `03394_distributed_*` worker-path tests, `StatelessWorkerThreads` and `ExchangeServerThreads` drain to 0 instead of parking at their high-water marks.

author: kcirred
body:
Lowers tt.reshape to tensor.reshape, fed by either tensor.from_elements 
(when the target shape is built from SSA values) or a folded arith.constant 
of the form dense<[16, 32]> : tensor<2xindex>. The interpreter previously
supported none of these, so any reshape-bearing kernel failed at parse
or execution time.

- Add tensor.reshape executor + parsers (regex and MLIR-frontend).
  Target shape is read from the result-type annotation rather than the
  runtime shape operand, matching how tensor.expand_shape and
  tensor.collapse_shape already work — the result type always pins the
  target shape statically, even when the operand is dynamic.
- Add tensor.from_elements executor + parsers, since it is the typical
  shape-operand producer for tensor.reshape.
- Extend arith.constant to handle non-splat dense<[...]> payloads. The
  splat path was the only one implemented, which silently mis-parsed
  list payloads to a splat-of-zero tensor. A new dense_list attribute
  routes the executor to materialize the array element-by-element.
  Covers both the regex parser and the MLIR-frontend adapter.

Tests pin the regression cases and exercise rank-changing reshapes
(1D->2D, 2D->1D, 1D->3D), the smallest legal tensor.from_elements
(N=1), an N>2 case, dtype generality of the dense-list path (index
and f32), and the size-mismatch error path.

The page that turns Trust Check scores from "a number on a website" into something other systems can cite and depend on. Moody's doesn't just publish ratings; they publish methodology. Now so do we.

author: emansyl
body:
`/code-review` follow-up to PR 2b (#298). The finding landed on `main` unfixed.

## The bug (latent)
`calculateFeesCents` rounds the total **once**; `getFeeBreakdownCents` rounded **base and tax independently** → the breakdown's `totalCents` could differ from the charged fee by **1¢** for some prices:
- `priceCents = 8` → charged **58**, breakdown total **59** (`round(50.64)=51` + `round(7.65)=8`).

Latent today (`getFeeBreakdownCents` has no live consumer — checkout charges via `calculateFeesCents`), but both are exported from `@troptix/api/server`, so a fee-breakdown display would mismatch the charge.

## Fix
`getFeeBreakdownCents` now derives `totalCents` from `calculateFeesCents` (authoritative charge) and sets `taxCents = total − round(base)`, so **base + tax always equals the charged total**. The charge is unchanged; only the breakdown's tax/total are made consistent.

## Validation
- ✅ 15 unit tests pass — incl. a new invariant `getFeeBreakdownCents(p).totalCents === calculateFeesCents(p)` over the previously-divergent prices (1, 8, 78, 85, 155, 169, …)
- ✅ typecheck green

Closes a gap surfaced during review: the current-state ingestion routes did **not** run the platform's sensitive-data quarantine, unlike every other upload route. A client uploading PHI/PII/regulated data **by mistake** through the current-state panel would have had it parsed and landed `review_required` — or **auto-committed** for a clean KPI table — with no automated scan.

Wire the existing, tested `evaluateSensitiveUpload` guard (audit B5a/B5c) into both current-state routes, **before** parse / evidence write / auto-promotion — the same ~5-line pattern used by `programs/workspace/[moveId]/upload`, `nexus/upload`, `tower/upload`, `data/upload`, and the admin import routes.

Declared `phi` classification, or detected SSN / MRN-patient-id / DOB / routing-account / card / email / phone patterns → quarantine. Conservative pre-ingest filter, not full DLP (see Known Gaps in the release record).

author: atbagan
body:
## Feature 2.3 — management-cluster GitOps lifecycle CLI

Maps to the **management scope** (console Feature #4). Closes the CLI/console
gap for management-cluster GitOps: the console exposes both read and lifecycle
operations on the management cluster; `butleradm gitops` now matches it.

### What

Six verbs under `butleradm gitops`, full console parity for the management scope:

| Verb | Endpoint | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `GET /api/management/gitops/status` | read |
| `discover` | `GET /api/management/gitops/discover` | read |
| `preview` | `POST /api/management/gitops/preview-cluster` | read/safe |
| `export` | `POST /api/management/gitops/export-cluster` | read/safe (writes to a Git repo, not the cluster) |
| `enable` | `POST /api/management/gitops/enable` | mutating |
| `disable` | `DELETE /api/management/gitops` | mutating (highest blast radius) |

Thin HTTP clients over `internal/common/serverhttp`; orchestration stays in
butler-server (ADR-016). Management endpoints carry no `{namespace}/{name}` —
the single well-known cluster is resolved server-side.

### The disable guard (load-bearing)

Management `disable` is `bootstrapper.Uninstall` against the **platform's own
Flux** — categorically worse than tenant disable. It manages butler-controller,
butler-console and the ImageUpdateAutomation that deploys releases.

- **No `--yes` path.** Proceeds only on the exact typed phrase
  `uninstall-management-flux` (via `--confirm` or interactive prompt), so
  habituated `--yes` muscle memory cannot fire it.
- The help and interactive prompt state plainly **what** it tears down.
- The refuse-path is **mutation-checked**: replacing the guard with an
  always-pass body fails the `yes` / cluster-name / empty / wrong-token cases,
  proving the test is non-vacuous.

`enable` carries a standard re-bootstrap confirmation (`--yes` or typed `yes`).

### Tests

- Read verbs: request building + output formatting (non-vacuous).
- `validateRepoFullName` (owner/repo contract; rejects URLs/ssh).
- Both confirm guards, including the disable refuse-path.
- `go build` (both binaries) + `go vet` + `go test ./internal/adm/gitops/` green.

### Validation status

- **Read verbs (status / discover / preview / export): live-validated** against
  butler-beta management (see E2E notes on the follow-up comment).
- **enable / disable: implemented + unit-tested, LIVE-VALIDATION-DEFERRED.**
  These were deliberately NOT run against butler-beta management — enabling or
  disabling Flux on the live management cluster would re-point or tear down the
  platform's own GitOps. They ship covered by unit tests (request shape, error
  handling, confirm guards) only.

Part of the CLI/console parity effort.

body:
Fixes #84 (Wave 1 of the Android product-review roadmap #101 — sequenced first: it gates every schema-touching issue).

## What changed
- **Migrations, never wipes**: `exportSchema = true` + KSP `room.schemaLocation`, the **v4 schema JSON committed** under `app/schemas/`, and `fallbackToDestructiveMigration()` **gone from the build path entirely** — a missing migration now fails loudly in development instead of silently erasing the user's data in production. `room-testing` wired (catalog + androidTest assets); `MigrationBaselineTest` proves v4 data opens intact under the current no-fallback builder and is the scaffold every future bump extends (the literal v4→v5 auto-migration test lands with the first real v5 bump — #87/#92 — which this PR makes safe and testable; stated honestly against the AC).
- **One-file backup/restore, schema-agnostically**: `SnappetBackup` (pure, JVM-tested codec) encodes a versioned JSON of column→value row maps read at the **SQLite level**; `SnappetBackupManager` walks `sqlite_master` for user tables — `SELECT *` on export, **transactional all-or-nothing** delete+insert on import. A new `@Entity` is covered with zero backup changes (17 per-entity DTOs would drift). Import is **strict same-schema-version** — never a best-effort restore of money/health data; cross-version restore is the migration pipeline's job.
- **UI**: `BackupScreen` — Export via SAF `CreateDocument` (dated filename), Import via `OpenDocument` behind a replace-everything confirmation — reached from a **Backup & restore** action on the App Library top bar (the Kilter catalog SAF pattern). Doubles as phone-to-phone migration for a no-account app.

## Verification
- JVM: `SnappetBackupTest` 4/4 (storage-class fidelity incl. Long/Double/null/BLOB, foreign-file rejection, cross-version rejection with readable guidance).
- Emulator (Pixel 7 AVD, via direct `adb shell am instrument` — Gradle's connected task wedges on this iCloud Desktop, see decisions.md): **full instrumented suite 36/36**, including new `BackupRoundTripTest` (export → wipe → import → identical reads across modules, and re-export equals the original export) and `MigrationBaselineTest`.
- `:app:assembleDebug` + `:app:testDebugUnitTest` green.

PDD prompt: `pdd/prompts/features/38-android-room-migrations-backup.md`; decisions.md records the reversal of the destructive-fallback norm; knowledge graph gains the `android-backup` surface.

author: thomvaill
body:
## Add `none` option for `systemModel`

### Context

In the Backstage [descriptor format](https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/descriptor-format), `spec.system` on a Component is **optional**. Today the
kubernetes-ingestor always assigns a system (and auto-creates the corresponding `System` entity) based on `systemModel` (`namespace` / `cluster` / `cluster-namespace` / `default`).

In some setups we simply don't want a default system attached to ingested components — only an explicit one when the resource asks for it.

### Change

Adds a new `systemModel: none` option:

- **No `terasky.backstage.io/system` annotation** → the component is ingested **without** `spec.system`, and **no `System` entity is auto-created**.
- **Explicit `terasky.backstage.io/system` annotation** → that value is used as `spec.system`; still no `System` entity is auto-created (it's assumed managed elsewhere).

* **New Features**

* **Documentation**
  * Backend docs updated to show `systemModel: 'none'` and per-mapping placement.

author: kanggle
body:
**Root cause** (pinned by TASK-MONO-210 federation-e2e log dump; also the root of TASK-MONO-207 spec flakiness): `OutboxPublisher.publishPendingEvents` is `@Transactional` at the default **REPEATABLE READ** and acquires a `FOR UPDATE` lock via `findPendingWithLock` (`SELECT … WHERE status='PENDING' … FOR UPDATE`), then does a synchronous blocking `kafkaTemplate.send(...).get()` **while holding that lock**. Under RR the `FOR UPDATE` takes next-key/gap locks over the PENDING range → a slow/warming Kafka makes the poller block concurrent business `INSERT`s into `outbox` for up to `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` (50s → `1205` → `PessimisticLockingFailureException` → the business write **500s**).

**Fix**: `@Transactional(isolation = READ_COMMITTED)`. RC drops gap locking (only matched rows locked, never gaps) → business INSERTs proceed while the poller publishes; a slow Kafka now only degrades poller throughput (intended degrade mode).

**Semantics preserved** (no consumer-visible change): `FOR UPDATE` still row-locks claimed rows (single-poller exclusivity / no double-publish); at-least-once + FIFO (`ORDER BY created_at`) intact; batch read-once-then-write so RC's weaker repeatable-read is irrelevant; § 4.6 batch-resilience dispatch byte-unchanged.

**Scope**: shared `libs/java-messaging` (applies to all services' outbox uniformly; isolation-scoped to the poll tx only — business tx isolation unchanged). No per-service adaptation needed (backward-compatible). Amends **ADR-MONO-004 § 4.7** (rationale + semantics analysis + deferred alternatives: claim-then-publish, SKIP LOCKED). Defensive reflection test guards the isolation. `:libs:java-messaging:test` green.

**Behavioural proof**: federation-hardening-e2e workflow (MONO-207 + MONO-210 specs without lock-wait 500) — to run post-merge.

按既定十项意见逐项落地，每项独立成提交（共 11 个提交），全部测试通过。

## 新功能（2D 地图）

1. **🎨 国别染色（choropleth）**：按当前筛选聚合每国投资/装机整国填色（√ 压缩 + 92 分位归一，热力同款渐变），悬浮看汇总、点国家开国别下钻；`lib/world-110m.js` 首次开启才懒加载。新增 `util.geoNameOf`（中文国名→Natural-Earth-110m 要素名，11 处叫法修正 + 微型经济体显式跳过），进校验器（5h）与单测。
2. **搜索升级**：拼音全拼（`shate`）/ 首字母（`st`）/ 多词 AND（"沙特 储能"）；字表由 `scripts/build-pinyin.js` 生成（构建期用 pinyin-pro，运行时零依赖，17KB），搜索索引按项目缓存，消掉每次按键重拼 3400 个串的旧开销；校验器新增缺字提醒（5g）。
3. **📖 导览/故事模式**：5 条剧本（沙特2030 / AI数据中心竞赛 / 非洲资源走廊 / 中国企业出海 / 核电复兴）共 41 站，全部绑定真实项目 id（校验器 5i ERROR 级把关）；逐站飞行 + 详情卡 + 底部解说条 + 自动播放；`#story=…&stop=…` 深链打开即播。
4. **⭐ 我的关注**：详情卡 ☆ 收藏 → 左栏一键只看收藏（与其他筛选正交、`fav=1` 入分享链接），⤓/⤒ JSON 备份恢复跨设备；收藏筛选下 CSV 导出即收藏清单。
5. **📈 趋势统计**：年度投资额（柱）+ 项目数（折线）SVG 图 + 大区×品类矩阵热格（数字=项目数、色深=投资额），点格子直接筛选地图；投资沿用 KPI 的国际大客户排除口径。

## 陪练与无障碍

6. **陪练档案备份/迁移**：存档加 `ver`（PROG_VER=2），读档统一走 `migrateProgress`（旧档/脏数据归一，不丢 XP/徽章/错题本）；成长档案新增「⤓ 备份 / ⤒ 恢复」JSON（绝不含 AI Key）。

## 工程化

8. **CI 扩容**（零依赖）：数据新鲜度告警（>2 月 warning）、体积预算（单 data 文件 600KB / 首屏 6.5MB，当前 3.29MB）、链接检查（站内缺失=ERROR，外链探活仅警告）、Lighthouse 趋势 job（性能≥60 / 无障碍≥90 警告线，`continue-on-error`）。

body: Based on https://project-simple-paratext-3-latest-935.magicpatterns.app/ # Code Review Summary **Branch**: `ai/feature/user-profile-popover-tj-06-09-2026` **Base**: `origin/main` **Date**: 2026-06-10 **Review model**: Claude Opus 4.7 **Files changed**: 6 ## Overview Consolidates the standalone theme toggle, Paratext registration button, and internet settings button from the toolbar into a single `UserProfilePopover` triggered from a user-profile icon at the top-right. The popover also introduces a Simple/Power **interface mode switcher**. Discovered during review that the existing dock-layout machinery in `web-view.service-host.ts` did not actually respond to runtime mode changes — the comment in `loadLayout` flatly said no user-facing switcher existed — so the review extended the scope to make the mode switch work live (subscribe to `platform.interfaceMode`, reload the layout on change, and stop simple-mode resizes from clobbering the saved power-mode layout in `localStorage`). The popover ships with comprehensive unit tests (19 cases covering trigger/open, header skeleton + 3 registration states, mode toggle, action rows, language picker including sort order, and appearance toggling), an updated toolbar test that stubs the popover at the boundary, parallel en/es localization, and a new `useInterfaceMode` hook that returns `[mode, setMode]` with a `'simple'` fallback (sibling to the existing read-only `useIsPowerMode`). ## API Changes None. No public API surfaces (`lib/platform-bible-react/`, `lib/platform-bible-utils/`, `@papi/` modules in `papi.d.ts`, or extensions' type declaration files) were modified. All changes are internal to `src/renderer/` plus additions to `assets/localization/{en,es}.json`. The new `useInterfaceMode` hook is renderer-internal. ## Findings ### Critical — Must address before merge None. ### Important — Should address before merge - [x] **Runtime mode switch was silently a no-op until restart** _(fixed during review: rewrote the `loadLayout` / `saveLayout` / `registerDockLayout` flow in `src/renderer/services/web-view.service-host.ts`. `loadLayout` is now invoked both at startup and again whenever `platform.interfaceMode` changes. `saveLayout` is now a no-op in simple mode so simple-mode resizes never clobber the saved power-mode layout in `DOCK_LAYOUT_KEY`. `registerDockLayout` subscribes to `platform.interfaceMode` with `retrieveDataImmediately: false`; the unregister callback tears the subscription down. Race-safe cleanup: an `unsubscribeRequested` flag handles the case where unregister fires before `subscribe` resolves. Promise chains replaced with named async helpers + `try/catch` per the author's preference. The stale comment was replaced with one that describes the new behavior.)_ - [x] **Local `RegistrationData` type duplicated extension shape** _(fixed during review: dropped the local declaration and `import type { RegistrationData } from 'paratext-registration'` instead — the same type the command's `CommandHandlers` entry references.)_ - [ ] ~~Popover refetches `getParatextRegistrationData` on every open~~ _(Dismissed by author: intentional. The data doesn't change until restart today, but the popover is forward-prepared for future live-update support.)_ - [x] **Inline `style={{ fontSize: ... }}` and Tailwind workaround comments** _(fixed during review: confirmed Tailwind is not running on core renderer — the root `tailwind.config.ts` is Storybook-only, and the renderer webpack config has no postcss/tailwind loaders. Replaced all five inline `style={{ fontSize: 'Npx' }}` props with classes defined in a new colocated `user-profile-popover.component.css` (mirroring the `web-view.component.css` / `platform-panel.component.css` pattern). The `tw:data-[state=on]:` workaround comment was removed.)_ - [x] **`useIsPowerMode` read/setter duplication** _(fixed during review: added a sibling `useInterfaceMode()` hook in `src/renderer/hooks/use-interface-mode.hook.ts` that returns `[mode: 'simple' | 'power', setMode]` with the same `'simple'` fallback policy. Popover now consumes it instead of re-implementing the read inline. Left `useIsPowerMode` alone per author's request to keep it simple.)_ - [x] **`DEFAULT_THEME_VALUE` JSDoc referenced the deleted toolbar copy** _(fixed during review: reworded the JSDoc to drop the "mirroring `platform-bible-toolbar.tsx`" reference, name the only field actually read (`theme.type`) and the `isPlatformError` gate, and explain the localize-key reuse without misleading reference-equality framing. Left the value local to the file per author's call.)_ - [ ] ~~`LOCALIZED_STRING_KEYS` passed without `useMemo`~~ _(Dismissed by author: module-level const has a stable reference; `useMemo` is unnecessary.)_ - [x] **Icon-only trigger missing a tooltip** _(fixed during review: wrapped the `PopoverTrigger` in `TooltipProvider` → `Tooltip` → `TooltipTrigger asChild`, matching the existing toolbar Home/Sync tooltip pattern. Tooltip content uses `%toolbar_userProfile_label%`. Added a `TOOLTIP_DELAY = 300` constant mirroring the toolbar value. Added a ResizeObserver no-op stub to the test (Radix Tooltip uses it internally and jsdom doesn't provide it), matching the pattern in `overlay-popover.component.test.tsx`.)_ - [x] **English strings violated sentence case** _(fixed during review: see "Sentence-case changes" section below for the exact strings. The author asked to flag this explicitly so they can confirm with UX, since the original design comp had these in title case — possibly intentional, possibly not.)_ ### Minor — Consider - [ ] ~~`%toolbar_theme_loading%` key reused for never-displayed sentinel label~~ _(Dismissed: already partly addressed via the JSDoc rewording above. The label is never displayed; visible-impact risk if the key is removed in the future is zero.)_ - [x] **`useData` generic dropped** _(fixed during review: restored the explicit generic on both `CurrentTheme` and `ShouldMatchSystem` calls. Downstream impact verified — typecheck and the 33 unit tests stay clean.)_ - [x] **`sendCommand(...).catch(...)` promise chain in handlers** _(fixed during review: converted `handleProfileAndRegistration` and `handleNetworkSettings` to `async` handlers with `try/catch`. author: farost
body:
## Product change and motivation

Add an additional API to the diagnostics manager to let the extensions of TypeDB insert their own metrics in the monitoring reports (both Prometheus and JSON). This way, libraries on top of `typedb` create can use the monitoring endpoint, combining typedb default metrics and any additional information they need on the page.

### Extension examples

**Prometheus** (just appending additional lines to the end with no extra markers)
```
# distribution: TypeDB
# version: 3.10.0-alpha-1
# os: Darwin arm64 15.7.3

# HELP typedb_build_info Build and runtime identity of this TypeDB server.
# TYPE typedb_build_info gauge
typedb_build_info{version="3.10.0-alpha-1", distribution="TypeDB", os_name="Darwin", os_arch="arm64", os_version="15.7.3"} 1

....

# HELP typedb_wal_fsync_duration_seconds WAL fsync latency.
# TYPE typedb_wal_fsync_duration_seconds histogram

# HELP raft_apply_total Number of committed entries applied to the state machine.
# TYPE raft_apply_total counter
raft_apply_total 0

# HELP raft_messages_sent_total Outbound raft messages sent.
# TYPE raft_messages_sent_total counter
raft_messages_sent_total 0
```

**json** (introduce an extra `extensions` key for every registered extension to avoid conflicts with already existing keys)
```json
{
  "actions": [],
  "deploymentID": "test",
  "distribution": "TypeDB",
  "errors": [],
  "extensions": {
    "raft": {
      "counters": {
        "apply_total": 0,
        "messages_sent_total": 0,
      },
      }
    }
  },
  ...
```

## Implementation

Previously `Diagnostics` directly owned every metric the server reported. This PR splits that into a built-in core plus a pluggable extension list:

- TypeDB's own metrics state (`server_properties`, `server_metrics`, load/action/error/histogram maps) moves out of `Diagnostics` into a new `TypeDBMetrics` struct in `metrics/typedb_metrics.rs`. `Diagnostics` now holds a `TypeDBMetrics` and a `RwLock<Vec<Arc<dyn MonitoringSection>>>` of extensions; all built-in `submit_*` / `observe_*` methods forward to the inner struct.
- A new `MonitoringSection` trait (`reports/monitoring_section.rs`) is the extension interface: a stable `name()` (used as both the dedup key on registration and the JSON section key) plus `write_prometheus` and `write_json` for the two scrape formats. `register_monitoring_extension` deduplicates by name, silently replacing on collision; `has_monitoring_extension(name)` lets callers detect the collision before registering and warn.
- `to_monitoring_prometheus` / `to_monitoring_json` render the TypeDB core first, then append each registered extension (JSON extensions nested under an `extensions` object keyed by `name()`). The PostHog reporting path is deliberately untouched.
- `DiagnosticsManager` gains `register_metrics` / `has_metrics` as the public facade for the two new methods, matching the existing wrapper style.

author: chromium-wpt-export-bot
body:
For subgrids whose final position isn't known at sizing time (e.g.
inside a grid-lanes ancestor that places after sizing), the accumulated
edge extra margins propagated to a nested subgrid must account for the
largest contribution the subgrid could pick up at any candidate
position. Previously we only forwarded the parent's accumulated edge
margins, which under-reserved space when a parent gap could land
immediately outside the subgrid's boundary.

Update `CreateSubgridTrackCollection` so that when the subgrid is
auto-placed in its parent, the start/end accumulated extra margins are
computed as follows:

 - If the subgrid spans every track of the parent, no parent gap can
 ever be adjacent to the subgrid's boundary; forward the parent's
 accumulated edge margins as-is.
 - If the parent has exactly one more track than the subgrid, the
 subgrid can only ever have a parent gap on one side. Reserve the
 half-gutter contribution on whichever side currently carries the
 smaller accumulated edge margin so we don't double-count.
 - Otherwise, take max(accumulated edge margin, parent gutter delta /
 2) on both sides, since any combination of start/end positions is
 possible.

Add a bit more test coverage, although a follow up change will be needed
to get the true largest final accumulation numbers, which will be
handled in a follow up change and will likely lead to some changes to
existing test expectations in some cases.

author: carreau
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the backend against cheating and improves security by implementing server-side replay verification of win submissions and hashing bearer tokens at rest. It also adds comprehensive input validation, fixes rate-limiting logic, and improves error handling for malformed requests.

## Key Changes

**Win Verification & Replay:**
- Implement `replayMoves()` in `catalog-solve.mjs` to deterministically replay recorded R/L/U/D move sequences against the server's own copy of a puzzle board, verifying that the sequence is legal, ends in a solved state, and its paid roll count matches the claimed `movesUsed` exactly
- Export `solutionCodes()` to render the stored solution as a full replayable code string (cursor walks + rolls), enabling the test suite and admin tools to generate valid win sequences
- Update `PATCH /api/attempts` to require and validate `moveSeq` for all wins; reject wins that don't replay to a solved board or whose move count doesn't match the sequence
- Remove the client-supplied `optimal` parameter from `POST /api/attempts` (was a poisoning vector); seed `optimal` from the puzzle's scramble length instead, and only lower it via validated wins or the solver

**Token Security:**
- Hash all bearer tokens at rest using SHA-256 (stored as `sha256:<base64url>` in the DB)
- Mint fresh tokens on every password/passkey login via new `rotateToken()` method; a leaked token no longer survives a password reset
- Add one-time migration to hash legacy plaintext tokens in existing DBs (deterministic so sessions stay valid)
- Update `userByToken()` to hash the presented token before lookup

**Input Validation & Error Handling:**
- Add `httpError()` helper to map client faults to specific HTTP statuses (400/413) instead of 500 or connection resets
- Validate usernames against control characters and bidi-override characters (`\u0000-\u001f`, `\u007f-\u009f`, `\u200e-\u202e`, `\u2066-\u2069`) that can spoof rendered text on leaderboards
- Improve `readJson()` to reject oversized bodies with 413 and malformed JSON with 400, keeping the socket alive so the client receives the status
- Cap `movesUsed` and `durationMs` to sane ranges (4096 rolls, 7 days) to prevent bogus submissions from skewing difficulty aggregates
- Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` header to all JSON and static responses

**Rate Limiting & Reliability:**
- Fix `clientIp()` to use `lastForwarded()` for X-Forwarded-For (the last entry is the only trustworthy one when multiple proxies append); use `firstForwarded()` for X-Forwarded-Host/Proto (which are replaced, not appended)
- Add rate-limit buckets to `POST /api/attempts` and `PATCH /api/attempts/:id` (60 per minute per IP)
- Add hard timeout (5 minutes) on solver worker to prevent pathological boards from burning CPU cores forever
- Add 10-second timeout to all client-side API requests via `AbortSignal.timeout()` so cold-start fallback works even if the server is half-dead

**Test & Game Updates:**
- Rewrite `test/api.mjs` to use real winning sequences (puzzle solutions padded with "wiggles" for varied scores) instead of arbitrary move counts
- Add tests for malformed/oversized request bodies, bidi-override characters in usernames, and win replay verification
- Update `src/main.js` to remember the generator's opening cursor (`initialSelected`) so Retry restores the correct start position for server replay verification
- Pass `targetColor` to `greedySolve()` so the solver doesn't "improve" a solution into one that solves to the wrong uniform colour
- Add `esc()` call in the "Solved!" overlay to prevent puzzle names from breaking HTML rendering
- Add timeout and keepalive options to client-side API requests

## Notable Implementation Details

- The `replayMoves()` function mirrors the game's input rules exactly: arrows toward

author: mcereal
body:
## Summary
- Diagnoses and closes the ~29MB/file warm `sfn check` memory growth from #1247: the leak is **not** in the per-file loop — the Phase 5a arena rewind works exactly as designed (instrumented marks show every `post_rewind` cursor returning to the loop mark). The linear term is **pre-mark**: `_cr_resolve_and_dedupe` ran the relative-import BFS once per entry, and each walk re-read + re-scanned every source in that entry's import closure.
- Fix: a `RelativeScanMemo` threaded across all entries of one resolution pass — each unique source is read + scanned at most once, and each unique dep's `CapsuleSource` (slug / workspace-member canonicalization) is computed once. Output is byte-identical (each entry keeps its own BFS + visited set).
- Adds a memory-bound e2e regression test that fails on the pre-fix seed binary (+61 arena pages) and passes post-fix (+0 pages).
- Rider (requested in-session, part of #843 Track A): `TEST_JOBS ?= 1` Makefile knob threading the runner's existing `--jobs N` (#1236) into every `make test*` target. Default 1 (RAM-budget call stays with the caller); `make test TEST_JOBS=4` halves the integration suite locally (67s → 34s warm). CI sharding unaffected.

Closes #1247

## Root cause (mechanism + file)
`compiler/src/capsule_resolver.sfn`: `_cr_resolve_and_dedupe` calls `enumerate_relative_sources(entry, members)` once **per entry path**. Each call BFS-walks the entry's whole import closure, calling `fs.readFile` + `collect_relative_import_specs` on every reachable module. The scanner's helpers are allocation-heavy — `_cr_byte_at` allocates a fresh 1-char string per source byte (~21B of arena garbage per scanned byte, measured) and `_cr_word_matches` allocates two substrings per scanned position. For `sfn check compiler/src/` that is 158 entries × ~100-module closures ≈ 15k full-source scans ≈ **4.0GB of arena allocations, all before `cli_check.sfn` takes its Phase 5a loop mark** — so the per-file rewind can never reclaim them. Arena-cursor traces (mark = `(page_index << 32) | used`):

| phase | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| post_resolve | page 1002 (~4008MB) | page 87 (~348MB) |
| post_load | +34 pages (136MB) | +34 pages (136MB) |
| per-file rewind | restores exactly | restores exactly |
| pages at exit | 1074 (4296MB) | 160 (640MB) |

Hypotheses (a) malloc-path helpers and (b) pre-mark structure mutation from the issue were ruled out: `--json` (no-rewind) vs default runs showed the rewind reclaiming ~1.2GB, and exit-time `used` (allocations below the mark) was the term growing linearly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Warm whole-tree `check compiler/src/` peak RSS ≤ ~(single-file peak + 2GB): **732MB** peak (was 4483MB)
- [x] Peak RSS not linear in file count: 40-file = 538MB vs 158-file = 732MB (~1.6MB/file residual = union-closure + per-file scratch; was ~29MB/file)
- [x] Diagnostics/output byte-identical: full-tree stdout + stderr diffed clean against pre-fix run
- [x] Root cause documented (above)
- [x] Memory-bound regression test: `compiler/tests/e2e/test_check_resolver_scan_memo.sh` (fails on pre-fix seed: +61 pages; passes post-fix: +0)
- [x] `make compile` passes (self-host); `make test` green on the fixed binary: unit 146/146, integration 32/32, e2e 5/5, capsules 34/34, e2e-sh 111/111 (an earlier exit-139 did not reproduce — it occurred while the suite shared a 4-vCPU container with concurrent 4.5GB pre-fix benchmark runs)
- [x] `sfn fmt --check` clean on touched files

## Verification
```bash
make compile                                              # self-hosts: pass
SAILFIN_DUMP_ARENA_STATS=1 sailfin check compiler/src/    # warm tree
#   before: pages=1074 capacity=4296MB  peak_rss=4483MB  wall=201s
#   after:  pages=160  capacity=640MB   peak_rss=732MB   wall=53s
sailfin check $(ls compiler/src/*.sfn | head -40)         # sub-linearity probe
#   after:  pages=126  peak_rss=538MB
bash compiler/tests/e2e/test_check_resolver_scan_memo.sh build/seed/bin/sailfin   # pre-fix: FAIL (+61 pages)
bash compiler/tests/e2e/test_check_resolver_scan_memo.sh build/native/sailfin    # post-fix: PASS (+0 pages)
make test                                                 # full suite green (see above)
make test-integration && make test-integration TEST_JOBS=4   # knob smoke: pass / pass (67s -> 34s)
```

## Files Changed
- `compiler/src/capsule_resolver.sfn` — `RelativeScanMemo` + memoized BFS core (`_cr_enumerate_relative_sources_memo`); `enumerate_relative_sources` kept as a thin fresh-memo wrapper; memo threaded in `_cr_resolve_and_dedupe`
- `compiler/tests/e2e/test_check_resolver_scan_memo.sh` — memory-bound regression test (new)
- `Makefile` — `TEST_JOBS` knob threading `--jobs` into the `make test*` targets (#843 Track A rider)

Pre-commit review (code-reviewer): approved, no blocking findings; aliasing of memoized `CapsuleSource` values is read-only downstream (the post-dedupe `ll_path` fill constructs new structs). Copilot review nits addressed in 97e597a.

author: katietoler
body:
Bug: 

The Holocene date-picker.svelte component has two user-facing bugs in its onInput handler. The displayed format (MM/DD/YYYY, 4-digit year) disagrees with the parser, which only fires when input is exactly 8 chars and assumes a 2-digit year (2000 + YY).

Impact:

Editing the date inline does nothing. Changing the prefilled year (e.g. 2026→2027) produces a >8-char string, so date change never fires. The displayed value updates but the bound value silently stays at the default or last calendar-clicked date — no validation feedback. On API key creation this means the key gets an expiration the user didn't choose.

Typing a 4-digit year produces a past date. Typing 06/05/2026 triggers parsing mid-type at 06/05/20 → year 2020; the final 26 makes it 10 chars so it's never re-parsed. The key silently expires in 2020.

Fix direction: Align displayed and accepted input on MM/DD/YYYY; parse only on a complete, valid date (reject partials and invalid dates like 02/30/2026); surface invalid input instead of silently keeping a stale value; apply isAllowed to typed input.

author: wkasekende
body:
## Summary

Anthropic shipped **[Claude Fable 5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-fable-5-mythos-5)** (Mythos-class frontier model) on 2026-06-09. This PR wires it across both provider paths AND adds a global control for how every anthropic-class `with <model>` override gets dispatched.

`@opencues/core` 0.3.6 → 0.3.7 · `@opencues/runtime` 0.3.0 → 0.3.1

## Two halves

### 1. Fable 5 support

- API path: `anthropic.knownModels += claude-fable-5`
- Subscription path: `claude-code-cli.knownModels += fable, claude-fable-5` + new `fable` model family in the CLI daemon with Opus-mirroring flag tuning (pending a real benchmark row)
- `COMMON_ALIASES['fable']` → `(anthropic, claude-fable-5)`. The CLI's `--model` does NOT alias-resolve short `fable` (only opus/sonnet/haiku are CLI-side aliases) — the daemon sends the full id.

### 2. Global `anthropic-subscription` routing

Every anthropic-class `with` override (`with anthropic` / `claude` / `opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` / `fable` / any full id) auto-routes through the local `claude` CLI when the binary is on PATH. New `applySubscriptionPreference` post-processor rewrites the resolved provider; non-anthropic overrides are never touched.

New `anthropic-subscription` global scalar in `OPENCUES.md` controls this:

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `prefer` (default) | CLI when available, silent fall-back to API when missing |
| `only` | **Billing safety.** Always use CLI. Fails at spawn if missing — no silent API charge |
| `off` | Always API, ignore CLI |

Cyclable via `opencues settings _`. Hot-reloads.

## Bug fix caught during validation

`resolveOverride` in both `FluidBlankSource` and `TransformBlankSource` gated on `apiKeys[adapter.envKeyName]`. The CLI provider has `envKeyName=''` (auth via `claude /login`), so the lookup returned undefined and every subscription override was silently dropped — agentic scenarios 72 + 74 caught it. Fix: short-circuit `transport === 'cli'` before the apiKey gate.

## What's NOT in this PR

- **No runtime fallback.** If the CLI is installed but auth has expired or the model isn't on the user's subscription tier, the dispatch surfaces the CLI error rather than silently retrying through the API. Adding runtime fallback would need explicit error classification + a session-level "CLI is broken" cache. Tracked as a follow-up.
- **Per-bucket subscription routing.** Bucket scalars (`cues-llm-provider: claude-code-cli`) already work today via the existing route — this PR only changes per-call `with` overrides.

## Tests

- **32 model-aliases unit tests** pin every routing cell — mode × CLI-available × token-class — including the three-mode parity (`prefer` default), `only`'s unconditional rewrite, `off`'s skip-everywhere, and the non-anthropic-untouched invariant.
- **4 new agentic scenarios** in `opencues-agentic#scenarios/recent-perf-prs` (72-75) drive the matrix end-to-end through the resolver and event-bridge on opencode 1.14.17. **All green.**
- **Existing override scenarios 65-67** updated to pin `anthropic-subscription: off` so their pre-feature assertions stay deterministic.
- **Feature-registry alignment test** confirms `OpenCuesState` ↔ `FEATURES` drift gate holds for the new 3-value enum.

## Bench (informational)

| Path | tiny prompt | short prompt | medium prompt |
|---|---|---|---|
| API (anthropic) | ~6.9 s | ~4.2 s | ~10.4 s |
| CLI (subscription) | ~4.3 s | ~8.8 s | ~9.9 s |

Both paths land in the 4-10s range — Fable 5 is slow like Opus. High trial-to-trial variance (API tiny went 3.7s → 10s between trials) suggests TTFT is queue-dominated at Anthropic two days post-launch. Thinking explicitly disabled on both paths — these are the fast-version numbers; enabling thinking would push latency to 15-30s.

## Docs

- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased entry covering both halves
- `docs/architecture/model-override.md` — full coverage matrix, plumbing, "no runtime fallback" caveat
- `docs/features/model-override.md` — user-facing aliases table now lists `fable`; new Subscription-preference section with the billing-safety rationale

author: tkhahns
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED` crash on the Vercel deployment.

## Root cause

Vercel's Python builder always resolves dependencies from the root `pyproject.toml` when one exists (verified in the `@vercel/python` builder source — the manifest is resolved at the repo root regardless of entrypoint location, and `pyproject.toml` takes precedence over `requirements.txt`). The full dependency closure (`databento` → pandas/pyarrow, `aiokafka`, `psycopg`, …) is ~290 MB, exceeding the bundle limit, so the builder deferred packages to runtime installation — which crashed function cold starts.

## Fix

Override `installCommand` in `vercel.json` with `uv pip install -r requirements.txt`. The builder honors a project-level install command by skipping its pyproject dependency sync entirely and running the custom command inside the build venv.

## Validation

Reproduced the failure and verified the fix with local `vercel build`:
- Before: `Total bundle size (293.63 MB) exceeds Lambda limit (245 MB)`
- After: `Build completed successfully` — function bundle contains the dashboard static assets, `market_platform` source, and vendored `fastapi`/`redis` only (no pandas/pyarrow/databento)

57 tests pass, ruff clean.

author: clovenbradshaw-ctrl
body:
## What & why

A Matrix ID (`@collective_boundary730383:hyphae.social`) is verified identity but a poor public byline. This lets a verified mxid set a **public-facing display name**, and makes the act **auditable** by storing it the way everything else here lives — as an **append-only EO event log JSONL on GitHub**.

Today `window.NPJ.PEOPLE[mxid]` already drives every `Handle` byline/avatar but is never populated, so stories render the raw `@name:server`. This wires it to a committed registry.

## How it works

New file **`site/usernames.jsonl`** — schema `npj/username-eo/1`, same grammar as the article logs:

```jsonl
{"v":"npj/username-eo/1","op":"INS","target":"username/@mx:hs","ts":"…","actor":"@admin","operand":{"mxid":"@mx:hs","username":"Public Name"}}
{"v":"npj/username-eo/1","op":"REC","target":"username/@mx:hs","ts":"…","actor":"@admin","note":"…","operand":{"mxid":"@mx:hs","username":"New Name"}}
```

- `INS` claims a name, `REC` renames — **nothing is ever rewritten**, so the file is the complete history of who published under which name and when.
- Folded into `NPJ.PEOPLE` at boot (cached + capped so first paint shows real names), then refreshed in the background.
- Committed through the **same n8n publish webhook** as the layout config — admin-only, re-verified server-side via Matrix `whoami` (a non-article file → founding admin only). Each line records `actor` + `ts` for the audit trail.

## Changes

- **`app/identity.js`** (new) — `window.NpjIdentity`: event lines, `foldLog` (keeps per-mxid `history`), `loadRegistry` → `PEOPLE`, `setUsername` (overwrite to seed the file, append thereafter), deterministic avatar color.
- **`index.html`** — load `identity.js`; fold the registry before first paint and refresh on boot.
- **`app/AdminEditor.jsx`** — a **Public byline** panel: set/rename the admin byline, with the committed audit trail (name · who set it · when · revision count).
- **`README.md` / `backend/README.md`** — documented.

## Notes / open questions

- Scope is **admin-curated** (matches the existing "founding admin curates" model and the webhook's non-article-file rule). If contributors should set their *own* bylines, that needs a webhook authorization change (`site/usernames.jsonl` append gated to the line's own `actor`) — happy to follow up if wanted.
- No backend/n8n redeploy required: the webhook is path-agnostic for content; `site/usernames.jsonl` already falls under its existing admin-only rule.

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
## Implementato

`validate-dist` red su deploy run [27276342857](https://github.com/valerielinc-ops/frontaliere-si-o-no/actions/runs/27276342857/job/80584719653): step **Post-build validations** → `validate:jobs-quality` `code_in_description: 2` (HOCH Health Ostschweiz, "CSS background-image, CSS display").

**Root cause:** SuccessFactors CSB (HOCH, Mobiliar, …) appende un foglio di stile inline come **testo** dentro il container description — a volte dopo un marker `/*f20250516*/`, a volte perché `readPropertyBlock` taglia il tag `<style>` di apertura → lo stripper `<style>…</style>` in `htmlToText` non lo raggiunge. La CSS residua faceva scattare il gate.

**Fix di classe** in `stripInlineJsCode` (sanitizer description condiviso da ~50 parser hospital/SF, via `htmlToText`):
- Aggiunto un terzo probe che tronca un blocco-regola CSS class/id finale con una dichiarazione reale (`display/background-image/margin/font/color/…`), opzionalmente preceduto da `/* … */`.
- Selettore deve iniziare con `.`/`#` → prosa tipo "Stufe 2.0 {…}" non viene toccata.
- Taglio al **primo** match tra i probe JS/CSS, così un tail widget+stylesheet sparisce intero.

author: coastal-ms
body:
## Symptom

Reboot and "Start BG Only" appeared to **hang for up to ~15 minutes** on the `Waiting for DB pod(s) Ready…` step (screenshot showed it climbing past 2:00 against a historical avg of ~32s).

## Root cause (verified on the live cluster)

The DB-readiness gate selects database pods by the `-db-` / `postgres` / `pg-` name pattern. That pattern **over-matches**: besides the real DB StatefulSet pod (`db-dbdepl-sts-0`), it also catches:

- `db-dbdepl-util-*` — a **one-shot Job pod that sits in `Completed` forever**
- `db-util-mon-*`, `db-util-pghero-*` — monitoring sidecars

`kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready` waits on **all** listed pods, and a `Completed` pod's Ready condition is `False` permanently — so the wait blocks for the **entire `--timeout` (900s)** and then exits non-zero ("proceeding anyway"). On boots where the util Job pod had already been garbage-collected, the wait was fast (~32s) — which is why it only *sometimes* hung.

Empirically confirmed: `kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready` on the Completed util pod ran the full timeout then returned `error: timed out waiting for the condition`.

## Fix

Tighten the `awk` filter in **both** the reboot and start paths to additionally:
- exclude `util` / `mon` / `pghero` helper pods by name, and
- exclude any terminal (`Completed` / `Succeeded`) pod by status column.

So the gate only ever waits on the real DB StatefulSet pod.

**Live verification** — same cluster, same moment:
- Old filter → 4 pods (incl. the `Completed` `db-dbdepl-util` that caused the stall)
- New filter → exactly 1 pod: `…-db-dbdepl-sts-0`

## Validation
- `dune-server.ps1` parses clean under pwsh 7.
- Version bumped 11.4.9 → 11.4.10; CHANGELOG + README updated.

author: os-zhuang
body:
## Summary

Both attempts of [run 27288401243](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/27288401243) (PR #1627) failed at the final "Comment PR with results" step with **401 Requires authentication**, even though the performance budget check itself passed.

Investigation showed this was a transient GitHub-side token rejection, not a workflow misconfiguration:
- the step received a non-empty `github-token` and the request carried an `authorization: bearer` header, yet GitHub's auth layer rejected it (401, not a 403 permission error)
- checkout authenticated with the same token minutes earlier in the same job
- the identical workflow commented successfully on PR #1626 just 38 minutes before

The workflow's real defects were that it turned this blip into a job failure:
1. `createComment` was un-awaited with no error handling → unhandled rejection fails the step
2. github-script retries were off, and its default retry-exempt list includes 401/403

## Changes

- enable `retries: 3` with `retry-exempt-status-codes: 400,404,422` so transient 401/403/5xx are retried
- `await` the `createComment` call in try/catch; on persistent failure, log a warning and write the report to the job summary instead so the data isn't lost
- `continue-on-error: true` as a backstop so the comment step can never fail the job (the budget check remains a separate, still-fatal step)

GitHub's attestation API returned `401 Failed to persist attestation: Requires authentication` on both v3.0.0 release attempts (run 27288564313, attempts 1 and 2), even though the repo is public, permissions are correct, and the same step worked for v2.3.6 this morning. author: fabiodalez-dev
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two e2e specs that failed deterministically (album-state-transitions T1 and nsfw-password-complete "Create 4 test albums") — verified failing identically on older commits, so test bugs rather than app regressions. Three compounding root causes:

1. **Unanchored URL regexes** in `nsfw-password-complete.spec.js`: `waitForURL(/\/admin\/albums/)` matched `/admin/albums/create` (and `/\/admin/` matched `/admin/login`), so the wait resolved instantly on the page being *left* — it never waited. The following `goto` then collided with the real, still-inflight navigation ("interrupted by another navigation"). Anchored like the sibling spec already documented.

2. **Navigation-event race with the CSRF-refresh handler**: the admin layout's capture-phase submit handler swallows every POST form submit, fetches a fresh token, and re-dispatches asynchronously. The resulting navigation can slip past `waitForURL`'s event window even when armed before the click — verified with traces showing the browser landing on `/admin/albums` with the success flash while `waitForURL` times out. All submit-and-wait pairs replaced with `expect(page).toHaveURL(...)`, which polls the URL and is immune to event races.

3. **Redundant re-navigation**: the `goto('/admin/albums')` right after the post-submit redirect already landed there is now conditional.

Plus: settle waits after force-toggling the NSFW checkbox, and `domcontentloaded` on admin gotos so background thumbnail-variant encoding can't stall `load`-based waits.

Note: `nsfw-password-complete.spec.js` was never tracked (`tests/` is gitignored with selective force-adds) — added with `-f` like its 27 tracked siblings.

## Test plan

- Both specs run serially, twice in a row: **29/29 passed** both times.
- Environment prerequisites for the suite (dev DB): `performance.cache_enabled=true` and `image.formats` enabled — otherwise the cache-header and variant-serving tests fail by design.

author: yeraze
body:
## Summary

Brings full **Apprise** notification support to the **desktop (Tauri) bundles**. Today the desktop app ships the Node backend but no Python, so the Apprise engine — which the Docker image runs as a Python sidecar — is unavailable; desktop users can only point at a remote Apprise API. This freezes Apprise into a single self-contained executable bundled next to the Node binary, so desktop gets the same 100+ notification services with no system Python.

**Draft intentionally** — the main goal of opening it is to **verify the per-platform builds (Windows + macOS) compile and bundle correctly in CI**. There is no local Rust toolchain in the dev environment, so CI's `lint-rust`/build jobs are the first real compile of the Rust changes.

## Approach (Option A: freeze the existing wrapper)

- **`desktop/apprise-sidecar/`** — PyInstaller spec (`collect_all('apprise')` pulls every notification plugin) + `build.sh`/`build.ps1` + pinned `requirements.txt`. Freezes the **existing** `docker/apprise-api.py`, so desktop and Docker share one notification code path. Built ~18 MB on Linux/Py3.14 and smoke-tested locally (`/health` + a `json://` dispatch confirm plugins load inside the frozen binary).
- **Rust (`lib.rs`/`main.rs`)** — `start_apprise()` locates the bundled binary, picks a free loopback port, spawns it bound to `127.0.0.1` only, and injects `APPRISE_URL` into the Node backend (which `appriseNotificationService` already honors). Started once, kept alive across backend restarts; a **missing binary is non-fatal**. Stopped on exit; timer/process cleanup wired in.
- **`docker/apprise-api.py`** — bind host is now `APPRISE_HOST` (default `''` preserves Docker behavior; desktop sets `127.0.0.1` so the sidecar never reaches the LAN). Backward-compatible.
- **CI** (`desktop-ci.yml` / `desktop-release.yml`) — per-platform PyInstaller build step on **Windows** and **macOS-arm64**; the release workflow signs the frozen binary with the hardened runtime (`apprise.entitlements`) before notarization.

## Known gap (documented)

**macOS x86_64** is cross-compiled to x64 on an Apple-Silicon (arm64) runner, and PyInstaller can't cross-compile — it would emit an arm64 binary. So the Intel build **omits** the sidecar (Intel users fall back to a remote Apprise API via the `appriseApiServerUrl` global setting). The Rust launcher treats a missing binary as non-fatal. See `desktop/apprise-sidecar/README.md`.

## Testing / verification asks

- ✅ Frozen binary builds + smoke-tests locally on Linux (~18 MB, plugins load, dispatch works).
- ⏳ **CI is the verification target**: Windows build, macOS-arm64 build (+ sidecar bundling), macOS-x64 build (no sidecar), and the Rust compile (`lint-rust`/clippy) — none of which can run in the local dev env.
- The 18 MB frozen binary lands in `desktop/resources/` (gitignored) and is produced fresh per-platform in CI; it is **not** committed.

body:
## Summary

Tunes `UJNodePoolStuckOperation` alert to reduce noise before prod deployment. Prod analysis showed ~25 grouped incidents per week in eastus2 alone at the 1h threshold.

## Changes

- Increase stuck threshold from 1h (3600s) to 2h (7200s)
- Add `for: 15m` sustained observation
- Update annotations to say "2 hours"
- Update tests (4, 5, 12) for new threshold
- Regenerate Bicep

## Rationale

mmazur's prod analysis showed:
- eastus2: 173 firings / 25 incidents at `for: 5m`, barely drops to 24 at `for: 30m`
- uksouth: 28 firings / 7 incidents at `for: 5m`

The stuck operations persist for long stretches (not transient), so increasing `for` alone doesn't help. A 2h threshold cleanly separates "slow but completing" from "genuinely stuck" operations. With `> 7200` + `for: 15m`, an operation must be stuck for 2h15m before firing.

## Related

- Merged alert PR: #5112
- Prod analysis: shared by mmazur in Slack

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

Adds live bank feeds and ML-assisted reconciliation to close the Xero-parity gap, behind a provider abstraction so US (Plaid), EU/UK (GoCardless Open Banking) and CSV all flow through one interface. New tables are RLS-enabled + tenant-scoped, credentials are field-encrypted with `KAPP_MASTER_KEY`, every mutation is audited, and Plaid/GoCardless config **fails closed** in production when half-configured.

This PR is the **backend core** (provider abstraction, migration, matcher, rule engine, sync handler, config). Routes, frontend, agent tools and KChat commands are intentionally deferred to follow-up PRs to keep this reviewable.

### Provider abstraction (`internal/ledger/bankfeed/`)
One interface, three implementations, selected via a registry:
```go
type Provider interface {
    Name() string
    InitiateConnect(ctx, tenantID, bankAccountID uuid.UUID, redirectURI string) (string, error)
    CompleteConnect(ctx, tenantID uuid.UUID, code string) (*Connection, error)
    FetchTransactions(ctx, conn *Connection, since time.Time) ([]RawTransaction, string, error) // returns next cursor
    Disconnect(ctx, conn *Connection) error
}
```
- `plaid.go` — Link token → `public_token` exchange → `/transactions/sync` cursor pagination (outflows negated).
- `gocardless.go` — requisition/consent link flow, bearer token cached until expiry.
- `csv.go` — wraps the existing CSV path so manual statements share the unified pipeline.
- `connection.go` — `ConnectionStore` persists connections with `access_token_enc` / `refresh_token_enc` encrypted via `internal/tenant` `KeyManager`; raw tokens never hit the DB or logs.

### Smart matcher (`internal/ledger/matcher.go`)
Confidence model in `[0,1]`: exact amount `+0.4`, date proximity `+0.2`, description similarity (Levenshtein + token overlap) `+0.2`, learned counterparty `+0.2`. `SuggestMatches` loads in-window journal candidates, scores them (best line per entry, never double-suggested), and persists suggestions above `MinConfidence`. `AcceptSuggestion` reconciles the line, rejects sibling suggestions, and feeds `bank_learned_matches` so the same counterparty is nudged to the same account next time. Recurring detection groups by description + approximate amount on a monthly/weekly cadence.

### Rule engine (`internal/ledger/bankfeed/rules.go`)
Tenant-configurable, priority-ordered auto-categorization (`description_contains` | `description_regex` | `amount_range` | `counterparty`) that runs on freshly-synced lines before the matcher; an `auto_approve` rule auto-accepts the top suggestion only when it clears `AutoAcceptThreshold` (0.80) — we never fabricate a journal entry.

### Sync handler (`internal/ledger/bankfeed/sync.go`)
`ActionHandler` pattern (mirrors `internal/inventory/reorder.go`): per active connection, fetch since cursor → `SyncBankTransactions` (idempotent dedup on `external_ref` via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) → rules → matcher → advance cursor, emitting `finance.bank_transaction.synced`. The handler depends on narrow interfaces (`connStore`, `ruleLister`, `suggester`) so unit tests run deterministically without a DB.

### Migration `000082_bank_feed.sql`
`bank_feed_connections`, `bank_reconciliation_rules`, `bank_match_suggestions`, `bank_learned_matches` — all `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with tenant-scoped policies.

### Config (`internal/platform/config.go`)
`PlaidClientID/Secret/Env`, `GoCardlessSecretID/SecretKey/InstitutionID`; production validation rejects a half-configured provider (one of a pair set) rather than silently disabling it.

## Testing
- Unit tests use in-memory fakes (no DB): providers, registry, rules, sync handler, matcher scoring, config fail-closed.
- Integration tests (`-tags=integration`, skip without `KAPP_TEST_DB_URL`) run against live Postgres as the non-superuser `kapp_app` role so **RLS is enforced as in production** — covering connection encryption round-trip, rule CRUD ordering, cross-tenant isolation, and the full `suggest → list → accept → reconcile → learn → reject` loop.
- New business-logic coverage: `bankfeed` 83.3%, `matcher.go` ~83% — both above the 80% bar. `gofmt`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint` clean on all new code.

Pre-existing lint findings in untouched code (`config.go` G115 read-replica conns, `bank.go` `ImportBankStatement` rangeValCopy / `MatchWindow` comment) were left as-is to keep the diff scoped.
