author: kemper
body:
## Summary

Upgrades agent code-search from "ripgrep for everything" to the three-modality model the agent-tooling space has converged on — lexical / structural / symbol-graph — using what the repo already had where possible:

- **`.mcp.json`: replace `typescript-mcp` with [Serena](https://github.com/oraios/serena)** (pinned `v1.5.3`, `ide-assistant` context, project-local). Serena wraps tsserver and exposes resolved-reference tools (`find_symbol`, `find_referencing_symbols`, `get_symbols_overview`, `find_declaration`, `find_implementations`) — no string-collision false positives, compact symbol-chunk output. `typescript-mcp` was already flagged in `docs/agent-tooling.md` as unstable upstream ("pin/replace it if its API drifts").
- **Promote ast-grep from lint-only to a search tool.** `@ast-grep/cli` was already a devDependency (behind `lint:consistency`); this documents `npx ast-grep run -p '<pattern>'` as the structural-search rung and pre-allows it in `.claude/settings.json`.
- **Encode the search ladder** (Grep → ast-grep → Serena) in `CLAUDE.md`, a new `docs/agent-tooling.md` section, and the `explore` agent (whose tools move from `mcp__typescript__*` to `mcp__serena__*`).
- **Deliberately skip embedding/vector search** (mgrep et al.) and document why: mgrep's index is cloud-backed, the local options are immature, and at this repo's scale the lexical/structural/graph trio plus the `explore` agent answers conceptual queries without index infrastructure.
- Gitignore `.serena/` (Serena's project metadata/cache).

Tool names in the settings allowlist and docs were verified against the **live** server surface (the `ide-assistant` context exposes `find_declaration`/`find_implementations`/`get_diagnostics_for_file` but not `search_for_pattern`), not upstream docs.

**Requires a remote-environment setup-script update** (install `uv`, allow `astral.sh`/`pypi.org`/`files.pythonhosted.org`/`github.com` in the network policy) — without it the Serena server won't start in fresh containers and agents fall back to ast-grep + Grep per the documented degradation path.

## Test plan

- [x] `.mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.json` validate as JSON
- [x] Serena server connects in this remote environment and `find_symbol` resolves `applyVoxelize` → `src/surface/modifiers.ts:647`
- [x] `find_referencing_symbols` returns exactly the import + the one true call site (`src/main.ts:7610`), no false positives
- [x] `npx ast-grep run -p 'showToast($$$)' -l ts src/main.ts` finds call shapes
- [ ] PR-checks shards green (config/docs-only change; no `src/` modifications)
- [ ] Fresh-session validation that the `explore` agent picks up `mcp__serena__*`

body:
## Summary

Adds a `notify-website` GitHub Actions workflow that propagates documentation changes from this spec repository to the website.

On push to `main`, the workflow sends a `repository-dispatch` event (`event-type: docs-updated`) to the `agentcontextdistributionprotocol/acdp-website` repository, allowing the website to rebuild whenever protocol documentation changes.

## Details

- Uses `peter-evans/repository-dispatch@v4`.
- Authenticates with the `ACDP_WEBSITE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret.
- Triggers only on changes to user-facing content: `docs/**`, `rfcs/**`, `manifesto/**`, and `README.md`.
- Configuration aligned with the canonical control-plane dispatch workflow.

## Prerequisites for the workflow to fire

- The `ACDP_WEBSITE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret must be configured in this repository with `repository-dispatch` permission on `acdp-website`.
- The `acdp-website` repository must have a workflow listening for the `docs-updated` event.

author: zylphrex
body:
Adds `merge_commit_id` to the `PrCloseMetricsEvent` analytics row emitted when a tracked PR is closed or merged.

The row previously carried only the merge commit SHA, which can't be joined to Sentry's own commit/release data downstream (BigQuery). We now resolve the merge commit's Sentry `Commit.id` from `merge_commit_sha` via the `(repository_id, key)` unique key and emit it on the event, so consumers can connect a merged PR to the commit Sentry tracks.

The field is nullable: `null` when the PR wasn't merged (`merge_commit_sha` is `None`) or when Sentry never recorded the landed commit — the pr_metrics module never creates `Commit` rows, so a match isn't guaranteed and we don't fail loud.

We resolve the **merge** commit rather than the head commit because the merge commit is what GitHub lands on the base branch (the squashed commit for squash-and-merge, the merge commit for a regular merge, the last rebased commit for a rebase merge). That's the commit Sentry's release tracking is most likely to have recorded; the head SHA points at the pre-merge branch tip, which is frequently squashed away and untracked.

The lookup is an equality match on `(repository_id, key)`, fully covered by the unique composite index that `unique_together = (("repository_id", "key"),)` creates on `sentry_commit` — a single unique index lookup, no new index needed.

First batch of quick wins from the `improve` codebase audit. Five small, high-confidence findings. The two with infrastructure dependencies were decided before implementation.

**Security**

body:
## Summary

- The `before_agent_reply` hook event only carries `cleanedBody`, so plugins that need to gate a reply on the **current message's materialized media** (e.g. refusing to generate a client-facing audit document unless an auditable source attachment is actually present) cannot see inbound attachments at all — even after the channel has already downloaded them.
- This PR extends `PluginHookBeforeAgentReplyEvent` with optional `body`, `content`, `rawBody`, `bodyForAgent`, and `attachments`/`media` (built from the message context `MediaPaths`/`MediaUrls`/`MediaTypes`) and populates them in the reply pipeline.
- All new fields are optional and only set when the data exists, so existing hook handlers are unaffected (`cleanedBody`-only consumers keep working unchanged).
- Out of scope: the agent-runner `before_agent_reply` call sites for cron/CLI prompts (`cli-runner.ts`, `embedded-agent-runner/run.ts`) — those are prompt-based and have no channel media context.
- Reviewers: focus on the event construction in `get-reply.ts` (attachment array built per-index from MediaPaths/MediaUrls/MediaTypes with MediaType fallback).

## Linked context

Maintainer request: none — limitation found while operating a production OpenClaw gateway where a plugin enforces a fail-closed "no audit document without an anchored source attachment" gate on Telegram.

Related #91984 (companion fix that makes local Bot API attachments materialize at all; independent changes).

- Exact steps or command run after this patch: re-sent the same "generate the audit document from the attached zip" request that previously got blocked.
- Evidence after fix (redacted): the plugin gate classified the request as anchored (attachment visible on the hook event), scheduled the isolated job, and the generated PDF was delivered with an `operation=sendDocument deliveryKind=document` outbound journal entry.
- Observed result after fix: same request that was previously refused with a "missing source" message completed end to end.
- Copied live output (redacted — chat ids, bot token segments, and the client project name masked):

- Proof limitations or environment constraints: live validation used this same event enrichment applied as a dist-level hotfix on the running gateway; this PR is the source port plus regression tests.

## What & why

The onboarding flow shipped but **nothing was wired** — "Choose a translation" showed *"No translations are available yet"*, and `main` CI was **red**: `BibleContentRepository cannot be provided` (no Hilt binding). This PR completes the content pipeline (spec task 14.1) so setup and the reader are functional, and fixes the broken graph.

### How real Bible apps source content
Open-source readers don't host scripture themselves — they pull from open distributors. We use the **Free Use Bible API** (`bible.helloao.org`): key-less, no rate limit, MIT-licensed, cleared for commercial use, and rich in **Indian-language** editions — Telugu (2), Tamil (2), Hindi (2), Malayalam (3), plus Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Punjabi, Urdu — exactly Manna's audience. All complete editions are public-domain/openly-licensed 66-book bibles.

## Changes

**DI / wiring**
- Provide `BibleContentDao`, `OkHttpClient`, `Retrofit` + `HelloAoApi`; apply the additive v2→v3 Room migration.
- `DefaultBibleContentRepository` over `BibleContentDao`.
- `DefaultHelloAoRemoteDataSource` replaces the empty stub: catalog limited to complete 66-book editions, ISO 639-3 → app codes (`eng→en`, `tel→te`, `tam→ta`, `hin→hi`, `mal→ml`, …), verse-text flattening, testament inference from OSIS id.
- Bind `BibleContentRepository`, `DownloadManager`, and the helloao source (catalog + content seams); delete `StubTranslationRemoteDataSource`.

**Tests**

body:
Closes #327.

## What

Replaces the stale RTX 5070 Ti single-request table in the README with current Qwen3-4B numbers against vLLM 0.22.1, backed by a new benchmark snapshot doc so every number is traceable.

## Method

Both engines on the same RTX 5090 (32 GB, TP1, BF16), sequentially, driven by the same `vllm bench serve` client. openinfer at main `6901965`, vLLM 0.22.1 from PyPI. All commands seeded (`--seed 42`) and recorded in the doc; drivers committed under `tools/bench/`.

1. **Poisson QPS sweep** — random dataset 1024 in / 128 out, `--burstiness 1.0`, ~60 s of arrivals per level, prefix cache off on both. openinfer wins low-load TTFT p50 (~10%); vLLM wins TPOT at every level (+11% → +27% as load grows) and saturates later (knee ~QPS 12 vs ~QPS 10).
2. **Warm prefix-cache-hit TTFT sweep** — identical prompt re-sent with `max_tokens=1`, lengths 256→16384, prefix cache on on both, SSE fully drained between samples. openinfer leads at every length, 3× at 16k (30.3 vs 90.8 ms p50).

A historical caveat did not reproduce: openinfer streaming usage accounting through the vLLM frontend is now exact (`total_output_tokens == completed × output_len` in every run).

## Files

- `docs/benchmarks/qwen3-4b-serving-vllm-rtx5090.md` — full tables, commands, readings, caveats
- `README.md` — Performance section rewritten, links to the snapshot

💡 **What**: Replaced `len(text.splitlines())` with `text.count('\n') + (1 if text and not text.endswith('\n') else 0)` for O(1) memory string line counting.

author: robertdias95
body:
## What changed
The Draw Schedule grid's lane-status derivation now chases **one hop** to the parent project's BP when the lane's own project has no permits AND `redesign_reuses_original_permit=true`. Reuse-redesign lanes now display the same derived status as the parent (Approved, Corrections, Under Review, DD-phase dates) instead of the raw `'Scheduled'` default.

## Why
12836 N 60th St [Redesign 1] showed `Scheduled` (grey) while the parent showed "Approval 06-01-26" (green): the parent had a permit to derive from; the redesign (created via fix-126 with `reuses_permit=true`) had none, so `deriveBlockStatus` fell back to the raw status. (The row was manually SQL-patched to `Approved` on 2026-06-09; the inheritance now overrides regardless, so that row is left as-is — harmless.)

## How
- New `deriveLaneStatus` wrapper in `drawScheduleStatus.ts`: picks the effective permit set (own, else the parent's when the redesign has none + parent has a BP) and calls the existing `deriveBlockStatus` with the redesign lane's **own** `currentStatus` + `manualStatus`. So a redesign derives identically to how the parent lane derives — the three permit-data branches still always win; a manual lane status is respected the same way it is on the parent. Both grid call sites (blocks + the status popup) use it.
- **Read-time only** — no writes, no cascade, no new RPC. The grid already loads all projects + permits, so the parent's BP is in memory (a `Map` lookup).
- **One hop** — a redesign-of-a-redesign chases to its immediate parent only.

## Rule chosen (flagged)
**Always inherit** the parent's derivation. Redesign lanes carry `manual_status=false` (auto), so in practice there's no explicit status to stomp; and threading the redesign's own `currentStatus`/`manualStatus` through means an explicit manual choice is still honored exactly as `deriveBlockStatus` honors it on any lane. (Considered fix-147's "don't-stomp" rule, but it's moot here and adds complexity.)

## Tests (+6)
New pure-unit `drawScheduleRedesignStatusInheritance`: parent derives Approved from its BP; reuse-redesign inherits Approved from the parent BP; redesign whose parent also has no BP falls back to its own status; redesign with its own permit (reuses=false) uses its own and never chases; non-redesign no-permit falls back; stale redesign status still inherits the parent's permit-data branch.

## Gauntlet
- typecheck clean, lint 0 errors (pre-existing wizard `exhaustive-deps` warnings only), build clean
- 2153 tests pass (+6 over the 2147 baseline)

## Summary
Slides the §05 Lab Journal paper up from below when the section enters the viewport.

To avoid Reveal's translate fighting with the paper's existing rotate, I split the wrapper in two:

- **Outer** (`<Reveal kind="rise" delay={200}>`) owns `position: absolute`, the placement (`left/right/top/bottom`), `width`, `aspectRatio`, and `z-index`. CaseReveal applies `translate3d(0, 28px, 0)` + `opacity: 0` initially, then transitions to `translate3d(0, 0, 0)` + `opacity: 1` when the section enters view.
- **Inner div** owns `transform: rotate(-3deg / -1deg)` and `transformOrigin`. The paper image, journal content, and index dots stay absolutely positioned within it exactly as before.

The 200ms delay lets the Lab section's other reveals (eyebrow, headline, body, CTAs) settle a beat before the journal page lifts in. `prefers-reduced-motion` is already honored inside CaseReveal.

author: mikesandoval10creator
body:
## Problema

El job "Tests" termina todos los tests (~6 min cuando va bien) y a veces el proceso **nunca sale** → muere al cap de 30 min. **Pasó 3 veces solo hoy** (deploy.yml ya lo conocía como "the flaky open-handle hang") y nos costó un ciclo extra de CI en cada PR.

## Causa raíz (investigación con candidatos rankeados)

Handles abiertos a nivel de módulo retienen el event loop del worker:
1. `healthCheck.ts:94` — `setInterval` del barrido de 6h **sin `unref()`**: cualquier worker que lo importe transitivamente no puede drenar jamás.
2. vitest sin `teardownTimeout` — los workers colgados esperan indefinidamente.
3. El detector de leaks `DETECT_HANDLES` que ya existía en `src/test/setup.ts` (nombra el archivo de test que deja un Timeout/Socket vivo) estaba gateado por env y **nunca corría en CI**.

## Fix (mínimo riesgo)

- `unref()` en el interval (sigue tickeando normal con el server vivo; SIGTERM drena más rápido).
- `teardownTimeout: 10_000` en vitest — mata workers rezagados en vez de colgar el job.
- Detector activo con `CI=true` — el próximo cuelgue **nombra al culpable en el log** en vez de morir mudo.

## Validación

49 tests de triggers/middleware verdes con `CI=true` (detector activo) · tsc 0.

author: cafzal
body:
Addresses the **medium-severity** findings from the security review. Each fix degrades to fail-closed/least-privilege rather than fail-open. Local single-user flows (stdio, `next dev`, ungated loopback) are unchanged.

## What's in this PR

### Auth — fail closed when exposed
- **Engine** (`mcp_server/server.py`): an SSE/streamable-http transport bound to a routable interface (e.g. `MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0`, or an empty/`INADDR_ANY` host) **without** `FRONTIER_MCP_TOKEN` now refuses to start, instead of silently serving an unauthenticated engine with full `model`/`solve`/`explore` access. Loopback binds still serve ungated (with a stderr warning) for local dev. The decision is extracted to a pure `_http_transport_action()` helper with unit tests. The blessed `render.yaml` path is unaffected (token is auto-generated).
- **Web UI** (`ui/middleware.ts`): with `UI_ACCESS_PASSWORD` unset, a **production** build (`NODE_ENV=production`) returns 503 rather than serving open — an open public deploy would let anyone with the URL spend the operator's `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `next dev` stays open for local use.

### Cost abuse — request rate limiting
- New `ui/lib/rate-limit.ts`: per-instance fixed-window limiter (per-IP **and** a global circuit-breaker). Independent budgets per route — `/api/chat` (paid Anthropic, tighter: 30/min per IP, 90/min global) vs `/api/render` (read-only engine compute, looser: 60/180) — so a render burst can't starve the chat cap. Returns 429 + `Retry-After`. Env-tunable (`CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_*` / `RENDER_RATE_LIMIT_*`). Client key uses the rightmost (trusted-proxy-appended) `x-forwarded-for` hop so the per-IP bucket can't be spoofed. Documented as a best-effort per-instance floor — per-user accounting is still D.1. Pure logic with an injectable clock + unit tests.

### Supply chain
- **`constraints.txt`**: full pinned dependency resolution (`uv pip compile`) for the `[sse,highs]` set. CI and `render.yaml` now install with `-c constraints.txt`, so builds are reproducible instead of resolving floating `>=` at run time. Regeneration command is in the file header.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`**: weekly version-update PRs. Dependabot bumps the `pyproject.toml` floors (pip), `ui/package-lock.json` (npm), and workflow action versions (github-actions); it does **not** track the standalone `constraints.txt`, so that lock is regenerated manually after a pip bump.
- **`ci.yml`**: added least-privilege `permissions: contents: read`.
- **PyPI name confusion**: docs instructed `pip install "frontier[highs]"`, but the bare name `frontier` on PyPI is an **unrelated third-party package** (dependency-confusion risk). Corrected to `pip install -e ".[highs]"` from a clone (`pyproject.toml`, `examples/cuopt_colab.ipynb`).

### Docs
- `architecture.md` §5 and `README.md` updated to describe the new fail-closed auth behavior (kept in sync per CLAUDE.md).

## Review fixes (post-open)
- `acfd46c` — **bug:** `""` was treated as a loopback host, but uvicorn binds an empty host to all interfaces (`INADDR_ANY`); with no token that would have served an open public engine. Now classified routable → refuse, with a test.
- `bb265cc` — spoof-resistant client key (rightmost XFF hop), per-route limiter split, and corrected the Dependabot/constraints note above.

## Verification
- Python: 491 passed (`pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/ui -q`), incl. `TestHttpTransportAction`.
- UI: 25 passed (`npm test`), incl. `rate-limit.test.ts`; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `constraints.txt` dry-run-resolved on a clean 3.11 venv; CI verifies the constrained install on Linux.

### Deliberately not changed
- **Sliding window** for the limiter (fixed-window allows a ~2× burst at a boundary) — over-engineering for a best-effort floor; the global cap bounds spend.
- **`--require-hashes`** on installs — incompatible with the `-e .` editable / local-package install without splitting the install step; version pins are the meaningful win here.
- **An env=0 off-switch** for the limiter — a foot-gun for a security control.

## Medium findings NOT in this PR (can't go in a code change)
- **Rotate the leaked Alpha Vantage key** — free-tier key in public git history (`7db4fd5 dev_temp/fetch_etf_data.py`); rotate at the provider, file is already gitignored.
- **Branch protection / required status checks** — repo ruleset change.
- **Enable secret scanning + push protection + Dependabot alerts** — repo settings toggles (this PR adds the Dependabot *config*; the alert/scanning switches are separate).

author: esnunes
body:
## What changed

The extension authenticate/authorize cache key now fingerprints only credential-bearing request headers (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `cookie`, `x-api-key`) instead of hashing every header minus a small noise denylist (`accept`, `content-length`, `host`, `user-agent`, `x-request-id`).

## Root cause

REAPI clients attach a deadline to every RPC, which arrives as a `grpc-timeout` header whose value is the remaining time at send — effectively unique on every request. Because the old fingerprint hashed all-headers-minus-denylist, every deadline-carrying request produced a fresh cache key, so the authenticate cache missed almost permanently. Trace propagation headers (`traceparent`) have the same effect on HTTP traffic.

Every miss re-runs the `authenticate` hook; with the Tuist hook that means a `POST /oauth2/introspect` round-trip to the control plane per miss.

Observed during a single cold `bazel build` of the Kura crate graph against a dev node (no local JWT verifier, so each miss introspects):

- authenticate cache: 15,340 misses vs 13,174 hits (~54% miss rate)
- ~6,800 introspection requests hit the control plane, pinning the Phoenix server's BEAM at ~300% CPU for the duration of the build

Production nodes are affected the same way — real traffic carries `grpc-timeout` and `traceparent` — just with the introspection volume spread across the fleet.

## Why this solution

The function is named `credentials_fingerprint` and the cache is documented as "per credentials"; the denylist approach was an under-approximation of that intent that silently broke whenever clients sent any per-request header. An allowlist of credential headers makes the intent hold structurally. Hooks that authenticate from non-standard inputs can still opt out of caching via a short/absent `ttl_seconds` — documented in the README.

## Validation

- New regression test: same credentials with varying `grpc-timeout`/`traceparent` reuse the cached result (identity backend called once); a different `authorization` value does not share the cache entry.
- `cargo test extension::` — 24 passed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- Live validation on a dev kind node running this patch, driving comparable Bazel build volume (a full re-upload pass plus incremental/no-op builds): authenticate cache went to **11,444 hits / 14 misses (99.9% hit rate)** and total introspection calls for the whole session dropped from ~6,800 to **14**.

body: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/SVLS-9287 ## Background For Firecracker-based container technology, in order to reduce cold-start latency, the system snapshots the entire process memory of a warmed-up instance and reuses it to launch new ones. Every resumed instance starts from the same frozen memory image — including any userspace state that was initialized before the snapshot was taken. ## Summary - Extends the existing `secureRandom` logic to also activate when running in AWS Lambda MicroVM environments (detected via the `AWS_LAMBDA_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN` environment variable) - MicroVM environments, like SnapStart, benefit from `SecureRandom`-based ID generation because memory snapshots can cause ID collisions with standard random sources - Adds `ConfigSecureRandomTest` with 5 JUnit 5 tests covering all activation paths (default, SnapStart, MicroVM ARN, empty ARN, config property) ## Test plan - [ ] `./gradlew :internal-api:test --tests datadog.trace.api.ConfigSecureRandomTest` passes - [ ] Verify `secureRandom = true` when `AWS_LAMBDA_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN` is set to a non-empty value - [ ] Verify `secureRandom = false` (default) when `AWS_LAMBDA_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN` is empty or unset - [ ] Integration shows `secureRandom = true` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

- Adds a Source Register inflation gate: registers with `>25%` uncited entries may not be marked source-traceability passed.
- Extends the declared-execution lint to fail partial-citation cases where most register IDs are never cited in the body.
- Documents the `<10%` / `10-25%` / `>25%` severity scale and extra-reading boundary.

## Problem

Issue #225 identified a traceability gap: a report can include a large Source Register while citing only a small fraction of its entries in the body. Existing rules already said every register entry should be cited, but the executable lint only caught the zero-body-citation case, so register inflation could still pass.

Closes #225.

## Why this change

This keeps the fix narrow: it strengthens the existing Source Register discipline and declared-execution lint without redesigning traceability parsing or expanding into route-specific checklist rewrites.

## Files changed

- `scripts/validate_declared_execution.py`: compares Source Register IDs to body `[Sxx]` citations and fails when uncited entries exceed 25%.
- `scripts/test_declared_execution.py`: adds regression coverage for uncited register inflation and a fully cited pass case.
- `checklists/source-traceability.md`: adds register inflation and hard-fail escalation checks.
- `references/source-traceability-and-claim-citation.md`: adds register discipline guidance, severity scale, and extra-reading boundary.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: records the behavior change.

## Expected behavior change

A report with a Source Register that lists many unused `Sxx` entries can no longer use that register as proof that source traceability passed. Authors must remove unused entries, cite them in the body, or move them to an explicit extra-reading appendix.

## Eval impact

- Added eval: none; issue #225 already points to `evals/cases/embodied-ai-market-outlook-register-and-label-gap-case.md` as the motivating case.
- Updated eval: none.
- No eval change because this PR adds a focused executable regression test for the declared-execution lint behavior.

## Risks / possible regressions

- The automatic lint intentionally only checks structured `[Sxx]` body citations. Functionally equivalent formats remain governed by manual checklist/reference guidance to avoid false hard-fails.
- Reports with legitimate background sources should move them to an explicit Extra Reading / Extended Bibliography section instead of counting them as Source Register traceability evidence.

## Validation

- TDD red: `python3 scripts/test_declared_execution.py` failed on `test_source_register_uncited_inflation_fails` before implementation.

author: maggiedp
body:
## Summary

When a game reaches a final status during a browsing session, it now visibly moves into the **Completed** section instead of just vanishing from the upcoming list (the behavior left after PR #68). Pure client-side change to the inline JS in `src/api/templates/homepage.html`.

Covers both ways a game vanishes today:
- **Live→final** — a game you were watching flips to FINAL mid-session (caught by the live-WP poll path, `hydrateOneLiveWp`, which already holds the `/api/live-wp` payload).
- **Stale-at-load** — a game already final when the page loaded (e.g. an evening visitor before the 6 AM run; `/api/games/upcoming` is DB-only and still serves it). The status poll corrects it and a new best-effort `rebucketFinalFromStatusPoll` fetches `/api/live-wp` for its scores so it can be spliced in.

## How

- **Local splice, not refetch.** `/api/games/completed` is DB-backed and a same-day final isn't written until the 6 AM run, so refetching wouldn't include it. `rebucketIntoCompleted(game, wpData)` builds a completed-shaped **clone** from the in-memory game + the `/api/live-wp` payload (`home_score`/`away_score`/`plays`) and pushes it into the client-side `allCompleted`. Clones rather than mutating the shared upcoming object so a final can never leak into the upcoming table with a score showing. `team_a` is the home team, so `home_score → final_score_a`.
- Split `excitementScore(plays)` (numeric) out of `computeExcitement` (label wrapper) so a spliced row carries a real `excitement_index` and renders identically (score column + Thriller/Close badge).
- **Startup-race fix:** `loadGames` fires `loadCompleted()` and `hydrateGameStatuses()` concurrently. `loadCompleted` now **merges** (preserves client-rebucketed espn_ids not in the server snapshot) instead of replacing `allCompleted`, so a rebucketed same-day final can't be clobbered regardless of which fetch resolves first.

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/` green (407 passed). New string-presence guards in `tests/test_completed_rebucket.py` pin the merge (vs a bare replace), the status-poll rebucket helper, and the `newlyFinal` re-filter.
- Reviewed by two-stage subagent review per task + a Codex adversarial pass (round 1 caught the startup race — fixed; round 2 approved) + a `/simplify` cleanup pass.
- **Manual live verification pending:** the rebucket behavior only manifests when a game finalizes during a session, so it will be confirmed against a live game (watch a game flip to FINAL → confirm it moves to Completed with correct score + excitement badge on desktop and mobile; load shortly after a game finishes → confirm it lands in Completed rather than vanishing).

## Summary

Fix multiple tray and system proxy issues:

1. **Tray sysproxy dot state inversion**: The tray menu dot was showing the opposite state of the actual system proxy setting. Fixed by using `TrayState` as the single source of truth instead of re-querying the system.

2. **Lightweight mode tray operations**: In lightweight mode (WebView destroyed), tray operations now work via Rust-side direct handling (`toggle_sys_proxy`) instead of depending on the frontend.

3. **Wrong proxy port in lightweight mode**: `toggle_sys_proxy` was using `last_port()` (API port 9090) instead of the actual proxy port (7890). Added `last_proxy_port()` that parses `mixed-port`/`port`/`socks-port` from the YAML config with proper priority. Ports with value `0` (disabled) are filtered out to preserve the fallback chain.

4. **Tray menu i18n in lightweight mode**: `rebuild_tray_menu_from_state` was using hardcoded English strings. Added `TrayLabels` struct to store i18n text from the frontend.

5. **Notification permission error**: Added `notification:default` to capabilities.

6. **Settings toggle sync**: Closing "minimize to tray" now auto-disables lightweight mode (consistent with smart/auto-test toggle behavior). Fixed `save()` race condition.

7. **Tray dot not syncing from main UI**: Added `updateTrayMenu()` to `appStore.subscribe('isSysProxyEnabled')` callback.

8. **Mutex poisoned recovery**: Use `unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)` consistently across all mutex lock acquisitions for robustness.

author: joerger
body:
Closes https://github.com/gravitational/pressure-washing/issues/25

Changelog: Fix inconsistent usage of the internal remote username transform - `remote-<user>-<origin>` - which could result in audit log inaccuracies and narrow ssh authz bypasses in shared sessions with a cross-cluster username collision among participants.

Overview: `UsernameForRemoteCluster` is now consistently called just once for remote users on the identity construction boundary for Teleport sessions. This fixes username collision authz/audit issues upfront, as opposed to the ad-hoc logic we had that was broken in multiple locations, particularly in the SSH service.

## Changes
- SSH `IdentityContext.TeleportUser` is now set to the cluster-qualified (`remote-<user>-<origin>`) username for remote users.
  - This fixes a class of authz bypass/failure bugs where we would cluster-qualify one side of an authz comparison, but not the other side. Specifically, this fixes:
    - `user(remote)@local-node` can now join their own session. `user(local)` can no longer join that session.
    - `user(remote)@local-node` initiates a file transfer and it gets approved. `user(local)` can no longer use the approved file transfer.
  - This matches the `authz.Context.User` used for Kube/DB/Desktop/App services, so we now consistently set the cluster-qualified username at the earliest Authn opportunity for consistent use in the session tracker, audit events, etc. There are now only 2 calls to `UsernameForRemoteCluster` outside of tests, where it was previously scattered.
- Fix inconsistent usage of cluster-qualified usernames in audit events / recovery and the predicate parser.
  - kube/db/desktop `session.end` events (emitted by the service or recovered by Auth) had double cluster-qualified usernames, e.g. `remote-remote-dev-root-root`.
  - predicate parser no longer cluster-qualify session participants. This was resulting in cluster-qualified usernames for SSH, but double cluster-qualified usernames for Kube/DB/Desktop/App. Now it works as expected for all 5 services.
### Side effects worth noting
- The cluster-qualified name now appears in session trackers (`tsh session ls` participants), moderated session output (`User remote-dev-root joined the session with participant mode: peer`), etc.
  - The raw username is only still used for SSH env vars set in the session - `SSH_TELEPORT_USER` and `TELEPORT_USERNAME`. This avoids breaking tsh / scripts / pam modules which interface with Teleport using these env vars as real Teleport usernames/emails/etc. 
- Web UI moderation context uses the target cluster username `clt.GetCurrentUser` instead of the proxy-local web session username, so it stays aligned with the cluster-qualified `HostUser` set by upgraded SSH services.

### Upgrade story
- Upgrading the SSH service fixes the primary bugs (SSH session joining collision, SSH file transfer collision).
- Upgrading the Proxy aligns the web UI moderation context with the cluster-qualified HostUser that upgraded SSH services write. The Proxy and SSH service should be upgraded together: upgrading only one breaks cross-cluster own-session join via the web UI until the other catches up.
- Upgrading DB/Kube/Desktop fixes the double-transform bug in their respective audit events.
- Upgrading Auth fixes the double-transform bug in the tracker parser and session-end recovery. The auth-side read paths apply an idempotent fallback transform for participant strings, so old-SSH-emitted raw usernames are normalized on read and there are no transient regressions during the upgrade window.
 
## Manual Test Plan
### Test Environment
Setup a trusted cluster (root and leaf). On each cluster, create a user "dev" with the "access" role. Create a third user on the leaf cluster with the "see-remote-user-sessions" role below.

```
kind: role
version: v7
metadata:
  name: see-remote-user-sessions
spec:
  allow:
    rules:
      - resources: [session_tracker]
        verbs: [list, read]
        where: 'contains(session_tracker.participants, "remote-dev-root.example.com")'
      - resources: [ssh_session]
        verbs: [list, read]
        where: 'contains(ssh_session.participants, "remote-dev-root.example.com")'
```

### Test Cases
- [x] user(root) starts an SSH session on a leaf node.
  - [x] user(root) can view or join with:
    - [x] `tsh session ls`
    - [x] `tsh join`
    - [x] WebUI
      - [x] can initiate and complete a file transfer
  - [x] user(leaf) cannot view or join with:
    - [x] `tsh session ls`
    - [x] `tsh join`
    - [x] WebUI
  - [x] user with "see-remote-user-sessions" role can view the session.
- [x] user(leaf) starts an SSH session on a leaf node.
  - [x] user(root) cannot view or join with:
    - [x] `tsh session ls`
    - [x] `tsh join`
    - [x] WebUI
  - [x] user(leaf) can view or join with:
    - [x] `tsh session ls`
    - [x] `tsh join`
    - [x] WebUI
      - [x] can initiate and complete a file transfer
   - [x] user with "see-remote-user-sessions" role cannot view the session.

- [x] Session start and end events are populated with the cluster-qualified name in the `participants` and `user` fields for:
  - [x] ssh
  - [x] kube
  - [x] db
  - [x] app
  - [x] desktop

# Summary

Follow-up to #376 (merged) — addresses the round-3 Copilot review comments that arrived after the merge, plus one hygiene-audit cleanup.

### Security & correctness fixes
- **WooCommerce webhook fails closed**: when `WOOCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not configured, the handler now throws `400` instead of skipping signature verification (previously an unauthenticated public surface in misconfigured environments)
- **Typed webhook body**: `receive()` now takes `WooCommerceOrderPayload` directly — removed the untyped `WooCommerceWebhookBody` interface and unsafe cast

author: mastermanas805
body:
## Problem (live-verified)

The SDK's single client-wide ~30 s HTTP timeout was too tight for **synchronous** provisioning. Under prod hot-pool contention a *fresh* Postgres provision exceeds 30 s; the client gave up, the server kept working and held a **60 s in-flight idempotency marker**, so the caller's retry hit `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`. Raising the client-side timeout to ~120 s fixed it in the field.

## Fix

- **Provisioning + deploy now default to a 120 s per-request deadline; reads stay at 30 s.** The provisioning paths (`ProvisionDatabase/Cache/MongoDB/Queue/Storage/Webhook` + `Deploy`) run on a dedicated `provisionClient` that carries **no client-wide `Timeout` cap**; the 120 s budget is enforced per-request via `provisionContext`. Read calls (`list/get/claim/delete/rotate`) are unchanged on the existing `httpClient.Timeout` (30 s), so the guarded read-path timeout tests stay green.
- **`WithTimeout` still overrides** — it now governs *both* the read and provisioning budgets. A `WithHTTPClient` whose `Timeout` is explicitly set governs provisioning too (the SDK won't silently widen a caller's deliberate budget to 120 s).
- **A tighter caller `context.Context` deadline is always honoured** — `provisionContext` only lengthens an open-ended context, never overrides a shorter caller deadline.
- The single client-wide cap was the root constraint: `http.Client.Timeout` is a hard ceiling on every request, so a per-request context deadline alone couldn't extend past 30 s. Splitting into two HTTP clients (sharing the same auth-wrapped transport) is the least-disruptive correct fix and leaves the read-path tests — `TestNew_DefaultsAndOptions` (`Timeout == defaultTimeout`) and `client_options_test.go`'s `TestWithHTTPClient_PreservesTimeout` — untouched.

No 30 s default was *intentionally guarded for the provisioning path*; the only pinned-30 s tests are read-path and remain valid.

## Tests (package `instant`, run under `-race` in CI)

- `TestProvisioningTimeoutDefaults` — pins read=30 s / provision=120 s split + `provisionClient.Timeout==0`.
- `TestProvisioningOutlivesReadCap` — behavioral proof: a provision succeeds against a server that stalls *past* the read-path cap, while a read against the same server times out (scaled to ms; same mechanism as 30 s/120 s).
- `TestProvisioningHonorsTighterCallerDeadline`, `TestWithTimeoutGovernsProvisioning`, `TestWithHTTPClientTimeoutGovernsProvisioning`, `TestProvisionContextOpenEndedGetsBudget`, `TestProvisionContextZeroTimeoutFallsBack`, `TestProvisionJSONMarshalError`.

100% coverage on every added line (`provisionContext`, `provisionJSONWithHeaders`, `jsonBodyReader`, `New`, `WithTimeout` all 100%; the only changed line in the shared `doWithClient` loop body — `hc.Do(req)` — is covered).

## Docs

README **Provisioning** section gains a "Timeouts: provisioning runs longer than reads" subsection; **Client configuration** `WithTimeout` comment updated; CHANGELOG Unreleased/Fixed entry added.

## Gate

- `go build ./...` ✓  `go vet ./... ./examples/...` ✓
- `go test ./... -race -count=1` ✓ (CI's exact command)
- `golangci-lint run ./...` → **0 issues**
- `gofmt` (real, `$GOROOT/bin/gofmt`) clean on all authored/edited files
- `go test -tags integration -run TestProdIntegration` ✓ (read-only prod checks, no regression)

author: nealcaren
body:
Phase 6 of the estimator-conformance program, and the close of the original motivating gap: the keyword/seeded/anchored Dirichlet models could not do held-out inference. They now implement `transform`.

## What changed
Added `transform(data, *, iterations=100, burn_in=10, num_samples=10, sample_interval=5, seed=None) -> (n, K)` to **KeyATM, SeededLDA, SAGE, PA, PT**, each reusing the existing `transform_gibbs` helper (per-doc collapsed Gibbs holding the fitted phi fixed):
- **KeyATM** — effective P(w|topic) (keyword switch already marginalized); estimated/symmetric alpha.
- **SeededLDA** — fitted phi (seed boost baked in); symmetric alpha.
- **SAGE** — group-averaged topic-word via the existing `topic_marginal()`; baseline (covariate-free) projection.
- **PT** — fitted phi; pseudo-document layer is training-only.
- **PA** — projects onto the fitted sub-topics (returns `(n, num_sub)`), marginalizing the super-topic layer.

Each docstring states its held-out approximation honestly.

## Payoff (loop closed)
`topica.perplexity` and `topica.eval_heldout` now run for KeyATM and SeededLDA (they previously raised "no transform"). `composition_theta`/`predicted_prevalence` already worked via Phase 5 draws; these five are now fully usable in every held-out / uncertainty facility.

## Conformance
- 5 `transform` gaps removed from `KNOWN_GAPS`; contract doc updated (only HLDA and DTM remain structurally transform-exempt).
- Stub updated. `tests/test_phase6_transform.py`: shapes/row-sums/determinism for all 5 + perplexity/eval_heldout payoff for KeyATM/SeededLDA.

## Validation
- `cargo test --lib`: 49 passed. Full suite: 1547 passed, 12 skipped, 15 xfailed (was 20; 5 closed). `tests/test_conformance.py` 5 cells now pass. `mkdocs build --strict` clean.

Conformance now: **15 gaps left** — Phase 4 (neural/cluster `coherence`/`save`/`load`/`doc_names`) and Phase 2b (neural `iters`).

author: justin13888
body:
## What

Fifth PR in the **on-device ML stack** (stacked on #339). Adds the `capsule-core::ml` orchestration layer — the inference seam, the pipeline that ties a runner to the signed lifecycle, and the standalone algorithms `ai.md` specifies.

### The seam (`ml::runner`)
- **`ModelRunner` trait** — `embed_image` / `embed_text` / `detect` / `model(task)` / `platform()`. Real per-platform runners (ONNX/CoreML/NNAPI, default-off weight-fetching feature) implement it.
- **`FixtureRunner`** — deterministic, weightless. Expands SHA-256 into L2-normalized vectors, so identical content embeds identically — semantic matches are testable with **no model weights**. Mirrors `ReferenceAuthority` standing in for live MLS behind `AlbumAuthority`.

### Orchestration (`ml::orchestrator`)
- **`embed_and_store`** — run the canonical model over an asset → signed embedding derivative (#339) + index entry (#336). **Refuses a non-canonical runner** (embedding-provenance invariant enforced at the boundary).
- **`auto_tag`** — zero-shot tagging by *reusing* the semantic embeddings (image-vs-label cosine over a threshold) → AI tags (#338); no separate classifier, per `ai.md`.
- **`semantic_search`** — natural-language query → KNN in the current `(platform, version)` partition.
- **Device policy** — `choose_batch_mode` (horizontal/vertical by RAM), `micro_batch_size` (1/4/8 ceiling), `should_pause_for_heat` (thermal throttle).

### Algorithms
- **`ml::video`** — video-as-sparse-photos: keyframe sampling at 10/50/90% per scene + Laplacian-variance blur rejection.
- **`ml::reid`** — IoU, cosine similarity, face↔body linking (IoU > 0.7), cosine-threshold pseudo-labeling.

## Design conformance (`ai.md`)

Maps to *Semantic Indexing*, *Image Categorization & Tagging* (zero-shot reuse), *Model Batching*, *Video-as-Sparse-Photos*, *Re-ID & Pseudo-Labeling*, and the *Algorithm correctness* / *Thermal throttle / batching bound* validation bullets. Per-platform bit-exact inference parity stays deferred (needs real runners + field testing).

## Testing

18 tests: fixture determinism + content-equality embedding + canonical declaration; batching/micro-batch/thermal policy; keyframe timestamps + blur rejection; IoU/cosine/linking/pseudo-label; and orchestrator smoke (embed→semantic-search match, non-canonical runner refused, zero-shot auto_tag lands in the AI namespace). Full `cargo test -p capsule-core` → **323 passed**. `clippy --workspace --exclude capsule-sdk -D warnings` + `fmt --check` clean.

## Stack
#335 ← #336 ← #338 ← #339 ← **this** ← regeneration + bounded E2E + demo.

author: romanornr
body:
# Rewriting the Relative Rotation Graph from scratch

This PR replaces the old script entirely. The old chart *looked* like an RRG, but two of its three core properties were broken, and it silently produced no data when run after mid-2024. This description explains what an RRG actually is, what was wrong, and why the new design is shaped the way it is. If you have never touched an RRG before, you should be able to follow all of it.

## What an RRG is, in one minute

An RRG answers one question: **which of my holdings are gaining strength against the benchmark, and which are losing it?**

Every symbol becomes one dot on a 2D plane:

- **x-axis (JdK RS-Ratio):** is this symbol in a relative *uptrend* vs the benchmark? Right of center means yes.
- **y-axis (JdK RS-Momentum):** is that relative trend *accelerating* or *decelerating*? Above center means accelerating.

```
                      RS-Momentum
                          ^
              IMPROVING   |   LEADING
           (still behind, | (outperforming
            but catching  |  and still
            up)           |  accelerating)
        <-----------------+-----------------> RS-Ratio
              LAGGING     |   WEAKENING
           (underperform- | (still ahead,
            ing and       |  but running out
            falling)      |  of steam)
                          v
```

Each dot drags a "tail" of its recent history. The famous property of RRGs is that these tails rotate **clockwise**:

```
        IMPROVING ----> LEADING
            ^              |
            |              v
        LAGGING  <---- WEAKENING
```

Acceleration fades before the trend does, and the trend fades before outright weakness sets in. That ordering is not a market mystery. It falls straight out of the math, as bug 2 below shows.

## The three bugs, and what each one teaches

### Bug 1: normalizing over the full sample lets the future leak into the past

The old code z-scored each symbol's indicator using the mean and standard deviation of the **entire downloaded history**:

```
old:    |------------------ whole sample -------------------|
                    ^ point at time t
        the mean subtracted at t includes data from AFTER t

new:    |#### trailing 14 bars ####| t
        the point at t uses only what was knowable at t
```

Two things go wrong, and both are instructive:

1. **Lookahead bias.** Every historical point on the tail gets repainted by data that did not exist yet. The chart shows a history nobody could have seen in real time. This is the same class of bug that makes naive backtests look magically profitable.
2. **Forced re-centering.** Subtracting a symbol's own full-sample mean drags its average position to the exact center of the chart. A sector that beat the benchmark *every single week* still spends half its time in the "Lagging" quadrant, by construction. The quadrants become decoration instead of information.

The rewrite normalizes with a rolling, trailing-only window, and a regression test asserts that the value at bar t is identical whether or not later data exists.

### Bug 2: the y-axis must be the derivative of the x-axis, or nothing rotates

Why do RRG tails rotate clockwise at all? Because RS-Momentum is defined as the **rate of change of RS-Ratio**. A rate of change always peaks before the thing it measures:

```
RS-Ratio       ____/^^^^\____         peaks LATE
RS-Momentum  __/^^^^\____/^^^         peaks EARLY (it is the slope of the line above)
```

Plot a value on x and its own slope on y and you get rotation for free. It is the same reason (sin t, cos t) traces a circle: cosine is the derivative of sine.

The old code instead computed momentum from the raw relative-strength line, with the same lookback used for the ratio. Both axes became near-duplicate measurements of the same thing, and the dots smeared along a diagonal:

```
   old: x and y measure the same     new: y is the slope of x

        y      .                          y    .----.
        |    .                            |   /      \
        |  .                              |   \      /
        |._______ x                       |    '----'____ x

       (diagonal smear,                      (actual
        no rotation)                          rotation)
```

StockCharts' own documentation calls RS-Momentum "an indicator of an indicator (RS-Ratio)". The rewrite computes it that way, and a test verifies the phase relationship: on a cyclical input, momentum must cross its centerline before ratio does.

### Bug 3: hardcoded dates rot

The old script downloaded a fixed date range but filtered relative to today:

```
downloaded:    [2023-08-07 .......... 2024-07-22]
filtered to:                                         [today-150 ...... today]
intersection:                                        (empty)
```

It worked the week it was written and never again. In the rewrite every date derives from `Sys.Date()`, and the download window is sized from the indicator parameters instead of being a magic number.

## The formulas used

The exact JdK formulas are proprietary. Bloomberg and StockCharts license them from RRG Research, and they have never been published. This PR uses the standard public approximation, on weekly bars:

```
RS          = 100 * price / benchmark
RS-Ratio    = 100 + rolling z-score of RS               (trailing window only)
RS-Momentum = 100 + rolling z-score of ROC(RS-Ratio)    (trailing window only)
```

Known, honest limitation: the licensed indicator applies heavier trend smoothing than this, so terminal RRGs look smoother than ours. That smoothness is bought with lag. StockCharts documents roughly ten weeks between a relative-strength peak and the corresponding RS-Ratio centerline cross.

## How the code is shaped now

The old version was one 200-line script where config, networking, math, and plotting all shared global variables. You could not reuse the math, test it, or feed it non-Yahoo data without editing the file. The rewrite is layered, and each layer only knows about the one below it:

```
main.r           config + four calls, nothing else
   |
   v
R/data.R         fetch_prices(), to_weekly()      <- the ONLY code that touches a network
   |
   v
R/rrg.R          rrg(prices, benchmark) -> an "rrg" object (trails + parameters)
   |             pure math, runs on ANY price matrix: Yahoo, CSV, synthetic
   v
R/plot.R         rrg_plot(g) / plot(g)            <- pixels, and only pixels
```

An RRG is now a value you can hold, print, and inspect, not just a side effect of running a script:

```
> print(g)
Relative Rotation Graph vs SPY (as of 2026-06-09)
window = 14, roc_period = 4, trail = 10 bars

 symbol rs_ratio rs_momentum  quadrant
    QQQ   100.92       98.93 Weakening
    VNQ    99.80      102.35 Improving
    XLE    99.32      100.62 Improving
    XLV   100.01      101.28   Leading
```

## Proof, not promises

`Rscript tests/test-rrg.R` runs 12 offline tests on synthetic data, no network needed. The two that matter most are direct regression tests for bugs 1 and 2:

- **No lookahead:** compute the metrics on a full series and on truncated copies of it; the overlapping values must be identical.
- **Rotation:** on a cyclical relative-strength series, RS-Momentum must cross 100 before RS-Ratio does.

Plus the basics: a steady outperformer must sit right of center, a steady underperformer left of it, quadrant labels must map correctly, and the object contract (columns, trail lengths, error cases) is pinned down.

Two edge cases flagged by review bots are also covered: a flat relative-strength window (rolling standard deviation of zero) yields NA instead of Inf, and weekly bars exclude the week still in progress, so a mid-week run cannot shift the head dot with a partial close.

`Rscript main.r` was run end to end on R 4.6.0: it downloads QQQ/XLV/XLE/VNQ vs SPY, prints the table above, and saves `rrg.png` with trails rotating through all four quadrants.

Routes with parameters like :version now correctly match decimal numbers such as 1.5.1 and semantic version strings.

Previously, a route like `Routes::map('download/:version', callback);` would work with `/download/release` but not `/download/1.5.1`.

author: ivandanielgg-sketch
body: ## Problem When creating an ECOVIS project from the admin modal, the project was inserted in the database but the UI showed **"Proyecto ECOVIS no encontrado"**, kept the modal open, and allowed duplicate submissions. ## Root cause `POST /api/ecovis/projects` wraps inserts in `db.transaction()` and uses the returned `lastInsertRowid` to fetch the created row via `getEcovisProjectOrFail(projectId)`. On PostgreSQL (production), the `betterSqlite3Adapter` transaction wrapper called the callback but **did not return its result**, unlike native `better-sqlite3`. So `projectId` was `undefined`, the insert + movement still committed, and the response handler failed with 404. SQLite (local dev) was unaffected because native `better-sqlite3` returns the callback result correctly. ## Changes - **Backend:** Fix `transaction()` in `betterSqlite3Adapter.js` to return the callback result and forward arguments (matches better-sqlite3 behavior). The ECOVIS project create endpoint already uses a transaction for project + movement inserts. - **Frontend:** Disable "Guardar proyecto ECOVIS" while the request is in flight; re-enable on error or when resetting the form. Strip empty `id` from create payloads. ## Testing - `node --test test/db-adapter.test.js test/ecovis.test.js` passes - Manual `POST /api/ecovis/projects` on SQLite returns 201 with project `id`

author: irvingoujatdevolution
body:
## What

Everything from the v0.2–v1.0 roadmap on top of the v0.1 base, e2e-verified (9 Playwright tests across WebGPU + WebGL2 projects, 20 host unit tests) and live-verified inside the IronVNC (VNC) and IronRDP (RDP) web clients behind a local Devolutions Gateway.

### v0.2 — performance
- **Packed-path gather heuristic**: narrow tall rects CPU-gather tightly into a lazily-grown storage-buffer tail instead of uploading the full row span (only when span > 2x tight). Demo workload upload: **1215 → 95 KiB/frame**.
- **A/B benchmark vs Canvas2D** (`?renderer=canvas2d`): identical workload through the tuned pack+putImageData path. Measured (Chrome 149, Intel Gen12): **GPU 0.53–0.87 vs Canvas2D 0.57–1.11 CPU-ms/frame, ~55% less upload**, same 60 fps.

### v0.3 — composition
- **Cursor/overlay layer**: separate RGBA texture, straight-alpha blend in the blit pass; moves are one uniform write (no uploads, no framebuffer churn).
- **External image ingestion**: `import_image_bitmap` (+ `import_video_frame` under `--cfg web_sys_unstable_apis`) via `copyExternalImageToTexture`; caller-sequenced ordering documented; persistent textures gained `COPY_DST | RENDER_ATTACHMENT`.

### v0.4 — native + video formats
- **Native window target**: `Surface::new_windowed` (raw-window-handle) + winit example (300-frame smoke test); GPU core is now platform-neutral, logic tests run on host.
- **I420 planar YUV**: BT.601 in the unpack pass, even-coordinate rect expansion, per-plane span uploads.

### v1.0 — coverage
- **New packed formats**: Rgb565 / Rgb555 / Gray8 / Gray16 via one generalized unpack shader.
- **WebGL2 fallback** (`webgl` feature): WebGPU probed at instance creation (web display handle, downlevel limits); compute-less adapters take a CPU-expand path. Dedicated e2e project verifies pixel parity with `navigator.gpu` removed.
- **API change**: `PixelFormat::bytes_per_pixel()` → `Option<usize>`; use `frame_len(w, h)` for buffer sizing.
- DPI-aware presentation demonstrated (`?hidpi=1`) and e2e-verified at deviceScaleFactor 2.

## Not included (documented in README)
- Native persistent-mapped staging ring (`Buffering::Double`).
- Worker-shaped Iron* clients (renderer is worker-proven; needs an iron-remote-desktop framework change).

author: fukusaka
body:
## Motivation

A capability-tier integration test failed deterministically on four-CPU hosts (five out of five runs) while passing on large hosts, and tracing exposed a cross-connection data-theft bug in the registered-file slot lifecycle. Teardown unregistered the transport's fixed-file slot unconditionally — while the just-cancelled recv could still be in flight, because `IORING_OP_ASYNC_CANCEL` is asynchronous. The freed slot was immediately registered by the next accepted connection, and a poll-armed request re-resolves its slot index on wakeup: the dead connection's stale recv then read the NEXT connection's bytes, and its kept callback's not-opened branch silently discarded them — the new connection's request vanished without a trace. On large hosts the cancel's terminal CQE happens to win the race against slot reuse, which is why the bug stayed hidden; on CPU-starved hosts (including typical CI runners) it loses deterministically.

## 動機

capability-tier の integration test が 4-CPU ホストで決定論的に fail し(5/5)、大型ホストでは pass する — このトレースから registered-file slot のライフサイクルに**接続間データ横取りバグ**が見つかりました。teardown は transport の fixed-file slot を無条件に unregister していましたが、`IORING_OP_ASYNC_CANCEL` は非同期であり、cancel したばかりの recv はまだ in flight であり得ます。解放された slot は次に accept された接続が即座に register し、poll 待ちの request は wakeup 時に slot index を再解決するため、**死んだ接続の stale recv が次の接続のバイト列を読み取り**、その kept callback の not-opened branch が黙って破棄 — 新しい接続のリクエストが痕跡なく消えます。大型ホストでは cancel の terminal CQE が slot 再利用とのレースにたまたま勝つためバグは隠れ、CPU 枯渇ホスト(典型的な CI runner を含む)では決定論的に負けます。

## Modification

- Count the in-flight SQEs that reference the transport's fixed-file slot — recv in all three modes, the async send / writev / zero-copy sends, and the direct-alloc shutdown (`POLL_ADD` uses the raw fd and is excluded) — incrementing at submit and decrementing at each terminal CQE (`F_MORE` clear for multishot; every CQE for single-shot ops; the once-per-op completion callback for zero-copy sends).
- Teardown unregisters the slot immediately when nothing is in flight; otherwise it sets a release-pending flag and the last terminal CQE performs the deferred unregister. The terminal-CQE bookkeeping runs before the callbacks' not-opened early returns so post-teardown CQEs still count down.
- Three seam tests over a fake-backed registry pin the deferral (teardown with an in-flight recv must not write the unregister; the terminal CQE must), the immediate path (nothing in flight), and the completed-before-teardown path.

### Design decisions

- **This is the same ownership rule the recv buffer already follows**: a resource an in-flight SQE references — the destination buffer then, the registered-file slot now — may not be released or reused until that SQE's terminal CQE. The slot case is strictly worse than a leak: reuse hands the stale request a live socket belonging to someone else.
- **A counter, not per-op slot tracking.** All of a transport's fixed-file SQEs reference the same single slot, so a count of outstanding references is sufficient and stays allocation-free on the hot path (one integer increment per submit).
- **Raw-fd close stays immediate.** The kernel's registered table holds its own file reference, so closing the raw fd at teardown remains safe; only the table slot's reuse needed sequencing.

## 変更内容

- transport の fixed-file slot を参照する in-flight SQE を数える — recv(3 モード全て)、async send / writev / zero-copy sends、direct-alloc shutdown(`POLL_ADD` は raw fd 使用のため除外)。submit で increment、各 terminal CQE で decrement(multishot は `F_MORE` clear、single-shot 系は毎 CQE、zero-copy send は op ごと 1 回の完了 callback)。
- teardown は in-flight ゼロなら即 unregister、そうでなければ release-pending flag を立て、最後の terminal CQE が遅延 unregister を実行する。terminal-CQE の bookkeeping は callback の not-opened early return より前に走らせ、teardown 後の CQE でも count down されるようにする。
- fake-backed registry 上の seam test 3 件で、遅延(in-flight recv がいる teardown は unregister を書き込まない / terminal CQE が書き込む)、即時 path(in-flight なし)、teardown 前完了 path を pin。

### 設計判断

- **recv buffer が既に従っている所有権規律と同一**: in-flight SQE が参照する資源 —(先に確立した)宛先 buffer、今回の registered-file slot — は、その SQE の terminal CQE まで解放・再利用してはならない。slot の場合は leak より厳密に悪い: 再利用は stale request に**他人の生きた socket** を渡す。
- **per-op の slot 追跡でなく counter。** transport の fixed-file SQE はすべて同一の 1 slot を参照するため未完参照数のカウントで十分であり、hot path は allocation-free(submit ごとに整数 increment 1 回)。
- **raw fd の close は即時のまま。** kernel の registered table は独自の file reference を保持するため teardown での raw fd close は安全 — 順序制御が必要だったのは table slot の再利用のみ。

## Test plan

- Red-Green verified, twice over:
  - seam: the deferral test fails on the pre-fix code (the slot is unregistered while the recv is in flight) and passes after; full io_uring module suite green.
  - integration: the capability-profile echo test is deterministically red on a four-CPU host before this fix (five out of five runs fail with the second connection's request silently consumed) and green after (five out of five pass). This is the test that exposed the bug and blocks CI on such runners.
- Full aggregate pre-merge gates (`-Ptls -Pbenchmark`, all detekt targets, all test targets, Dokka): BUILD SUCCESSFUL on a Linux host (47 executed / 758 up-to-date) and a macOS host (40 executed / 788 up-to-date; the diff is in the Linux-only module).
- Hot-path regression A/B (one integer increment per SQE submit): Linux host, 32-core, loopback, `raw-io-uring` `/hello`, wrk 16t/500c, `BENCH_RUNS=3` median, temperature capture — baseline 2,968,587 req/s [2,950,459–2,978,828] vs this branch 2,955,554 req/s [2,951,116–2,955,698] — ranges overlap, tied (-0.4 %).

author: calebsargeant
body:
Three follow-ups requested after the stack went green: collect the Pi's logs, expose Grafana, and back up MinIO offsite.

## 1. ff-pi1 logs — Grafana Alloy
fluent-bit can't run on ff-pi1: the Pi's arm64 kernel uses **16KB pages** and the image's jemalloc is built for 4KB (`<jemalloc>: Unsupported system page size`). **Vector** would risk the same (it can use jemalloc), so the safe pick is a **Go** shipper. **Grafana Alloy** (the supported, Loki-native successor to Promtail) is page-size-agnostic.

`kubernetes/apps/alloy/` — a Pi-pinned DaemonSet shipping container logs to `loki-gateway` with the **same label schema as fluent-bit** (`cluster=firefly`, `k8s_namespace_name/pod_name/container_name`), with `job="alloy"` to distinguish ff-pi1 from fluent-bit's ff-vm1. **Verified live**: 17 Pi namespaces now queryable in Loki under `{job="alloy"}`.

> ⚠️ ff-pi1 is **~100% memory-committed** by over-provisioned non-observability apps (nextcloud 759Mi, mariadb/n8n/homeassistant/atlantis 512Mi each…). Alloy runs **BestEffort** (memory request `0` + 192Mi limit) so it schedules; right-sizing those apps per KRR would free room for a proper reservation.

## 2. Grafana ingress — grafana.sargeant.co
`grafana.ingress.enabled` via Traefik, matching the `radarr.sargeant.co` pattern (cert-manager `letsencrypt-dns`, `websecure`, `sargeant.co` + `sargeant.local`, TLS). external-dns auto-publishes the record.

## 3. MinIO → OCI backup
Daily `minio-backup` CronJob `mc mirror`s `thanos-metrics` + `loki-chunks` + `loki-ruler` to OCI Object Storage (additive — keeps history even after source compaction), using the same OCI S3 creds CNPG uses (`minio-backup-oci` ExternalSecret from vault `backup-oci-s3-credentials`).
- **Terraform:** adds `minio-backups` to the `backups` module's `bucket_names` (creates the bucket + auto-scopes the IAM policy). This applies via Atlantis on merge — the first CronJob run is 04:00, after which the bucket exists.

## Longhorn — recommendation: skip it for observability
The big PVCs (Prometheus/Loki/Thanos) are reconstructable from MinIO, and MinIO is now backed up to OCI. Replicating them to the small ff-pi1 via Longhorn adds I/O + risk for little gain. Keep `local-path` (ff-vm1) + the OCI backup as the durability layer. (Details in the doc.)

## Notes
- Alloy is already running live (validated). Flux's `prod-alloy` adopts it on merge.
- Ordering: the k8s CronJob is harmless until the terraform bucket exists; it retries.

author: markheath
body:
Adds the NAudio 3 software sampler: a pure-managed, cross-platform, AOT-safe instrument that plays MIDI through SoundFont 2 (`.sf2`) and SFZ (`.sfz`) files, or a single sample mapped across the keyboard. Design notes in `Docs/Architecture/SamplerDesign.md`; user-facing tutorial (including the explicit supported/unsupported feature statement) in `Docs/Sampler.md`.

## What's in the package

- **New `NAudio.Sampler` package** — `SoundFontSampler`, `SfzSampler` and `SingleSampleSampler` over one shared `SamplerEngine`: pooled voices with Hermite-interpolated looping playback (stereo, loop-seam crossfade), DAHDSR amplitude + modulation envelopes, two LFOs, modulated resonant filters, per-region EQ, the full SF2 modulator engine (default + file modulators per §8.4/§9.5), reverb/chorus send buses, voice stealing with click-free fades, exclusive/choke groups, sustain pedal, RPN 0 bend range, GM/GS/XG percussion handling.
- **SFZ support** — parser (`#define`/`#include`/`<control>`), full Tier 1 + Tier 2 opcode coverage including triggers, keyswitches, round-robin, random layers, crossfades, CC gating, `amp_velcurve_N`, `off_mode`, `polyphony`, WAV `smpl`-chunk loops, and FLAC/Ogg samples via `NAudio.SoundFile`. Unsupported opcodes are listed explicitly in the docs.
- **MIDI playback hosts in `NAudio.Midi`** — a new `IMidiInstrument` seam (`ISampleProvider` + `ProcessMidiEvent`) with `MidiFileSequence`, `SequencedMidiPlayer` (sample-accurate timeline playback on the sequencing core), `OfflineMidiRenderer` (faster-than-realtime WAV render) and `LiveMidiInstrument` (lock-free live-input bridge). The seam is deliberately instrument-agnostic so the VST3 host work can reuse these unchanged.
- **DSP primitives in `NAudio.Core`** — `InterpolatingSampleReader`, `DahdsrEnvelope`, `SynthMath`, `SendBus`, plus additive extensions to `Lfo` and `BiQuadFilter` (state-preserving retune, block transforms). All additions are additive; existing `BiQuadFilter.Transform` is untouched.
- **Three WPF demo panels** — SoundFont/MIDI player (live + offline render), live MIDI sampler with on-screen keyboard, and a single-sample editor with draggable waveform loop markers.

## Quality measures

The branch went through a multi-pass review (SF2/SFZ spec conformance, DSP correctness, architecture, performance, test quality) and the findings were fixed on-branch:

- **Correctness**: spec-faithful generator accumulation (§9.4), modulator merging and source curves (§8.2/§9.5 — including two documented SF2 spec typos), constant-dB envelope rates, zero-rising LFO start, Butterworth-referenced filter Q with gain compensation, key-tracked envelope times, pedal/release-trigger semantics, bank-select MSB mapping.
- **Performance** (measured by the committed `[Explicit]` benchmarks, Release): ~12× realtime at 64 busy voices (filter + both LFOs + sends), **zero heap allocations** in steady-state rendering and in note-on/off cycles (CI-guarded), lock-free and allocation-free sequenced playback. Voice resources are pooled and persistent; presets pre-warm at construction; modulation runs at control rate with block-advanced sources proven bit-exact against per-sample processing.
- **Tests**: ~470 new tests across `NAudio.Core.Tests` and the new `NAudio.Sampler.Tests` (1,413 + 204 total, all green, ~10 s combined on Linux) — deterministic offline-render assertions, bit-exactness equivalence sweeps for every fast path, segmented-vs-monolithic render bit-identity, and zero-allocation guards. No binary test assets; SF2 files are built in memory.

## Breaking change

`SoundFont.SampleHeader`'s public fields became properties (binary-breaking for compiled consumers; source-compatible for normal use). Noted under Breaking changes in RELEASE_NOTES.md.

## Out of scope (documented)

NRPN §9.6 generator control, GS/XG SysEx mode detection (a CC0 = 120/127 heuristic is included), windowed-sinc interpolation, disk streaming for very large libraries — all listed as unsupported in `Docs/Sampler.md` and tracked in the design doc.

body:
In a backgrounded `claude --bg /flow <key> --auto` run the orchestrator's
cwd is pinned at the repo root and the bg-isolation guard rejects the Write
tool inside the .flow/worktrees worktree. Do-loop step d (the subagent and
skill capture sub-branches) tells the orchestrator to write the stage .out
with the Write tool to a path inside the worktree, so the capture stalls.

Document the fallback: SKILL.md step d now points each sub-branch at a
collision-safe heredoc recipe (kept terse so SKILL.md stays thin), and the
recipe itself lives in references/verb-do.md under a new "Orchestrator .out
capture when Write is blocked" subsection. A quoted heredoc with a long
random sentinel neutralizes $/backtick/\ in the body and avoids early
termination, restoring the safety the Write-tool path had.

Prose-only; seam_check green, no scripts touched.

body:
Adds support for the Watts WFHT-RF and WFHC-MASTERH&C-RF wireless underfloor heating thermostats.

The decoder extracts the device ID, ambient temperature, target setpoint, heat/cool mode, pairing state, and call-for-heat status. Frame integrity is verified using CRC-8 and CRC-16/CMS checksums.

The observed A-B-A burst behavior during setpoint changes and the pairing flag have been documented.

Corresponding test captures and documentation will be submitted separately to the rtl_433_tests repository.

author: mattcheramie
body:
The Airspy R2 / Mini are real-sampling receivers: the firmware streams
bare ADC samples (unpacked uint16, 12-bit, DC at 2048) at twice the
configured IQ rate. The driver was reading those real samples as
interleaved I/Q pairs, so two adjacent real samples were paired as I
and Q. The reporter saw the signature exactly: ~+78 deg quadrature
imbalance and ~3.3 dB image rejection, and nothing locked.

Add a host-side real-to-IQ converter (Fs/4 translation + half-band
Hilbert pair, decimate-by-two) and feed the bulk-IN stream through it,
matching what libairspy does in its IQ sample modes. The converter is
stateful across USB packets so there is no discontinuity at buffer
boundaries. Implemented independently from standard DSP; the half-band
coefficients are a canonical filter design.

Drops the dead INT16_IQ path (setSampleTypeInt16, sample-type consts,
decodeInt16IQ). New unit tests assert 2:1 decimation, packet-boundary
continuity, and — reproducing the issue's metrics — phase imbalance
< 1 deg and image rejection > 40 dB (measured ~70 dB).

### Motivation
- Trenne Exportlogik aus `SchedulerService` in ein eigenständiges Modul, um Zuständigkeiten zu entkoppeln und Wartbarkeit zu verbessern.
- Biete echte PDF-Exporte für Wochen-, Tages- und Mitarbeiterpläne samt Kopfzeile (Firma, Zeitraum, Erstelldatum, Benutzer) für professionelle Ausgaben.
- Ergänze Datenschutz- und Anzeigeoptionen (Stundenlohn, Abwesenheitsgrund, nur veröffentlichte Schichten) damit Exporte konfigurierbar und GDPR-freundlich sind.
- Decke Edge-Cases ab (leere Pläne, Sonderzeichen) und sichere die Änderungen durch Tests ab.

### Description

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The app was hitting "Connection reset by peer" errors from Postgres because Prisma's default connection pool (10 connections) was being exhausted by the combined load of HTTP requests and persistent WebSocket connections. With 97 connections visible in the logs, the pool was saturating and dropping connections, causing high latency and WebSocket failures across all endpoints.

## Solution

Added a private `appendPoolParams` helper in `PrismaService` that appends `connection_limit=20`, `pool_timeout=10`, and `statement_cache_size=0` to the database URL at construction time for any standard PostgreSQL connection. Prisma Accelerate URLs (`prisma://...`) are left untouched since they manage pooling externally. This approach keeps the pool configuration in code alongside the service that owns it, rather than relying on the environment variable being set correctly in every deployment environment.

### Changes
- **Modified** `apps/backend/src/modules/providers-modules/prisma/prisma.service.ts`

author: mikeishiring
body:
## Summary

Fork port of dmarzzz/shape-rotator-os#262, with `cohort-surface.json` regenerated against this fork's `main`.

Person and team dossier timelines fill their capped transcript slots with the *oldest* transcripts, so heavily-mentioned people never surface the newest sessions (e.g. the weekly WDYDLW standup recaps). This flips the pre-cap sort to date-descending within each priority tier so the cap keeps the newest items, while source-named transcripts still rank first.

## Why

`buildPersonTimeline` (and its twin `buildTeamTimeline`) in `scripts/build-bundles.js` rank transcript-derived items by `_priority` (source-named 3 > direct-hit 2 > team-context 1), then by date **ascending**, then cap with `uniqueTranscriptItems.slice(0, 6)`. For anyone matched in more than six transcripts, the cap keeps the oldest and drops the newest — dossiers go stale by construction, and every new weekly transcript makes it worse.

The pre-cap sort only controls *which* items survive, not display order — the final timeline is re-sorted ascending by `sortTimeline` either way — so the flip is safe for presentation. Full bug walkthrough and the albiona-hoti repro against the WDYDLW ingestion data are in dmarzzz/shape-rotator-os#262.

## Changes

- `scripts/build-bundles.js`: sort date-descending within each `_priority` tier in both `buildPersonTimeline` and `buildTeamTimeline` (the same copy-pasted comparator in each). Source-named transcripts still outrank direct hits and team context.
- `apps/os/src/cohort-surface.json`: regenerated **against this fork's data** (26 teams / 13 events here vs 25/12 upstream, so the artifact intentionally differs from the upstream PR). Thirteen person timelines (albiona-hoti, andrew-forman, andrew-miller, dmarz, hunter-horsfall, james-barnes, josh-chang, lsdan, novel-tokens, qendresa-hoti, quasimatt, roman-svistel, will-cory) and seven team timelines (dcnet, etherea, feedling, searxng-wth-frnds, shape-rotator-os, teesql, teleport-router) swap their oldest items for newer ones; every other section is byte-identical.

## Testing

On this branch (this fork's tree): `npm run check:cohort` green, `npm test` 8/8, longest person timeline 27 (≤ 28 cap).

## Prompt your agent with

```text
In scripts/build-bundles.js, buildPersonTimeline and buildTeamTimeline collect transcript-derived timeline items, sort them by _priority (source-named 3 > direct-hit 2 > team-context 1) and then by date ASCENDING within each tier, then cap with uniqueTranscriptItems.slice(0, 6). For people/teams matched in more than 6 transcripts the cap therefore keeps the OLDEST transcripts and silently drops the newest sessions (e.g. weekly standup recaps). Fix by sorting date-DESCENDING within each priority tier in BOTH functions, keeping the priority ordering, the dedup-by-href pass, the 6-item transcript cap, and the overall 28-item timeline cap. Then run npm run build:cohort to regenerate apps/os/src/cohort-surface.json and commit it, and verify npm run check:cohort and npm test stay green.
```

## Summary
Agrega 6 categorías para gastos personales que el Art. 697 del Código Fiscal de Panamá define como NO deducibles:
- `gastos_alimentacion`, `gastos_vestimenta`, `pension_alimenticia`
- `manutencion`, `viajes_recreativos`, `fiestas_entretenimiento`

**Para el usuario:** elige "Manutención" → sistema marca personal → ve el gasto en el dashboard y estadísticas, no se cuela al cierre fiscal.

author: onedr0p
body:
## Summary

Maintainer feedback (Discord, following #163): the icon-only "open on the forge" link on the PR card — between the signal badges and the disclosure chevron, with a boxy hover background and tooltip overlay — read as noise. It was the row's one hoverable control sitting among inert badges, and "makes no sense" there. Requested placement: in the row's dropdown, on the merge-command bar, to the right of the copy button.

A second meta-row nit rode along: the label pills rendered taller than the resource/image signal badges (heights were emergent from line-height/font metrics, which differ between the icon-bearing badges and dot+text labels across browser/font stacks).

## Changes

**Forge link**
- **Row**: the `ForgeLink` is removed; the card keeps only the inert signal badges plus the disclosure chevron.
- **Panel**: a new `.pv-actions` row in the expanded preview carries the merge-command chip (spanning the bar) with the forge link at the far right, after the copy button — restyled to the copy button's quiet idiom (muted glyph, colors on hover, **no padded hover box**).
- **No merge command** (merged PRs, or the feature off): the action row degrades to just the link, pinned right — verified against the merged-PR fixture.
- PRs without a rendered summary have no expander, so no list-side link; the review header's numbered forge link still covers them.
- The mobile rule that sized the row link's touch target to the disclosure column is removed with the row placement.

**Pill heights**
- The whole meta-row pill family (`.badge`, `.tag`, `.label`) is pinned to `height: 20px` with `line-height: 1`, so UA font metrics can't re-inflate any of them unevenly.

## Tests

- The landing-list test asserts the card shell carries **no** forge link and that every meta-row pill measures the same height.
- The expander test asserts the panel link's `href`/`target`/tooltip, icon-only rendering, and that it sits geometrically right of the copy button.
- The merged-PR test asserts the link-only action row (no merge command).
- The forge-link assertions fail against the previous markup. (The pill assertion locks the contract — Chromium happened to render them equal already; the skew shows on other font stacks.)
- `svelte-check` 0 errors; all 63 Playwright tests pass.
