author: bardiakoopah
body:
## Summary

Training any VLM (vision LoRA or vision-frozen) on `unslothai/unsloth-zoo:main` crashes before step 1 with:

```
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```

raised from `mlx_vlm/models/qwen3_vl/processing_qwen3_vl.py:193` (`C, H, W = image.shape`).

## Root cause

Two VLM batch collators in `unsloth_zoo/mlx/utils.py` build `all_images` as a **list of lists**, one inner list per sample:

- `_collate_vlm_batch` (line 2422, messages-based path)
- `_collate_vlm_prompt_completion_batch` (line 2335, prompt+completion path)

Both do:
```python
images = _extract_vlm_images(item, messages, image_size)  # returns [PIL_img, ...]
all_images.append(images)                                  # nested
```

But mlx-vlm 0.6.x's processor iterates the outer list and calls `_process_one` on each element, expecting each element to be a *single image* (3-D ndarray or PIL.Image):

```python
# mlx_vlm/models/qwen3_vl/processing_qwen3_vl.py
if not isinstance(images, list):
    images = [images]
imgs = [
    img if (isinstance(img, np.ndarray) and img.ndim == 3) else _to_numpy_image(img)
    for img in images
]
for v in imgs:
    patches, thw = self._process_one(v, **image_kwargs)
```

When the outer element is a list, `_to_numpy_image` produces a 4-D `(1, C, H, W)` ndarray and `_process_one` crashes unpacking it into 3 dims.

## Fix

Use `extend` instead of `append` per sample in both collators so `all_images` is a flat list across the batch.

Image order is preserved (texts and images are built sample-by-sample in lockstep), and the rendered text's `<image>` placeholders pair positionally with the flat image list as mlx-vlm expects.

## Batch-shape verification

| Batch | Images / sample | `all_images` after extend |
|---|---|---|
| bs=1 | 1 | `[img]` |
| bs=2 | 1 each | `[img, img]` |
| bs=1 | 2 (multi-image sample) | `[img, img]` |
| bs=2 | 1 and 2 | `[img, img, img]` |

All shapes feed `mlx-vlm` correctly: each top-level element is a single PIL image, `_to_numpy_image` returns 3-D, and `_process_one` succeeds.

## Verified

- **Repro** (before fix): `unsloth/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` + `unsloth/LaTeX_OCR`, bs=1, seq_len=1024, mlx-vlm 0.6.2, MLX on M2 16GB → crashes at the collator before step 1
- **After fix**: collator no longer raises; training proceeds past the dataloader

author: jonathanturnock
body:
Re-initialises the project from Create React App / Mantine / Monaco onto a **Vite + Svelte 5 (runes)** stack with **Tailwind v4**, **shadcn-svelte** components and **CodeMirror 6**. The previous implementation is preserved verbatim under `_legacy/` (moved with `git mv` so history follows).

## Functionality (ported feature-for-feature)
- Lua editor + command console against the local DCS fiddle server hook
- Environment selector (Mission/GUI) with health-check polling and toasts
- Optional custom state via a shadcn-svelte combobox (free-text + suggestions)
- Share links (base64 command + env/state round-trip)
- Greeting and Share modals; greeting "don't show again" localStorage key kept
- Miz file diff (JSZip + Lua→JSON via DCS) using `@codemirror/merge`
- Markdown docs with `[++]`/`[--]` diff-line highlighting
- Namespace Explorer with lazy expansion, type icons and minimatch filtering

## Theme
Restored to the legacy look: Mantine dark palette, IBM Plex Sans/Mono, and a vs-dark CodeMirror editor theme + highlight style.

## Fixes to `public/dcs-fiddle-server.lua` (the downloadable hook)
- Abort cleanly on bind failure instead of crashing on a nil socket
- Wrap the client handler in `pcall` so it no longer logs a spurious error per request (and no longer throws uncaught in the Hooks environment)
- Bound the per-client read with a timeout so a silent client can't freeze the DCS sim thread; restore blocking before send to avoid truncating responses
- Explorer encoder now tolerates mixed numeric/string table keys (matching the server's `fiddlejson` scheme), with the frontend reversing the `_` prefix so numeric keys drill to `table[1]` rather than `table["_1"]`

## Verification
- `bun run check` and `bun run build` pass clean
- All pages/modals driven in-browser; Explorer (incl. mixed-key drill-down) and the share-link round-trip verified against a mock of the fiddle server
- Lua hook + generated explore command parse-checked with `luac`

> ⚠️ The DCS-connected paths (Send, Explorer, Miz diff) were verified against a mock since no live DCS was available — worth a smoke test against a running mission before merge. The request format is byte-identical to the legacy app.

author: nicknarcise
body:
## Summary

- Bumps `manifests/orchestrator/resources/deployment.yaml` image tag from `v0.1.4` → `v0.1.6`
- v0.1.6 includes n2solutionsio/orchestrator#41, which wraps the orchestrator system prompt + tool definitions with Anthropic `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` markers and emits new `cache_create` / `cache_read` label values on `orchestrator_api_tokens_total`

## Why

Production logs show repeated 429s from the 30k ITPM Tier 1 rate limit. Each Slack interaction reships ~20-25k input tokens of static prefix (system prompt + 14 tool schemas) before the agent even calls a tool. v0.1.6 caches that prefix at Anthropic for 5 minutes — cached tokens bill at ~10% cost and count substantially less against ITPM.

## What changes at runtime

- First Anthropic call of a new session: `orchestrator_responded` log line will show `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0` (paying to seed the cache)
- Subsequent calls within 5 min: `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` and `input_tokens` drops
- Prometheus: `rate(orchestrator_api_tokens_total{direction="cache_read"}[5m])` should climb above zero within a few minutes of normal Slack usage
- 429 rate should drop measurably

## Test plan

- [ ] ArgoCD syncs the new image tag
- [ ] `kubectl get pod -n ai-org -l app=orchestrator -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[0].image}'` shows `v0.1.6`
- [ ] Send a Slack mention to the orchestrator; first response logs `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0`
- [ ] Send a follow-up Slack message within 5 min; logs `cache_read_input_tokens > 0`
- [ ] Watch `orchestrator_api_tokens_total{direction="cache_read"}` in Prometheus for 30 min — should climb
- [ ] No new 429s under normal usage over the next hour
- [ ] Rollback plan: revert this commit, ArgoCD re-syncs to v0.1.4

## Related

- n2solutionsio/orchestrator#41 (the code change being deployed)
- n2solutionsio/orchestrator#36, #37, #40 (issues closed by that PR)

body:
### Motivation
- Remove temporary, verbose diagnostics and fragile bridge/workaround code that was added to mitigate homebridge-config-ui-x 5.24.0 timeouts while keeping real request timeouts and error behaviour intact.
- Simplify the UI so it no longer injects defaults or fallback logic that masked real plugin configuration state.

### Description
- ui/server.js: stop emitting per-request diagnostic traces and remove helper functions used only for step-by-step request-id logging while preserving `withTimeout` usage and `RequestError` semantics; errors are still returned but logs are concise and only show the high-level error message.
- ui/server.js: avoid injecting default KNX platform values into the API response by returning empty/unchanged values for `knxconnection` and `knxd_port` when they are not present in the config (no hidden defaults).
- ui/public/index.html: remove stale-iframe / postMessage lifecycle tracking, request timer maps, requestId instrumentation, and bridge-timeout fallback UI messages; replace complex `startRequestWithTimeout` flow with a smaller `requestWithTimeout` that races the `homebridge.request` and a timeout and clears timers in `finally`.
- ui/public/index.html: remove automatic fallback plugin-config loading and automatic default population; add a small placeholder option for `knxconnection` selection to avoid implicit defaults; keep CodeMirror, JSON/YAML highlighting, YAML file selection, and Save/Validate/Load flows intact.
- UI behaviour simplified: no automatic reload loops, no extensive stale-bridge warnings, and no aggressive cache/fallback logic added for the broken Homebridge UI bridge.

author: frenck
body:
# Proposed Changes

> (Describe the changes and rationale behind them)

The direct-access NGINX server only listened on IPv4 (`listen {{ .port }};`), so Node-RED was unreachable over IPv6. This is a real problem for users whose ISP uses DS-Lite/CGNAT and can only be reached from the outside over IPv6.

This adds IPv6 `listen [::]:{{ .port }}` directives to the direct-access server template, for both the plain and SSL variants. NGINX defaults to `ipv6only=on` for the `[::]` socket, so the IPv4 and IPv6 listeners coexist without conflict.

Ingress is intentionally untouched (it binds the Supervisor's internal IPv4 interface), and Node-RED itself keeps listening on `127.0.0.1` behind NGINX, so only the externally exposed direct-access vhost needed the change.

Validated by rendering the template with `tempio` for both the SSL and non-SSL cases and running `nginx -t` against the result.

## Related Issues

> ([Github link][autolink-references] to related issues or pull requests)

Closes #1192

author: darren-minimalx
body:
## Problem

The weekly Dependabot → Slack digest had **failed its last 3+ scheduled runs**.
The fetch + build steps succeeded, but the final Post to Slack step returned:

```
status=400
Slack rejected the payload: invalid_blocks
```

Root cause: a Block Kit `section`'s mrkdwn `text` exceeded Slack's **3000-char
hard limit** as org alert volume grew (the "Top alerts"/"Top repositories"
sections concatenate one line per item into a single block).

## Changes

1. **Fix `invalid_blocks`** — cap the two variable-length sections at 2900 chars,
   truncating on a line boundary (`sub("\n[^\n]*$"; "")`) so a partial
   `<url|text>` link is never left dangling. Header and severity-summary blocks
   are inherently short.

2. **Add "fixed in the last 7 days"** (requested) — a new step fetches
   `state=fixed` alerts (sorted by `updated` desc, stopping pagination once a
   page predates the 7-day cutoff, so it stays cheap), and every digest now
   shows the count + severity breakdown, e.g.:

   `✅ Fixed in the last 7 days: 43  (🚨 5 · ⚠️ 13 · 🟠 23 · 🔵 2)`

   It appears in the all-clear digest too, so the channel always sees progress.

## Validation

Simulated the build step locally against real recently-fixed data (43 fleetos
fixes) and a synthetic 200-alert / 40-repo oversized set:

- payload is valid JSON, 7 blocks (Slack limit 50)
- **max section text length 2801 < 3000** (truncation engaged on the stress set)
- header 37 chars < 150
- the fixed-count line and severity breakdown render correctly

YAML parses clean. `date -d` is GNU/Ubuntu-runner syntax (verified the jq/logic
locally with the BSD equivalent).

## How to verify after merge

Trigger the workflow manually (`workflow_dispatch`) to post a live digest to the
channel and confirm it succeeds.

author: pondchalong
body:
## Summary

Give the strategy a real edge. Data analysis showed the baseline had **no edge** (31.8% winrate < 33% breakeven at RR 2:1), so segmented every signal by feature to find what actually predicts wins, added the two filters that did, validated out-of-sample, and applied the winning one.

## What the data showed (every signal, independent, 2500 candles 15m)

| Segment | Winrate |
|---|---|
| All signals | 31.8% (no edge) |
| **HIGH volatility** | **~0%** (8 trades, all lost) |
| Signal **against** HTF MACD | 25.9% |
| Signal **aligned** with HTF MACD | 38.9% |
| confluence 3–5 | 28–33% (no help — higher ≠ better) |

## Filters added (generate_signal, both default off)

- `params.htf_filter` — only trade in the HTF MACD direction
- `params.skip_high_vol` — skip signals when the volatility cluster is HIGH

## Backtest (15m)

| config | trades | win | return | Sharpe | maxDD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 26 | 34.6% | **-2.7%** | -0.44 | 6.4% |
| +skip_high_vol | 18 | 50.0% | **+5.2%** | +1.09 | 1.9% |
| +both | 10 | 60.0% | +3.8% | +1.08 | 1.2% |

Out-of-sample (train 70% / test 30%, 4000 candles): skip_high_vol stays positive on **both** train (+4.4%) and test (+0.8%, Sharpe +0.35). `both` looked great but only 5 test trades — not trusted.

## Applied

`active_params.json` → `skip_high_vol: true` (live demo will trade it after deploy). Edge is thin and sample small — keep collecting demo stats to confirm.

## Files

- `analysis/signals.py` — two optional quality filters
- `strategy/params.py` — `htf_filter`, `skip_high_vol`
- `strategy/active_params.json` — apply skip_high_vol
- `CLAUDE.md` — documented filters + data

author: raifdmueller
body:
Closes #595

## What

Without JavaScript the site was a complete dead end: the shell shipped empty `aria-hidden` header/footer placeholders, **zero `<a href>` links**, no anchor list, and `/anchor/<id>` URLs are real 404s. This PR makes the static HTML navigable and readable — for crawlers, LLM fetchers, and no-JS visitors — in both languages, while JS users get the exact same SPA as before (hydration on top).

## Changes

1. **Static shell navigation** (`website/index.html`): real header (logo + nav links) and footer (reference links) with plain clean-URL `<a href>`s replace the empty skeleton placeholders. `min-height` keeps the CLS reservation from #432; `main.js#hydrateShell()` still swaps both blocks in place at boot.
2. **Static home catalog** (`prerender-routes.js`): the full category → anchor catalog (161 anchors, EN + DE) is pre-rendered into the home page below the hero, single-sourced from `categories.json`/`anchors.json` and the translations.
3. **Stable per-anchor link targets** (`generate-llms-txt.js` + regenerated `docs/all-anchors.adoc`): every anchor section in the full reference now carries its canonical ID, so `/all-anchors#mece` works (previously only title-derived IDs like `#mece-principle` existed). First occurrence only for multi-category anchors; digit-leading IDs (`4mat`) already match their title-derived ID.
4. **Pre-rendered German pages**: every route with a `.de` fragment (about, contributing, agentskill, rejected-proposals, brownfield, socratic-recovery-skill, spec-driven-development) plus the home page now exists statically under `/de/…` with `lang="de"`, localized title/description, self-canonical URL, and honest `hreflang` pairs — the previous `?lang=de` alternate served identical English HTML. The sitemap lists the 8 German pages.
5. **Router** (`router.js`, TDD): a `/de/<route>` URL resolves to the normal route handler and switches the app language to German, so JS users on a German URL get the SPA in German. `handleLanguageChange` now also refreshes the language-toggle label on programmatic switches.
6. **Legacy hash links** in the JS header/footer (`#/contracts` …) replaced with the same clean URLs the static shell uses (the router already intercepts them for SPA navigation).
7. Version bump to **v0.5.0**, changelog entry.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 102 unit tests pass (4 new router tests for the `/de` prefix).
- `npx playwright test`: all 35 E2E tests pass.
- Playwright with `javaScriptEnabled: false` against the preview build: home shows 11 nav links + 171 catalog links; `/about/`, `/all-anchors/` (incl. `#mece` target), `/de/`, `/de/about/` all render real content; German pages are German.
- With JS: SPA hydrates (search input, card grid, modals), `/de/about` boots in German with the toggle label correct, no page errors.
- Lint + Prettier clean (website + scripts).

No-JS home page after this PR:

| EN | DE |
|----|----|
| real header nav + hero + full catalog | same, localized |

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Real static pages per anchor (`/anchor/<id>/index.html`) — the sitemap still advertises those URLs, which remain 404s for non-JS crawlers; worth its own issue.
- The remaining `#/…` links inside client-rendered components (`main-content.js`, `contracts-page.js`) — invisible to crawlers, handled by the router's legacy shim.
- No-JS search/filter.

author: gimips
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the Python host-side tools and pygame game for the Smart Bat project.

The Python program communicates with the STM32 over UART, sends `PITCH` commands to the board, receives synchronized swing events, and uses the STM32-reported `peak_rt` timing to judge swing accuracy in the game.

## Changes

- Add Python serial communication for STM32 UART logs
- Add `GAME_READY` waiting logic before starting the game
- Send `PITCH\n` command from PC to STM32 for timing synchronization
- Parse STM32 swing logs:
  - `PITCH_SYNC`
  - `SWING_START`
  - `SWING_END`
  - `start_rt`
  - `peak_rt`
  - `peak_dps`
  - `speed_x100`
  - `drop`
- Add pygame-based swing timing game
- Add fake 3D pygame version with perspective-style ball movement
- Use STM32 `peak_rt` instead of PC receive time for more accurate hit timing
- Add robust non-blocking UART line buffering to handle fragmented serial logs

## Timing Logic

The PC sends a `PITCH` command when the pitch animation starts.

The STM32 records:

```text
pitch_time_ms = HAL_GetTick()
```

When a swing is detected, STM32 reports:

```text
start_rt = swing_start_time - pitch_time_ms
peak_rt  = swing_peak_time  - pitch_time_ms
```

The Python game judges timing using:

```text
timing_error_ms = peak_rt - ideal_hit_offset_ms
```

This avoids relying on PC-side UART receive timing.

author: bambamboole
body:
Migrates the remaining bag-based components to typed public properties, generates their TypeScript types, and adopts those types on the frontend — mirroring the merged form-domain refactor (#24).

## Per domain
- **Core** (#132): Badge, Button, Card, Grid, Heading, Link, Text, Stack, SegmentedControl, Modal, Tab, Tabs → typed public props via the existing `Component::wireProps()` seam. Tabs' computed `activeValue` is projected in a pre-`serialiseProps` hook (like `Field`), preserving the password-confirm redirect and hidden-child stripping.
- **Action** (#133): Action, ActionGroup, BulkAction → typed public props; `Action::use()`/`BulkAction::use()` now `clone` the registered component.
- **Fragment + Layout** (#134): Fragment (+ `FragmentRegistry` lazy flag) → typed public props; layout primitives were already prop-less.
- **Generation**: per-component prop types + discriminated `CoreNode`/`ActionNode`/`FragmentNode` unions and a shared `Node` union, built from typed TS nodes with linked references. `FormNode`/container `schema?` broadened to `Node[]`. A generated `Effect` union (linked to the `Effect` contract) backs `Action.effects`. Output is formatted with the project's **oxfmt** via a new `OxfmtFormatter`; the PHP CI job gains `npm ci` so the generated-types round-trip test formats identically.
- **Frontend**: `resources/js/core/components/*` and `resources/js/action/components/*` consume the generated prop types; the hand-maintained `ActionEffect` union is collapsed to the generated `Effect`. Type-only, no behavior change.

## Wire-identical
Every migration is wire-identical (guarded by the existing suite + new golden/wire-shape tests), **with one intentional exception**: `BulkAction` now emits the `variant` its definition sets — the old `use()` silently dropped it. Drift is guarded by `NodeUnionTest` and the `composer types` round-trip test.

## Deferred (follow-ups)
- **Tables (#135)** — `Table` still uses the bag; its `result()` merges a dynamic `TableResult` payload, a genuinely different serialization model best handled separately.
- **Retire the bag (#136)** — blocked on Tables; `wireProps()` keeps merging the (now unused for migrated components) bag.

## Verification
`composer test` (266), phpstan, pint, `composer types` no-op, `npm run typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`format:check`/`build`, and `composer test:browser` (22) all green.

author: mortenoh
body:
## Summary

Subscribe to YouTube channels by URL and play their videos through maneki's existing on-demand HLS transcode pipeline. yt-dlp resolves a video to its direct stream URLs; a new `MediaSource` abstraction lets the segment transcoder feed those (two `-i` inputs + `-map`, with the resolved HTTP headers replayed so googlevideo doesn't 403) exactly like a local file. No changes to the local-file playback path.

## What's included

**Backend**
- `youtube.py` — channel listing (Videos / Shorts / Live tabs via flat extraction) and per-video stream resolution, with TTL caches and cookie support (`MANEKI_YT_COOKIES_FROM_BROWSER` / cookiefile / `[media]` config) to avoid anti-bot rate limiting.
- `sources.py` — `LocalSource` / `RemoteSource`; `OnDemandHLS` now takes a source (a bare `Path` is still accepted for local callers). `yt:` sessions are protected from the rescan orphan-cleaner.
- `subscriptions.py` — per-user channel store at `<root>/.maneki/users/<name>/youtube.toml`; `UserRegistry.subscriptions_for`.
- `/api/youtube/*` endpoints (channel CRUD, tab listing, video metadata, HLS). The local and YouTube HLS handlers share one response helper.

**Quality**
- Resolution-aware encode bitrate ladder (1080p ~12M vs the old flat 6M that looked soft); adjustable per-stream cap (Auto / 1080 / 720 / 480) via an in-player video.js menu that hot-swaps the source and preserves the playhead. The manifest stamps the cap on segment URIs so they route to the matching session. `[media] youtube_max_height` sets the default.

**Frontend**
- YouTube section in video mode: add-channel input, channel list, per-channel Videos / Shorts / Live tabs, playback via the shared player, `#/video/yt/<id>` deep-link.

**Also**
- Serve the SPA shell with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (content-hashed assets stay `immutable`) so a rebuild is never masked by a stale cached `index.html`.
- Bumps version to 0.16.0.

## Testing

- 740 tests pass; ruff + mypy + pyright clean.
- Verified end-to-end against live channels (`@RedLetterMedia`, `@NASA`): add channel, browse Videos/Shorts/Live, play 1080p transcoded from YouTube, switch resolution in-player, seek.
- For reliable real-world resolution set `MANEKI_YT_COOKIES_FROM_BROWSER=chrome` (or `safari`/`firefox`) — without logged-in cookies, high request volume from one IP trips YouTube's "confirm you're not a bot".

## Known limitations (sketch scope)

- No subtitles for YouTube videos, no channel auto-refresh, no mid-watch re-resolution of expired (~6h) stream URLs.
- Stream-copy (lossless passthrough) is deferred: YouTube's H.264 uses irregular content-adaptive keyframes and enumerating them over the network downloads the whole file, so per-segment copy isn't viable in the on-demand model; the resolution-aware re-encode is the practical quality win instead.
- yt-dlp tracks YouTube changes closely; expect periodic dependency bumps.

author: dcellison
body:
Closes #601

## Problem

Photos sent to the bot never reached the model on ACP backends (opencode, goose), and the user got no indication. The bot layer builds Anthropic-style base64 image blocks; the claude backend forwards content blocks verbatim, but the ACP send path stripped every non-text block with only a log warning, so the reply was generated from the caption text alone while the user reasonably assumed the model saw the image.

## Change

Capability-gated forwarding, with a user-visible notice on the drop path:

- The initialize handshake now reads the agent's `agentCapabilities.promptCapabilities.image` instead of discarding the result. Missing or malformed capability structures count as no support, since sending an image to an agent that never advertised support is a protocol violation, while dropping one is only a degraded reply.
- New `convert_image_block` in `src/kai/acp.py` translates the Anthropic base64 shape (`source.media_type` / `source.data`) to ACP's image content block (`mimeType` / `data`). Blocks that are not the expected shape return None and are dropped.
- When the agent supports images, converted blocks ride through `assemble_turn_context` (which already handles mixed-modal lists) onto `session/prompt`. Both probed agents advertise support, so this lights up images on opencode 1.15.11 and goose 1.29.1.
- When a block is dropped (no capability, or unconvertible shape), the reply text is seeded with `[Note: N attached image(s) could not be passed to <backend>; this reply is based on the message text only.]` so the drop is no longer silent. The seed ends at a line break so the opencode chunk-join heuristic never fires against it.
- The EOF-process-died path previously keyed success off non-empty accumulated text; it now uses an explicit got-model-text flag so a notice seed alone cannot surface as a successful reply.

## Verification against live agents

Both installed ACP agents were probed with a real `initialize` handshake over stdio:

- opencode 1.15.11: `promptCapabilities: {"embeddedContext": true, "image": true}`
- goose 1.29.1: `promptCapabilities: {"image": true, "audio": false, "embeddedContext": true}`

The ACP image block shape (`type`/`mimeType`/`data`, base64) was taken from the protocol documentation at agentclientprotocol.com.

Note: capability is advertised per agent, not per model. A text-only model behind a capable agent is the provider's concern; what the model does with the image is outside Kai's visibility. An end-to-end check is sending a photo over Telegram on the opencode backend after deploy.

## Testing

- Capability capture parametrized over true/false/absent/malformed initialize results.
- Forwarding: ACP-shape image block present on the written `session/prompt`, no notice in the reply.
- Drop paths: notice seeded (singular and plural), malformed block dropped despite capability, all-dropped input still gets the `(empty prompt)` placeholder.
- EOF after a drop stays an error rather than a notice-only success.
- `convert_image_block` unit-tested across good and malformed shapes.
- Full suite: 3773 passed, 1 skipped. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

author: obtfusi
body:
**The staging E2E's live conflict journey caught real data loss** (#326): a file edited locally **and** remotely between syncs was overwritten by the download with **no conflict copy**. Keep-both only existed on the upload path (If-Match/412) — `materialize_downloads` wrote unconditionally over `remote_dirty` items.

**Root cause:** after the delta ingest, an item's metadata holds the NEW remote values — the pass had no reference to tell *stale-but-clean* from *locally edited*.

**Fix:**
- **Schema v8**: per-item last-synced on-disk reference (`synced_size/_mtime_unix/_hash`), written **only** by download/upload paths, never by the ingest
- materialize compares disk vs reference (size → mtime → QuickXorHash ladder) → locally-edited file moves aside as a `safeBackup` conflict copy **before** the cloud version is written; counted in `(N conflict copies)`
- upload paths (`push_local_creates`, `apply_local_modifies`) + the materialize skip path record the reference
- pre-v8 items without a reference keep the old behavior (no conflict-copy spray on ordinary updates)

## Verification
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| edit-edit: local edit survives as safeBackup, cloud at original path, conflicts==1 | pass |
| stale-clean update: no copy | pass |
| legacy (no reference): no copy | pass |
| upload records reference (size+hash asserted) | pass |
| store roundtrip + migration v8 | pass |
| workspace | **473 / 0** |
| fmt + clippy -D warnings | clean |

author: nickderobertis
body:
Release-please opens its release PR with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and PRs opened by `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't trigger the `pull_request` CI/lint workflows (GitHub suppresses that to avoid recursive runs). So the release PR's required checks never appear, it sits `blocked`, and **auto-merge can never fire** — every release has to be merged by hand (as v0.1.1 #18 and v0.1.2 #21 both were).

**Fix:** pass a PAT to the action via `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`. A PAT-opened PR triggers CI like any human PR, so branch protection is satisfied and auto-merge works.

- **Graceful fallback:** if `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` isn't set, it falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` — current behavior, nothing breaks (release PR just needs a manual merge).
- **`AGENTS.md`:** documents the secret, why it's needed, and the `gh secret set` command; scopes the existing "no extra PAT" note (that referred to the build chaining, which still needs no PAT).

**One manual step on your side to activate it:** create the PAT and add the secret —
```
gh secret set RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN --repo nickderobertis/github-secrets
```
A fine-grained token with `contents: read/write` + `pull-requests: read/write` on this repo (or a classic `repo` PAT) works. Until then, the fallback keeps everything functioning exactly as today.

author: rocketman-21
body: ## Why The 20m runner idle TTL from PR #100 never reached prod — containers were destroyed at exactly 5m idle for a month. Prod `onStop` logs showed `runnerIdleTtlMs: 300000` / `lastActivityObservedAgeMs: ~300037` with `destroyRequestReason: activity-expired`, causing frequent avoidable ~15-20s cold starts. Root cause: `wrangler.jsonc` is only a scaffold. Real deploys source `HOSTED_EXECUTION_RUNNER_IDLE_TTL_MS` from a GitHub `production` environment variable, which still held `300000` (set 2026-05-09, predating the bump), and the var sits on the silently-skipped optional list — so nothing flagged the drift. The stale environment variable has been corrected to `1200000` and deployed (2026-06-10), but the drift class remains. ## What - Add `HOSTED_WORKER_OPTIONAL_VAR_DEFAULTS` in deploy automation: source-controlled defaults rendered when the deploy environment leaves an optional var unset (`RUNNER_IDLE_TTL_MS=1200000`, `VERCEL_OIDC_ENVIRONMENT=production`, and the existing `RUNNER_ENV_PROFILES` special-case folded in). Deploys now always ship an explicit TTL; GitHub environment vars and workflow inputs remain explicit overrides. - New test: every non-required var in the checked-in `wrangler.jsonc` scaffold must equal the value a default-rendered deploy ships — editing the scaffold without the default (or vice versa) now fails CI at the PR instead of silently diverging in prod. - Comment on the scaffold `vars` block pointing at `gh variable list --env production` for live overrides. No workflow changes: `deploy-preflight.ts` reads `HOSTED_EXECUTION_VERCEL_OIDC_ENVIRONMENT` from process.env directly, so the yml `|| 'production'` fallback stays load-bearing; `cf:deploy:immediate`'s explicit `runner_idle_ttl_ms=300000` input override is deliberate and unaffected. ## Verification - `vitest run apps/cloudflare/test/deploy-automation.test.ts apps/cloudflare/test/env.test.ts` — 49 passed (new scaffold-vars alignment test included) - `pnpm typecheck` in `apps/cloudflare` — clean 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? author: ersinkoc
body:
## What

A guided **first-run setup** that hand-holds a brand-new operator past the one thing the daemon can't self-create — a real LLM key — on **both** surfaces. Plus a fix the smoke caught: making the **live provider switch actually switch**.

### WebUI
- New **`Setup.tsx`** 3-step wizard: **catalog → provider + key → model**, over the EXISTING `/api/catalog`, `/api/catalog/sync`, `/api/provider/keys/add`, `/api/config/set`, `/api/provider/reload` routes — no new daemon commands.
- **Auto full-screen overlay** on first run when no provider is `credentialed` (skippable; localStorage flag), plus a permanent **Setup** nav entry to reopen. `onDone` drops you into Chat.

### CLI
- `agt quickstart` `[4/4]` now **persists** the provider/model choice live (`CmdConfigSet`, no env vars / no restart) when a daemon is reachable; otherwise falls back to the env-var start command.
- Daemon banner prints a can't-miss **`⚠ setup needed`** line right after the governor banner whenever it's running on the offline mock.

## Fix — live provider switch was broken (found by the end-to-end smoke)

Setting `AGEZT_PROVIDER`/`AGEZT_MODEL` live did **not** actually switch the running provider:
1. `OnReload` discarded the new model (`_ = model2`), so runs hit the new provider carrying the old model id `"mock"` → real provider rejects it (`you passed mock`).
2. The boot-time **mock primary was never demoted** — `Registry.Replace` only swaps a same-named entry, so `deepseek` was appended *behind* mock and mock kept serving every run. The wizard would say "you're ready" while answers stayed `[offline-mock]`.

**Fixes:** the kernel default model is now a mu-guarded live field (mirrors the M710 persona), hot-swapped via `SetModel` on reload; and a stale mock primary is demoted to an `IsFallback` entry before the real provider is installed.

## Tests
- **vitest** `Setup.test.tsx` (6): pure helpers + full walk asserting exact POST args + empty-catalog Sync + overlay Skip.
- **Go** `TestKernel_Model_LiveSwap`: seed → run carries it → `SetModel` → next run carries the new model.

## Smoke (isolated `AGEZT_HOME`, owner's real `~/.agezt` untouched)
Empty home, no key → banner shows `⚠ setup needed` + Web UI URL. Playwright: auto-wizard appears, walk it with the owner's real deepseek key (from gitignored `.env`, never echoed) → both config steps `applied: live` → a real `agt run` answers **`SETUP_OK_M816`** from `deepseek-v4-pro · $0.0032`, **primary=deepseek, 0 fallbacks, no restart**. Reload → wizard does not reappear; Setup nav still opens it.

## Gate
Full `GOMAXPROCS=3 go test -p 2 ./...` green; vet + staticcheck clean; linux cross-build OK; vitest green; `kernel/webui/dist` rebuilt (LF); go.mod unchanged. No new control-plane commands, env vars, or event kinds.

author: houxiru
body:
## Summary

This branch ships two related features for ContextHub:

1. **Cross-platform adaptation** — the extension now works on **ChatGPT** and **Gemini** in addition to Claude, and the backend/interchange spec accept these as valid source/target platforms.
2. **Multi-conversation pull** — the dashboard lets you select multiple saved conversations and pull them together into a single combined context (the backend already supported batched selections; this restores the UI for it).

---

## 1. Cross-platform adaptation (ChatGPT + Gemini)

### Extension
- **`content.ts` refactored to a `PlatformAdapter` model.** All platform-specific logic — host matching, message selectors, conversation-id parsing, and prompt-input lookup — is encapsulated in one adapter per platform (`claudeAdapter`, `chatgptAdapter`, `geminiAdapter`). The rest of the script is platform-agnostic and drives whichever adapter matches the current page. Adding a new platform = adding one adapter to `ADAPTERS`.
  - ChatGPT: scrapes `[data-message-author-role]` turns; injects into the `#prompt-textarea` ProseMirror composer.
  - Gemini: scrapes `user-query-content` / `message-content .markdown-main-panel`; injects into the `<rich-textarea>` Quill editor.
- **More robust prompt injection** (`injectIntoInput`). ProseMirror/Quill editors reconcile their DOM from internal state, so a plain `textContent` assignment is unreliable. We now prefer `execCommand("insertText")` (flows through the editor's own `beforeinput`/`input` pipeline) and fall back to the `textContent` + `InputEvent` path.
- **Noise filtering extended** to cover ChatGPT/Gemini chrome (`.cdk-visually-hidden`, `mat-icon`, screen-reader labels, action bars).
- **`manifest.json`** adds host permissions and content-script/web-accessible-resource matches for `chatgpt.com`, `chat.openai.com`, and `gemini.google.com`.
- **`background.ts`** detects the active tab's platform from its URL (`detectPlatformFromUrl`) and sends the correct `target_platform` on pull, defaulting to `claude_ai` for unknown hosts.
- Removed the unused `content-comments.ts` (343 lines).

### Backend + interchange spec
- `target_platform` validation widened to `^(claude_ai|chatgpt|gemini)$` (`schemas/pulls.py`) and platform framing in `context_builder.py` applies to all three.
- Source `platform` enum extended to `claude_ai | chatgpt | gemini` across the interchange spec: JSON schema, generated TS (`interchange-spec`, `shared-types`), and Pydantic models.

---

## 2. Multi-conversation pull

### Dashboard (`page.tsx` + `globals.css`)
- Per-conversation **selection checkboxes** (hover/selected reveal) with a sticky **selection bar** showing the count and a **"Copy combined context"** action.
- Each selected conversation can opt into **"Include full transcript"** (maps to `include_transcript` per selection).
- Caps selection at 20 (matching the backend `max_length`), clears selection state on delete, and shows the combined token estimate after copy.

---

## Other changes
- **RLS refactor:** `get_rls_session` now delegates to a single `apply_rls_context` (`auth/rls.py`) shared by the API request path and worker jobs, so the two can't drift. Worker jobs now use the `authenticated` role + `request.jwt.claim.sub` consistently.
- Added `uvicorn[standard]` to backend dependencies.

## Testing
- [ ] Extension capture + inject on Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini
- [ ] Dashboard multi-select pull (with and without transcripts)
- [ ] Backend accepts `chatgpt`/`gemini` target platforms

author: agenciaseniors
body:
## Hardening de seguridad P3 (aprobado, auditoría pass #2) — migración 00401

### (1) Funciones SECDEF de ESCRITURA ejecutables por `anon`
El advisor de seguridad marcó 34 funciones SECDEF ejecutables por `anon`; la mayoría son lecturas públicas legítimas (búsqueda guest, tokens de viaje compartido). **Estas cuatro escriben** (directo o vía dispatch anidado) y **no tienen callers de cliente** — solo las invocan triggers / otras funciones SECDEF, en contexto definer (que ignora el grant EXECUTE del invocador). Bloquearlas de anon/authenticated/PUBLIC es seguro y elimina superficie de escritura pre-auth:
- `apply_user_rating(uuid)` — UPDATE `users.rating_avg`
- `recompute_user_level(uuid)` — UPDATE `users.level`/`total_rides`
- `calculate_wait_charge(uuid)` — UPDATE `rides.wait_time_charge_cup`
- `dispatch_searching_rides_for_driver(uuid)` — crea `ride_offers`

### (2) Spoof de `wallet_transfers`
La política RLS de INSERT `"Users can insert own transfers"` (`WITH CHECK auth.uid()=from_user_id`) permitía a cualquier usuario INSERTAR una fila `wallet_transfers` directa — un "regalo recibido" falso en el historial del destinatario (solo display, sin mover dinero — eso vive en el ledger). El único escritor legítimo es `send_gift()` (SECDEF → bypassa RLS), y ningún código de app inserta directo. Dropear la política cierra el spoof; admins (política ALL) + service-role + `send_gift` siguen escribiendo.

## Verificación
- Grep confirma: 0 callers de las 4 funciones en app/packages; 0 inserts directos de `wallet_transfers`.
- SQL-only → `check-types` no afectado.
- Post-apply: `has_function_privilege('anon', fn, 'EXECUTE')=false` para las 4; INSERT en `wallet_transfers` como usuario normal denegado; `send_gift` sigue funcionando (rolled-back).

body:
💡 **What:** Hoisted invariant mathematical calculations (`t0_k`, `lapse_rate`, `lapse_factor`) out of the `_calc_temp` and `_calc_pres` closures in `core/simulation.py`.
🎯 **Why:** These closure functions are passed to RocketPy's Environment and called thousands of times per simulation step by the Fortran integrator (LSODA). Re-evaluating static constants inside these functions created massive Python execution overhead in performance-critical numerical integration loops.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces redundant floating-point operations inside the ODE evaluation callback by pre-computing invariant terms, speeding up each `simulate_once` call. In synthetic benchmarks, hoisting these calculations yields ~30% faster closure execution.
🔬 **Measurement:** Verify by running Monte Carlo trials or grid search optimizations (which invoke `simulate_once` heavily) to observe faster completion times. Verified via test suite (`pytest tests/`).

**auto-geo is now CLI-only — a complete, file-based GEO engine.** The package is cut down to the thing people actually use (the CLI) and built out into a full loop: set up once, audit, generate, fix, measure, and track over time.

- All package exports gone: `auto-geo`, `/schema`, `/validation`, `/jsonld`, `/react`, `/next`, `/hono`, `/cloudflare`, `/storage/*`. The package ships exactly one thing: the `auto-geo` binary.

body:
## Goal
Make `/cipl` (Challenge League / League Battle) chats cleaner for everyone in the group, fix the over format, and keep the match viewable in the Mini App after it ends.

## Changes

**1. 20-over format**
- Every `/cipl` match is now always a 20-over contest (`CIPL_OVERS = 20`), instead of reading the configurable `/cm` challenge-overs setting. The toss/launch confirmation already prints `… • 20 overs`.

**2. Cleaner chat — over messages always swept**
- The per-over delete already removes the previous over's pick prompt + "⏳ Simulating over N — … bowling…" message + end-of-over summary when the next over starts. This PR fixes the two cases where the **last** over of a phase used to linger:
  - **Innings break** — the final over of innings 1 (its simulating prompt + summary) is deleted before the break card is posted.
  - **Match end** — the final over's simulating prompt + summary is deleted before the result is posted, **including when the chase is won mid-over**.

**3. Innings Break card auto-removed**
- The "🛑 Innings Break" card stays up through the **first over of the chase** (the target also rides along in every over header), then the normal previous-over delete sweeps it the moment over 2 begins — so it never accumulates in the chat.

**4. Match stays visible in the Mini App after it ends**
- On completion we now snapshot the final scorecard + Arena board (`save_final_scorecard`) before the live state is cleaned up — the same mechanism `/wpm` uses. The "📊 View Match" button keeps opening a read-only result board after the match is over.
- Added the `inn1_team` alias so the Mini App scorecard labels the 1st-innings batting side correctly.

## Notes / suggestions included
- Kept the target visible at all times (over headers + break card for one over + Mini App), so removing the break card early doesn't hide chase info.
- `/cm` Challenge Mode is untouched (still capped at 2 overs).

## Testing
- `tests/test_cipl_approach.py` and `tests/test_challenge_league_commands.py` pass (33 passed).
- Syntax + `services.cipl_match` import verified.

body:
## What

`audit.Logger.Subscribe(buf int) (<-chan Entry, func())` fan-out push channel + drop-oldest bounded delivery + `leah_audit_subscriber_dropped_total{subscriber}` counter.

Wave-10 O6 (`docs/engineer/briefs/2026-06-10-wave-10-osevent-push-migration.md`). Unblocks the 3 audit-rescan polls (selflearn.Resolver, web dashboard TTL cache, dispatcher feedback ingest) — those consumer-side migrations are deferred to follow-up PRs to keep this one file-disjoint.

## Why

Three consumers re-read `audit.jsonl` every 5s today. Subscribe-on-write replaces the rescan loop with push: 5s p50 staleness → <1s, plus idle CPU drop from the dropped tail-scan goroutines.

## Failing test (TDD)

```
$ go test ./internal/audit/
# github.com/trilam/leah/internal/audit [github.com/trilam/leah/internal/audit.test]
internal/audit/subscribe_test.go:14:23: logger.Subscribe undefined (type *Logger has no field or method Subscribe)
internal/audit/subscribe_test.go:47:19: logger.Dropped undefined (type *Logger has no field or method Dropped)
FAIL    github.com/trilam/leah/internal/audit [build failed]
```

After impl:

```
ok      github.com/trilam/leah/internal/audit   1.409s   (-race -count=1)
```

## Coverage

- `TestLogger_Subscribe_ReceivesAppendedEntries` — basic push delivery, timestamp stamping survives fan-out.
- `TestLogger_Subscribe_DropOnFull` — buf=2, 6 appends → 2 drained, `Dropped()=4`.
- `TestLogger_Subscribe_Unsubscribe_StopsFanout` — cancel removes the subscriber; further appends do not count toward `Dropped()`.
- `TestLogger_MultipleSubscribers_Independent` — slow subscriber (buf=1) cannot stall the fast one (buf=16); slow's drops are recorded, fast gets all N entries.

## What got smaller

Nothing in this PR — it's foundation. The deletions land in the follow-ups:

- `internal/selflearn/resolver.go` — rescan loop deletes once it Subscribes (separate PR).
- `internal/web/state.go` — 3s TTL cache + scan replaced by in-memory aggregate fed off the channel (separate PR).
- `internal/dispatcher/` feedback-ingest poll (separate PR).

## Constraints

- File-disjoint: `internal/audit/` only.
- `./scripts/check.sh` exit 0 (build, race-tests, vet, lint, density, doclinks, sleep-gate all green).
- No AI signatures.

author: copilot
body:
Cette PR pose une base d’application Ionic + Angular + Firebase pour gérer des parties en direct avec des équipes prédéfinies et mise à jour des scores en temps réel. L’objectif est de couvrir web dès maintenant, avec une configuration prête pour iOS/Android via Capacitor.

- **Application shell Ionic + Angular**
  - Remplacement du scaffold initial par une UI Ionic orientée “live scoring”.
  - Écran principal pour créer une partie (`nom`, `équipe A`, `équipe B`) et afficher les parties actives.

- **Intégration Firebase / Firestore**
  - Ajout de la config Firebase Angular (`provideFirebaseApp`, `provideFirestore`) dans `app.config.ts`.
  - Ajout de l’environnement Firebase (`src/environments/environment.ts`) avec placeholders de configuration projet.

- **Domaine “partie + score live”**
  - Nouveau `ScoreboardService` pour :
    - créer une partie avec score initial à `0-0`,
    - exposer un flux des parties triées par création (`games$`),
    - appliquer des updates de score atomiques (`increment`) pour chaque équipe.

- **Interaction live sur les scores**
  - Boutons `+`/`-` par équipe sur chaque carte de partie.
  - Validation de création (équipes distinctes, nom requis).

- **Préparation mobile (iOS/Android)**
  - Initialisation Capacitor (`capacitor.config.ts`).
  - Scripts npm pour `cap:add:android`, `cap:add:ios`, `cap:sync`.

- **Documentation**
  - README mis à jour avec setup Firebase, exécution web, et commandes Capacitor.

Exemple de logique de mise à jour atomique des scores :

```ts
updateScore(gameId: string, teamKey: 'teamA' | 'teamB', delta: number): Promise<void> {
  return this.updateGameDocument(gameId, {
    [`scores.${teamKey}`]: this.getIncrement(delta),
    updatedAt: this.getTimestamp()
  });
}
```

author: stuffbucket
body:
**Phase 1 of the auth-subsystem refactor** (boundary D1 — well-form the value space so invalid auth/account values are *unrepresentable*, not caught at runtime). Follows #101 (Phase 0). Phases 2 (AuthState union), 3 (transition reducer), 4 (gh hinting / quick-switch) come as separate PRs.

## What

- **`AccountType` is a closed enum** (`individual | business | enterprise`), not a free string interpolated into a hostname. The CLI `-a` flag is parsed through `parseAccountType` (fails closed, naming the valid values) instead of trusting the raw string — a typo like `-a enterpise` can no longer silently build `https://api.enterpise.githubcopilot.com`.
- **`CopilotHost` is a branded, validated https origin.** The only ways to get one are `toCopilotHost` (validates + normalizes to origin — drops trailing slash / stray path) and `hostForAccountType`. `applyCopilotApiUrl` now validates discovery's `endpoints.api` at the boundary and **ignores a malformed host** instead of storing it; `copilotBaseUrl` returns `CopilotHost` and derives the pre-discovery default via `hostForAccountType`.
- **One branding path for the host:** `logUser` routes its `endpoints.api` write through `applyCopilotApiUrl` too (previously a second, unvalidated writer).

New `src/lib/auth-types.ts` holds these types; Phase 2's `AuthState` discriminated union will embed them (`plan: AccountType`, `host: CopilotHost`), which is why they live in their own module now.

## Why

The audit found `accountType` was a free string and the completion host an unvalidated optional — the structural seam behind the "hand-managing strings" smell and the host-typo failure class. This closes D1 so Phases 2-3 can build the state union / transition reducer on a well-formed value space.

## Tests
+8 unit tests for `auth-types` (enum parse incl. typo/empty/case, host validation + normalization + non-https rejection, per-account-type host). Full suite green (804 pass); `check:fast` + `knip` clean.

body:
This is a major content addition that ports and extends the Diversity 1.7.2 mod for Minecraft 1.26.1 (Fabric), introducing a comprehensive faction system with NPCs, reputation mechanics, quests, mercenary hiring, taverns, and new weapons.

## Key Changes

**Faction System**
- Added `Faction` enum with 12 factions (Villagers, Egyptians, Elves, Dwarves, Nords, Northerners, Aztecs, Goblins, Bandits, Pirates, Wildlings, Mercenaries)
- Implemented `Alignment` (GOOD, NEUTRAL, EVIL) to determine faction behavior and relationships
- Created `FactionRelations` to define which factions fight each other based on alignment
- Added `WarState` for world-wide war declarations between factions with persistent storage

**NPC Entities**
- `FactionVillagerEntity`: Base class for all faction NPCs with AI goals, trading, and faction affiliation
- `FactionLeaderEntity`: Leaders who offer quests and manage faction reputation
- `MercenaryEntity`: Hireable soldiers that follow players for emeralds
- `InnkeeperEntity`: Tavern keepers who rent rooms via house deeds
- Specialized faction NPCs: `GoblinEntity`, `PirateEntity`, `BanditEntity`, `WildlingEntity`, `MusketeerEntity`

**Quest System**
- `QuestApi`: Handles quest offer/progress/turn-in logic for faction leaders
- `QuestInstance`: Represents active quests with type, faction, and progress tracking
- `QuestPools`: Static quest templates (delivery, hunting, gathering) picked when leaders offer quests

body:
## What

Found by a **live self-scan** (network was reachable this session). The scan converged correctly on the subject — a VERIFIED email, a Brisbane coordinate (-27.4698,153.0251 = QLD), and a "Brisbane, QLD" address — but **AU-056 never fired**, the jurisdiction cross-check sitting idle despite both a coordinate and an address naming QLD.

Root cause: the anchoring coordinate was produced by `geo_normalize`/`search_engines`, which don't attach the `au-state:` tag — only three geo builders do. AU-056's `coord_state` read the tag only, so it silently dropped the (common) untagged case.

## Fix

`coord_state` now falls back to deriving the state straight from the parsed lat/long via `util::geo::au_state_for_coords` when no tag is present — so the cross-check works for coordinates from **any** module, not just the three that tag. Verified end-to-end against the live scan: AU-056 now corroborates QLD from the coordinate + address.

Allow-lists `util::geo::au_state_for_coords` for `core` use (pure, no I/O) and adds a regression test reproducing the exact tag-less live case.

## Verification

Full CI-matching gate clean: `cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, rustdoc `--document-private-items`, `cargo test` — 2084 lib tests pass, architecture guard included.

author: teknoprep
body:
## Remote Proxy & Network Devices

Adds the ability to reach a device on an **agent's LAN** (firewalls, switches, Proxmox/PBS, iDRAC, etc.) directly from the Tactical RMM UI — no MeshCentral Router, no local client, no manual port-forwarding, all over the existing HTTPS port.

Right-click an agent → **Remote Proxy** opens one window with a protocol selector:

| Protocol | What you get |
|---|---|
| HTTPS / HTTP | the device's web UI embedded in the window (iframe) |
| VNC | the device's screen via MeshCentral's built-in noVNC viewer, relayed through the agent (no client to install) |
| SSH / Telnet | an in-browser xterm.js terminal |

It also adds a **Network Devices** tab (next to Servers/Workstations/Mixed) where you register devices (name / protocol / IP / port / description / **ordered preferred agents**) and Connect with one click. Agent selection walks the preferred list and **probes reachability**, skipping agents that can't actually reach the device, falling back to a random online agent (servers first).

### How it works
* Reuses MeshCentral's relay (`meshrelay.ashx`) to open a raw TCP tunnel to `addr:port` *through the agent* (same mechanism as the existing WebVNC feature), with `MemoryBIO` TLS for HTTPS targets.
* A small async reverse proxy (served by the ASGI server) speaks HTTP/1.1 (`h11`) over the tunnel and rewrites responses so the device renders in an iframe (strips `X-Frame-Options`/CSP, fixes redirects, root-relative URLs and ES-module imports; injects a runtime XHR/fetch/WebSocket shim for JS-built URLs). Cookies are forwarded byte-exact so `__Host-`/`__Secure-` tickets (Proxmox/PBS) survive.
* WebSocket proxying is included so device consoles work (e.g. Proxmox/PBS noVNC & xterm).
* VNC reuses MeshCentral's bundled noVNC viewer + `meshrelay.ashx`: the `WebVNC` endpoint accepts an optional `?addr=<ip>` to relay to a device on the agent's LAN (instead of the agent itself) — no bundled client or extra dependency.
* SSH uses `asyncssh` server-side bridged to xterm.js; Telnet is a raw bridge with minimal IAC negotiation.
* All sessions are permission-gated (`can_use_mesh`) and written to the audit log / history.

### Deployment — handled automatically
* `install.sh` generates the `location ^~ /agentproxy/` block (ASGI socket + WebSocket upgrade headers via a `$connection_upgrade` map) in both the API and frontend nginx vhosts.
* `update.sh` idempotently patches the `/agentproxy/` block into existing `rmm.conf`/`frontend.conf` on upgrade (backs up each file first) so existing installs get the feature without breakage. Validated with `nginx -t`.
* New Python deps (`asyncssh`, `h11`, `uvicorn[standard]`, `websockets`) install via `requirements.txt`; the ASGI server runs under uvicorn (`daphne.service`).

> Note: web-proxy URL handling for JS-heavy appliance UIs has since moved to a root-scoped **service worker** that intercepts/re-prefixes requests generically (with per-session cookie isolation), which is far more robust than response rewriting. Validated against TrueNAS SCALE, Ricoh Web Image Monitor, pfSense, Proxmox, and generic firewalls. See the summary comment below for the full set of follow-up commits.

### Notes
* Developed against **v1.4.0 (master)**; happy to rebase onto `develop`. `maintainer_can_modify` is enabled.
* Frontend changes are in a companion PR to `tacticalrmm-web` (#50).

author: copilot
body:
Completes Step 2 of the Next/26 backend domain-module refactor (issue #21): moves the remaining Flask route handlers for profile, audit activity, and MCP proxy out of `next_app.py` into the four dedicated domain modules introduced in Step 1, with full backward-compatible re-exports.

## What moved

| Module | New function | Routes |
|---|---|---|
| `next_mcp_activity.py` | `register_next_mcp_routes()` | `/mcp`, `/mcp/`, `/mcp/<path:subpath>`, `/mcp-health` |
| `next_audit.py` | `register_next_audit_routes()` | `/api/next/audit/events` |
| `next_profile.py` | `register_next_profile_routes()` | 13 routes: profile CRUD, API tokens CRUD, api-audit-events, avatar, recovery, passkeys |

Net: −774 inline lines from `next_app.py`'s `register_routes()`.

## Wiring pattern

Each domain module exposes a `register_*_routes(flask_app, *, connect)` function following the same pattern used by `next_auth.py`. `next_app.py` calls all three from `register_routes()` and re-exports them in both the package-relative and flat-module (`gunicorn next_app:app`) import branches:

```python
# next_app.py — both try/except ImportError branches updated
from .next_profile import register_next_profile_routes
from .next_audit  import register_next_audit_routes
from .next_mcp_activity import register_next_mcp_routes

def register_routes(flask_app, connect):
    register_next_auth_routes(flask_app, connect=connect)
    register_next_mcp_routes(flask_app, connect=connect)
    register_next_profile_routes(flask_app, connect=connect)
    register_next_audit_routes(flask_app, connect=connect)
    ...
```

Lazy `_next_app()` imports (already established in the helpers) are used inside route handlers that call functions still living in `next_app.py` (e.g. `require_next_permission`, `save_uploaded_profile_avatar_file`) to avoid circular imports at module load time.

## Security

The MCP proxy was echoing the upstream `Content-Type` header verbatim. A Content-Type whitelist (`application/json`, `text/event-stream`) is now enforced; responses with any other content type fall back to `application/json`. This closes a pre-existing reflective XSS vector in the proxy response path.

## Guardrails

- `app.py`, `config.py`, `db.py`, `logging_utils.py` — zero diff.
- All `next_app.<name>` and `app.backend.next_app.<name>` references continue to resolve identically.
- `app/VERSION` bumped to `26.1.7` per the version-guard requirement.
- `BACKEND_REFACTOR_PLAN.md` Step 4 updated to reflect route handlers moved.

author: ssilvius
body:
## Summary

Dark-mode state variants (hover, active, focus) were clamping at the scale boundary because the ladder step always went toward darker. The state plugin now detects `--dark` in the parent token name and tells `semanticFor` to flip the step direction, so dark states step toward lighter -- the perceptually correct direction on a dark surface.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

### 1. Dark state variants differ from their parent by visible ladder steps toward lighter

The state plugin (`packages/design-tokens/src/plugins/state.ts:29`) checks `input.from.includes('--dark')` and passes `dark: true` through to `semanticFor.pair()`. Inside `statePair` (`packages/color-utils/src/semantic.ts:295-296`), `dark` flips the sign on the rank step: hover steps `rank - 1` and active steps `rank - 2` instead of `+1`/`+2`. A parent at position 950 (rank 10 on the ladder) now lands hover at 900 (rank 9) and active at 800 (rank 8) instead of clamping at 950.
Evidence: test "dark hover/active step toward lighter (lower index), not darker" in `packages/color-utils/test/semantic.test.ts` -- asserts `hoverIdx < 10` and `activeIdx < hoverIdx` across all four seed families.

### 2. Light-mode state selection unchanged (parity tests hold)

The `dark` parameter defaults to `undefined`/`false`, producing `sign = 1` -- identical to the previous hardcoded `+1`/`+2` behavior. The existing parity test suite ("matches the plugin ladder walk for every position and state") covers all seeds x all positions x all states without the `dark` flag and still passes.
Evidence: test "light state stepping is unchanged (parity)" asserts `sem.pair({use:'hover', from:'50'})` equals `sem.pair({use:'hover', from:'50', dark:false})` across all seeds. The full parity block (lines 103-183) runs 4 seeds x 11 positions x 4 states = 176 assertions unchanged.

### 3. Snapshot table reviewed by Sean before locking

The snapshot test "snapshot: dark state positions (REVIEW WITH SEAN BEFORE LOCKING)" generates a table of parent position x state -> dark state position for all four seed families, written to `packages/color-utils/test/__snapshots__/semantic.test.ts.snap`. The snapshot is committed but the test name flags it for review.
Evidence: snapshot block in `semantic.test.ts.snap` starting at "semanticFor -- dark state stepping (#1646: direction-aware) > snapshot: dark state positions".

### 4. huttspawn fixture proves interaction depth in dark

Deferred to 0.0.66 release -- the huttspawn re-import that produces the fixture depends on S2/S4 of #1638 landing first. This PR ships the direction-aware math; the end-to-end palette verification runs when huttspawn re-imports against the full surface system.
Evidence: not yet available -- tracked as a remaining acceptance criterion on #1646, to be closed at re-import time.

### 5. pnpm preflight green

Lefthook pre-commit ran lint, typecheck, and unit tests on both commits. All passed.
Evidence: commit hooks passed on both `c81c89db` and `20c35016`.

## Not done

- huttspawn fixture verification (criterion 4): deferred to the 0.0.66 release cycle when huttspawn re-imports with the full surface system. The math is proven in unit tests; the end-to-end palette verification requires the import pipeline to run against a live project.
- `disabled` state is deliberately unchanged -- it targets the scale midpoint regardless of dark/light, which is the correct behavior (disabled elements reduce contrast toward neutral, not toward the surface direction).

Upgrades `sha2` to 0.11.0, which removed the `asm` feature and selects hardware backends automatically: SHA-NI on x86_64 (as before) and ARMv8 SHA2 intrinsics on aarch64 with runtime detection (previously the portable software implementation by default).

Per-target effect:
- **x86_64 (servers)**: no behavioral change (SHA-NI was already runtime-detected).
- **aarch64 linux (e.g. Graviton) and macos (dev machines)**: hardware SHA-256, ~4.3-5.4x faster.
- **wasm32 and other targets**: portable implementation, as before.

Criterion results on Apple M-series vs the previous default (soft) backend:

```

sha256::hash_message/msg_len=4096      6.90 us  -> 1.49 us  (-78%)
```

author: rabsef-bicrym
body:
Dependent on #14 (base branch). Gives the monitor a surface to sit on — and makes it read as a *plane*, not wainscoting.

## Why the first attempt read flat

The blind shadows painted one uninterrupted pattern across the wall-desk boundary. Same pattern + same angle + same spacing = same surface; no tonal band can argue with that. The stripes *are* the plane.

## The fix: terminate the light, don't bend it

Rather than re-projecting the slat pattern onto a foreshortened desk plane (a junction-continuity problem CSS gradients can't win — a near-miss fold reads worse than none), the window light simply stops at the desk edge:

- A new untransformed `tk-window-light` wrapper around the blinds projection carries one mask that cuts the static slats **and** the sweeping car-pass bars together at the fold, with a short grazing fade just past the edge. It sits outside the `matrix3d`, so the cut is exactly horizontal — a mask inside the transform tilts ~58px across the frame (measured before moving it).
- Physical story: the window has a sill and the shaft descends from a high streetlight; the desk lives in the sill's shadow. Perceptual story: **pattern termination is itself the depth cue** — stripes ending abruptly say "the surface they were painted on ends here."
- The unstriped car-pass glow still floods the desk softly during a pass (bounce light), so the desk participates in events without inheriting the wall's pattern.

## The desk itself

- `tk-desk`: bottom 22% plane — back-edge highlight catching the streetlight (strongest toward the window), dim warm sheen falling away, darkening toward the viewer. Deliberately darker than the wall: equal illumination implies equal orientation.
- `tk-monitor-seat` (replaces the invisible `tk-underglow`): contact shadow at the monitor's base plus the screen's phosphor reflection pooling on the surface in front, breathing on the existing `tk-breathe` cycle. Attached to the monitor element so it stays aligned at any viewport size.

## Verification

Full-res crops at rest and mid-pass: slats terminate at the fold in both states; during a pass the bright bars rake the wall and stop dead at the edge while the desk catches only the soft flood. Mask presence verified via computed style; tilt corrected by the wrapper move. `format` / `lint` / `tsc` / `test:unit` (32) / `test:e2e` (11/11) / `build` all green.

author: asaxcs
body:
## Problem
On Chrome 103 / older Chromium (common on managed Chrome OS devices), opening an expense report from `/search` crashes with `TypeError: filteredActions.toReversed is not a function`. The ErrorBoundary catches this and renders a full-page crash screen.

## Root Cause
`Array.prototype.toReversed()` is ES2023 and only available in Chrome 110+ / Safari 16.4+. On Chrome 103 the method is `undefined`, causing a render-phase crash in `MoneyRequestReportActionsList.tsx:177`.

## Fix
Replace `filteredActions.toReversed()` with `filteredActions.slice().reverse()`. This produces an identical non-mutating reversed copy using only ES5 methods available in all targeted browsers.

## Files Changed
- `src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportActionsList.tsx` — 1 line change

## Test Plan
- Chrome 103 (or `delete Array.prototype.toReversed` in console): open expense report from `/search` → renders normally, no ErrorBoundary
- Modern Chrome: no regression
- Report actions still render newest-first (ordering preserved)

author: andrewh
body:
Closes issue 112 (topology-driven log and event generation).

Adds a `logs:` section to service and operation definitions, following the same design as topology-driven metrics: service-level entries are evaluated for every span in the service, operation-level entries only for that operation.

## DSL

```yaml
services:
  gateway:
    logs:
      - severity: INFO
        body: "handled {operation.name} method={http.request.method}"
    operations:
      handle:
        duration: 15ms
        logs:
          - severity: ERROR
            body: "upstream timeout for {operation.name}"
            condition: error
            at: end
            attributes:
              error.type:
                value: TimeoutError
```

## Features

- **Severity**: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL (case-insensitive), mapped to OTel log data model severity numbers with matching severity text
- **Body templates**: `{key}` placeholders resolve against the record's own attributes, then span attributes, then `service.name`/`operation.name` built-ins; unresolved placeholders stay literal
- **Conditions**: `error`, `success`, `slow` (slow uses `--slow-threshold` and never fires when the flag is unset); omitted = every span
- **Volume control**: per-entry `probability` (0-1)
- **Timing**: `at: start|end` anchor plus `delay` offset, applied to the record timestamp so it works with synthetic/offset time
- **Attributes**: reuses the existing attribute generators (static, weighted, sequence, range, distribution), emitted as typed log attributes
- **Trace correlation**: `SpanInfo` now carries the producing span's `SpanContext`, and records are emitted with it on the context, so every log record (including the derived ones) carries trace/span IDs

## Answers to the issue's design questions

- **Existing hard-coded ERROR/WARN logs**: kept as the default. A service that defines any `logs:` (at either level) replaces the derived logs for that service; other services keep them. The README documents how to recreate the derived behaviour explicitly.
- **Volume control**: one evaluation per matching span, gated by `probability`.
- **Span attribute references**: supported in body templates (log attributes take precedence).
- **Scenario overrides for logs**: out of scope here — a natural follow-up alongside scenario metric overrides.

Span events (issue 86) remain a separate concept; this only covers standalone log records.

## Validation and docs

- `ValidateConfig` checks severity, body, condition, probability range, timing anchor, delay, and attribute generators with the usual contextual error messages
- DSL reference section in `cmd/motel/README.md` and a runnable example at `docs/examples/topology-driven-logs.yaml`

Verified end-to-end with `motel run --stdout --signals traces,logs --slow-threshold 100ms` on the new example: topology logs interpolate span attributes, conditions and probability behave as configured, the no-logs service still emits derived WARN/ERROR records, and all records carry trace/span IDs.

## What Brings the POST Builder closer to the refined prototype (`av-post.jsx`), leading with the **confirm-on-mutation** safety rule the app already applies on the Operations screen. ## Changes - **Send confirmation dialog** — every send is a live write, so `Send` now opens the shared Fluent confirm dialog first: *"Send {METHOD}?"*, the effective URL as the target line, and a **destructive caveat** for PATCH/DELETE (styled danger). Reuses `IDialogService`; the shell wires the real `DialogService` (now injectable, so tests pass a stub). - **Auto If-Match** for PATCH/DELETE (optimistic concurrency); POST clears it. - **Seeded grid defaults** on scaffold — `dataAreaId = "usmf"` and a concrete `false` for Boolean fields — so a write starts closer to ready. - A live **"{Entity} · N field(s) included"** summary under the entity picker. ## Testing - Full Avalonia headless suite green (**385 tests**). New tests: confirm-decline blocks the send (gateway never called), confirm-accept proceeds, destructive methods carry a danger caveat + `Send DELETE` label, keyed-method auto-If-Match, `dataAreaId` seeding, and the included-field count/summary. The shell-routing test injects an `AutoConfirmDialogs` stub so it runs headless. - `DesignLintTests` / `DesignSystemTests` green; clean `dotnet build`. > `AutoConfirmDialogs` is the default when no dialog service is supplied (design-mode / tests not exercising the gate); the composition root injects the real dialog so live mutations are always gated. ## Deferred to a follow-up Kept out of this slice to stay focused: always-on **entity rail / grid-as-default**, the **`$batch` queue**, **saved requests**, the **segmented toned method control**, and the **PK/REQ/→URL** key-section pills. (`cross-company` default stays off — a test pins that.) Part of the multi-slice effort to close the gap to the refined design (Profiles #134, Query Builder #135; a fidelity pass on the remaining screens to follow). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces a **confirm-on-mutation** dialog gate for every POST Builder send (mirroring the Operations screen's pattern), auto-enables `If-Match` for PATCH/DELETE, seeds `dataAreaId`/Boolean grid defaults on scaffold, and adds a live `GridSummary` field-count line under the entity picker. - **Confirm gate** — `ConfirmSendAsync()` shows the shared Fluent dialog before the HTTP call; PATCH/DELETE are styled as destructive with a caveat. `AutoConfirmDialogs` is the headless/design-mode default; `ShellViewModel` injects the real `DialogService` for production so live mutations are always gated. - **Auto If-Match** — switching `Method` to PATCH/DELETE sets `UseIfMatch = true`; switching to POST clears it. The user can override afterward. - **Grid defaults + summary** — `dataAreaId` is seeded `\"USMF\"` and Booleans default to `\"false\"` at load time; `IncludedFieldCount` / `GridSummary` are notified after grid rebuild and after each `Include` toggle.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge; the confirm gate, auto If-Match, and grid defaults are well-scoped and thoroughly tested. All new behaviour is covered by targeted tests (decline-blocks-send, accept-proceeds, danger caveat, method-driven If-Match, dataAreaId seeding, field-count tracking). The composition root correctly injects the real DialogService so the gate is never bypassed in production. The one hardening gap — ConfirmSendAsync being called outside the try-catch — is an unlikely failure path that doesn't affect correctness under normal operation. PostBuilderViewModel.cs — the ConfirmSendAsync call sits just before the try/catch; a dialog-service failure would bypass local error handling.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | avalonia/toolBax.App/ViewModels/PostBuilderViewModel.cs | Adds confirm-on-mutation gate, auto If-Match for PATCH/DELETE, grid defaults, and IncludedFieldCount/GridSummary summary properties; ConfirmSendAsync is called before the try-catch, leaving dialog failures unhandled | | avalonia/toolBax.App/Services/AutoConfirmDialogs.cs | New IDialogService stub that always confirms — used as the design-mode/headless-test default so tests without a UI can exercise the send path without a real window | | avalonia/toolBax.App/ViewModels/ShellViewModel.cs | Wires IDialogService through ShellViewModel constructor; defaults to real DialogService in production and passes it down to PostBuilderViewModel | | avalonia/toolBax.App.Tests/PostBuilderViewModelTests.cs | Adds 6 new targeted tests: confirm-decline blocks send, confirm-accept proceeds, destructive methods carry danger caveat, method-change auto-enables If-Match, dataAreaId seeding, and IncludedFieldCount/GridSummary tracking | | avalonia/toolBax.App.Tests/ShellViewModelTests.cs | Injects AutoConfirmDialogs stub in the shell routing test so it runs headless without opening a real dialog window | | avalonia/toolBax.App/Views/PostBuilderView.axaml | Adds a monospaced TextBlock under the entity picker showing the GridSummary (entity name + included field count), hidden when empty via IsNotNullOrEmpty converter |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[User clicks Send] --> B{CanSend?} B -- No payload issues --> C[ConfirmSendAsync] B -- Has payload issues --> Z[Send disabled] C --> D{Dialog result} D -- Cancelled --> E[StatusText = Send cancelled.\nreturn] D -- Confirmed --> F[IsBusy = true\nStatusText = Sending…] F --> G[client.SendAsync\nmethod, path, body, headers, ct] G -- Success --> H[StatusText = response\nSendSucceeded = true] G -- Exception --> I[StatusText = Request failed.\nResponseBody = ex.Message] H --> J[IsBusy = false] I --> J style C fill:#ffd700,stroke:#b8860b style D fill:#ffd700,stroke:#b8860b style E fill:#ffcccc,stroke:#cc0000 ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `avalonia/toolBax.App/ViewModels/PostBuilderViewModel.cs`, line 319-357 ([link](https://github.com/s0l0m0n8und9/toolbax/blob/7a823c0a29d7727b2c26413675bdf42a9e08a019/avalonia/toolBax.App/ViewModels/PostBuilderViewModel.cs#L319-L357)) **Stale `GridSummary` and `IncludedFieldCount` on early return** `LoadFields()` calls `Fields.Clear()` before the early-return guard, but `OnPropertyChanged` for `IncludedFieldCount` and `GridSummary` is only raised at the *bottom* of the method — never on the early-return path. If `SelectedEntity` is set to `null` while `UseFieldGrid` is true (e.g., the ComboBox selection is cleared), `OnSelectedEntityChanged` calls `LoadFields()`, the grid is emptied, but the view still reads the previous entity's name and count. The `GridSummary` `TextBlock` — bound through `IsVisible` on `StringConverters.IsNotNullOrEmpty` — remains visible with stale text. Fix: move the `OnPropertyChanged` pair before the guard check, or duplicate it on the early-return path so the binding is always notified after `Fields.Clear()`.

author: rossirpaulo
body:
## Summary

- Change `log.info`, `log.debug`, `log.warn`, and `log.error` builtin signatures from `map<string, unknown>` to `unknown`.
- Keep the existing log event schema and runtime extraction path, preserving the user-provided value directly in `LogEvent.data`.
- Update compiler/runtime comments and proto comments to describe general log values instead of structured-map-only payloads.
- Add compiler snapshots, runtime preservation checks, collector coverage, and `baml describe log.info` coverage for the widened API.

## Why

The runtime log pipeline already preserves arbitrary `BexExternalValue` data, but the stdlib signatures restricted callers to structured maps. That made scalar, list, class, enum, and null logging fail typechecking even though the event system could already carry those values.

## User Impact

BAML code can now log any value directly:

```baml
log.info("hello")
log.debug(2)
log.warn(true)
log.error(null)
log.info(my_user)
log.info({ step: 1 })
```

Map payloads continue to represent structured fields, and named-argument call sites using `data:` remain compatible.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p baml_tests event_system`
- `cargo test -p baml_tests __baml_std__`
- `cargo test -p bex_engine test_log`
- `cargo test -p bex_engine test_collector_log_events_extraction`
- `cargo test -p baml_cli render_describe_log_info_builtin`

body:
## What
Temporary, `continue-on-error` diagnostic to capture the worker container's own logs + OOM/exit state on the GitHub-hosted runner.

## Why
The gated `e2e-groundtruth` passes locally (cjson/zlib/lua ground-truth) but fails on CI: the worker spawns (`worker_started`) then the RPC dies ~10s in (`worker-unavailable`) — identically for both the previously-pinned and a freshly-rebuilt worker image. So the cause is the **runner environment**, not the image or the merged code. The adapter removes the worker (`--rm`), so its crash reason is lost.

## How
A standalone smoke step runs the worker with the launcher's exact hardening (no `--rm`) and dumps runner memory/cgroup info, the container exit code + `OOMKilled` state, whether the UDS bound, and `podman logs` — so the next dispatch reveals why the worker dies (suspected JVM OOM under `--memory 4g`, or a rootless/crun limit).

## Scope
Workflow-only; no product/test changes. Removed once the cause is pinned.

author: andrey-embarklabs
body:
The five XNAT data volumes (and the bundled CNPG cluster) defaulted to accessMode ReadWriteMany on a storageClass literally named "default", which is unsatisfiable on a standard EKS/EBS cluster (EBS has no RWX, and few clusters have a class named "default") — PVCs sit Pending on a fresh single-replica install.

- Default the data volumes to ReadWriteOnce.
- Default storageClass to "" so PVCs use the cluster's default StorageClass; the templates omit storageClassName when empty rather than setting it to "" (which would disable dynamic provisioning).
- Same for cnpg.cluster.storage.storageClass; the Cluster template now omits the field when empty.
- Document that multi-replica XNAT or the container-service should set the shared volumes (build, archive) to ReadWriteMany on an RWX class.
