body:
Fixes the bug documented in #416.

`ca-enforcement-gate.sh` (shipped in #410) emits the gate text and then the JSON on a later line:
```bash
echo "$gate_output"
echo '{"continue": false}'
```
Empirically on Craft Agent, that mixed stdout fails to parse, so `continue:false` is silently ignored and the agent proceeds — the gate looks wired but is a **no-op at the moment of truth**. Verified with a probe session: mixed text+JSON → not blocked (probe replied 5s after the emit); single `{"continue": false, "systemMessage": "..."}` → blocked (turn halted, no reply).

This emits one clean JSON object with the gate explanation in `systemMessage`. electinfo verified this exact change blocks (landed locally as `hooks/electinfo/electinfo-ca-enforce.sh`).

Companion finding in #416 also notes `CRAFT_SESSION_ID` is absent from the CA hook env but `session_id` is on stdin (for any scoping the gate later needs).

Refs: #409, #410, #416, #335.

author: rcdw
body:
A Dependabot bump put react-dom on ^19 while react stayed ^18. It built, installed, and served 200s, but the app never mounted (blank page) and reached production. CI did not catch it. Three reasons, all verified:

1. The npmrc file was named `npmrc`, not `.npmrc`, so pnpm never read it (`pnpm config get strict-peer-dependencies` -> undefined). The strict-peer setting added in #36 has been inert since.
2. Even correctly named, strict-peer cannot catch this class: with autoInstallPeers on, the react-dom 19 bump resolves against react 18 and is baked into the lockfile as satisfied, so there is no unmet peer. The lockfile-only strict re-resolve exits 0 against that lockfile.
3. The build job's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` replays the lockfile and never evaluates peers, so it stays green too.

Fix: assert the installed react/react-dom (and their @types) majors match, inspecting what is actually installed so the lockfile games above cannot hide it. Added as a step in the build job after the existing frozen install (no extra install cost). Proven red on an 18+19 split, green on a matched pair.

Also rename `npmrc` -> `.npmrc` so strict-peer is finally active as local defence-in-depth, and add Node globals for scripts/ in the eslint config. Removes the ineffective peer-check job it replaces.

## Summary

Adds a thin bridge between EmailMessage and the existing event spine so that calendar invitations (iCalendar text/calendar attachments) can be expressed in GMEOW without duplicating the event model.

## Constitution principles

- Principle 4 (One canonical source): Reuses gmeow:Event from events.ttl and gmeow:EventInvitation from calendar.ttl; email module only adds bridge terms.
- Principle 5 (Maximal bridging by reference): iCalendar METHOD/UID aligned to icaltzd by reference; schema:about used as a loose skos:relatedMatch for describesEvent.
- Principle 9 (Inclusive without overtyping): Calendar invitation categories overlap, so modeled as a MessageKind value individual rather than a hard subclass. iCalendar METHOD is an open value vocabulary (CalendarMethod), not a free literal.

author: copilot
body:
After a game ends, clicking through to start another round was sending players back out of the active lobby context. That broke the rematch flow and prevented the original host from reliably returning as host and starting the next game.

- **Rematch transition**
  - Treat `GAME_ENDED -> WAITING_FOR_PLAYERS` as a rematch return, not a full exit from the multiplayer session.
  - Pass rematch context from `GameTable` back to the app shell instead of using the generic lobby-exit path.

- **Lobby session preservation**
  - Keep the per-game lobby session entry in storage during rematch return.
  - Preserve the active `?gameId=` URL so the client re-enters the same lobby instead of the top-level lobby screen.

- **Host continuity**
  - Recompute and persist host status during the rematch transition using the current game/player identity.
  - Preserve the local player's lobby identity so the same host can start the game again without re-creating the room.

- **State cleanup**
  - Clear in-game session state while retaining the lobby session needed for rematch.
  - Reset app-level transient game/chat state so the client rehydrates cleanly into the lobby view.

```tsx
if (prev === 'GAME_ENDED' && curr === 'WAITING_FOR_PLAYERS') {
  onBackRef.current?.({ preserveLobby: true, game });
}
```

This changes the post-game path from “leave game” to “return to the same multiplayer lobby,” which keeps the room, host role, and restart flow intact.

Unregister listeners while the controls are still alive, then remove the container.

Wired into all six plugins ([lifecycle] tag). The dangling read passes by luck in a plain Release build, so a valgrind-nightly job (xvfb + memcheck) runs the lifecycle tests across all plugins to catch regressions.

body:
## Summary

Add two Google Apps Script files that automate host communications for Merritt Wellness events: a post-event review request sent the morning after an event ends, and a 24-hour pre-event reminder with onboarding details.

## Key Changes

- **`reviewEmails.gs`** — Sends Google review requests to event hosts the morning after their event
  - Parses booking system event descriptions to extract organizer and contact details
  - Implements per-event skip tags (`[skip-review]`) and automatic filtering (Sunday services, internal staff)
  - Tracks sent emails with a 60-day cooldown per host to avoid spam
  - Handles recurring events: skips all recurring by default, or sends once per series if enabled
  - Includes lightweight, spam-safe HTML email design with plain-text fallback
  - Provides test functions (`testRun()`, `previewEmailToSelf()`, `previewReviewWithSampleData()`)

- **`reminderEmails.gs`** — Sends 24-hour pre-event reminders with onboarding info
  - Reuses parsing and host-lookup logic from `reviewEmails.gs`
  - Includes Wi-Fi credentials, onboarding video links, and day-of contact info
  - Tracks reminders per event/series to prevent duplicates on re-runs
  - Provides `seedExistingRecurringSeries()` to pre-mark existing recurring bookings so long-time partners aren't reminded
  - Matches the review email's design system and deliverability practices

- **`README.md`** — Documents setup, configuration, and deliverability best practices
  - Explains the intentional lightweight design (no images, multipart MIME, plain inline CSS)
  - Lists test functions and configuration steps
  - Notes the dependency: `reminderEmails.gs` requires shared helpers from `reviewEmails.gs`

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Spam-safe design**: Both emails deliberately avoid images, heavy HTML, and external resources. They include matching plain-text bodies to maintain a healthy text-to-markup ratio and stay out of spam folders.
- **Shared styling helpers**: `mwEmailShell()`, `mwButton()`, `mwParagraph()` and color constants are defined once in `reviewEmails.gs` and reused by `reminderEmails.gs`.
- **Flexible host lookup**: Tries three strategies in order: parsed "Email:" field from booking description, first non-excluded guest, or any email in the description.
- **Recurring event handling**: Review emails can skip all recurring or send once per series; reminder emails track by series ID so the first occurrence sends and later ones are skipped.
- **Tracking sheet**: Both scripts log to a shared Google Sheet with separate tabs (`ReviewRequests` and `ReminderEmails`) to prevent duplicate sends and enforce cooldowns.

body:
## Summary

Adds `messages.QueryBuilder.GetMediaGroup(ctx, peer, msgID)` to fetch every message belonging to the same media group (album) as a given message — the gotd equivalent of pyrogram's `get_media_group`.

Implementation:
- Fetches a window of messages around the anchor (`msgID ± (10-1)`, the max album span), via `channels.getMessages` for channel peers and `messages.getMessages` otherwise.
- Reads the anchor's `grouped_id` and returns all fetched messages sharing it, sorted by ID.
- Returns an error if the message is not found or is not part of a media group.

Usage:

```go
group, err := query.NewQuery(api).Messages().GetMediaGroup(ctx, peer, msgID)
```

## Test

`TestGetMediaGroup` covers the user-peer path, the channel-peer path (asserting `InputChannel` construction), and the not-in-a-group error case, using `tgmock`.

Fixes #884

author: efpiva
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Gateway diagnostics OTEL trust path for runtime-managed plugin installs.

Lobster/OpenClaw FRE showed `diagnostics-otel` loading from the configured package path but still logging:

```text
diagnostics-otel: internal diagnostics capability unavailable
```

RCA: Gateway runtime load context retained `plugins.installs` for discovery, but did not pass those runtime install records into the plugin metadata snapshot. The lower-level loader correctly kept raw config-authored install records untrusted, so the diagnostics plugin could load but never receive `internalDiagnostics` and therefore never forward Gateway OTEL batches.

This PR now:

- threads runtime config install records into `resolvePluginMetadataSnapshot` from `resolvePluginRuntimeLoadContext`
- preserves the existing safety boundary: direct user-authored config install records remain untrusted unless they are in the trusted installed-index/runtime context
- adds Gateway-effective trust coverage proving persisted/runtime records make `diagnostics-otel` trusted before services start
- keeps spoofed/wrong-path/non-official install records untrusted
- keeps service-context coverage for `internalDiagnostics` grants to trusted diagnostics exporters

## Verification

RED/GREEN:

- RED: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/runtime/load-context.test.ts -t "passes runtime config install records into the metadata snapshot"`
  - failed because `installRecords` was not passed to `resolvePluginMetadataSnapshot`
- GREEN: same command passed after the fix

Focused validation:

```bash
git diff --check
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  src/plugins/loader.test.ts \
  src/plugins/loader.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-registry-installed.test.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-registry.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/load-context.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/load-context.ts \
  src/plugins/gateway-effective-trust.test.ts

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/load-context.test.ts \
  src/plugins/gateway-effective-trust.test.ts

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts \
  -t "diagnostics-otel|trusted official|user-authored"

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-registry-installed.test.ts \
  -t "diagnostics-otel|official|untrusted"

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts \
  src/plugins/services.test.ts \
  -t "grants internal diagnostics only to trusted diagnostics exporter services"

OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-include-loader.json \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts \
  -t "keeps user-authored diagnostics-otel config install records untrusted during plugin load"
```

All commands above passed after the fix. A full `loader.test.ts` run was attempted, but the repo wrapper terminated it after 120s of no output; the targeted security regression from that file passed.

## Deployed evidence driving this PR

Lobster PR #2858 fixed the baked install-record/package version drift and deployed to FRE301 in OpenClaw builds `26.162.04`, `26.162.05`, and `26.162.06`. Kusto still showed fresh Gateway startups with:

- `diagnostics-otel` plugin loaded
- Gateway ready
- zero `OpenClaw Gateway OTEL batch forwarded` rows
- persistent `diagnostics-otel: internal diagnostics capability unavailable`

This PR addresses the remaining OpenClaw runtime trust propagation gap.

author: svilgelm
body:
## Overview

`DataProxyService.GetActionData` materialises action inputs/outputs by fetching `inputs.pb`/`outputs.pb` via the URIs returned by `RunService.GetActionDataURIs`. For **condition** actions (`ACTION_TYPE_CONDITION`) the literals don't live in object storage at all — the signal payload lives inline on the action row (`RunInfo.Output`). The run service signals this case by returning **both URIs empty**.

Today the dataproxy hits that empty-URIs case, skips both S3 fetches, and returns its zero-value skeleton `{Inputs: {}, Outputs: {}}` — losing the literal even though the run service has it ready to hand back inline.

This PR adds a small fallback: when both URIs come back empty, call `RunService.GetActionData` once and pass its inline `Inputs`/`Outputs` straight through. Tasks/traces are unaffected — they always have a non-empty inputs URI from RecordAction time.

## Why not unconditionally?

We don't want to lose the dataplane-fetch optimisation for tasks/traces (they hold large literals in S3 and the dataproxy is co-located with the bucket). The fallback only triggers when `urisResp.inputs_uri == "" && urisResp.outputs_uri == ""` — which today only happens for condition actions.

## Changes

- `flyteidl2/dataproxy/service/dataproxy_service.go` — new condition fallback branch in `Service.GetActionData`, gated on both URIs empty. Logs at debug level so the call site is easy to spot in traces.
- The `RunService.GetActionData` call is marked deprecated (in favour of `DataProxyService.GetActionData`), but calling ourselves would loop, so a `//nolint:staticcheck` directive explains the intentional reach-into.

## Test plan

- `make test` (flyte2 unit tests).
- Manually verified on dogfood-cloud-staging: a signaled BOOLEAN condition that previously returned `{"inputs":{}, "outputs":{}}` now returns `{"outputs":{"literals":[{"name":"<condition_name>","value":{"scalar":{"primitive":{"boolean":true}}}}]}}`.

## Upstream context

This is part of a larger end-to-end fix in `unionai/cloud` ([PR #16408](https://github.com/unionai/cloud/pull/16408)) that plumbs condition signal payloads inline through:

1. actions-service `Update.output` proto field (closed-source)
2. RedisStream replicator + workflow consumer carrying the literal
3. workflow service merging the literal into `RunInfo.Output`
4. **dataproxy fallback (this PR)** to surface the inline literal to the UI

author: vppillai
body:
## Root cause
The deploy workflow read instance booleans with `yq '.carry_over_balance // true'`. In yq/jq, `//` substitutes the default when the value is null **or false** — so eatout's explicit `carry_over_balance: false` has deployed as `true` since day one (confirmed via the Lambda env and the float fingerprint in the ledger). Decision: keep full carry-over as the semantics (config now honestly says `true`) and make the carried amount **visible** instead of silently folding it into totals.

## Changes
**Workflows** — read booleans raw, default only when the key is absent (explicit `false` now honored in both deploy workflows).

**Backend**
- `roundCents()` at the service boundary + month-summary construction. `CreateMonth` computed `starting + allowance` in float64 and marshaled full precision: prod contains `-22.159999999999968` (= `-522.16 + 500`). Deltas already used `%.2f`; this closes the absolute-value writes and JSON inputs.
- `ensureMonthExists` now carries the previous ending when carry-over is on — an expense filed into a not-yet-created month no longer breaks the carry chain.
- New tests: prod-replay rounding (asserts the *marshaled string* — dusty vs clean differ by ~1 ULP, invisible to tolerance compares), auto-create carry matrix, amount rounding. Plus `gofmt` on three drifted files.

**Frontend**
- "Carried from May: −$522.16" line in the balance card (hidden when zero). Previously a carried deficit was invisible: This Month read **+$346.60 green** while the real position was **−$175.56**.
- Expenses line gains budget context: `$153.40 spent of $500.00`.

**Follow-up after merge:** one-time cleanup of the June ledger row's float dust; tag v2.2.5.

author: dereuromark
body:
Aligns carve-rs ordered-list nesting on **Model A**, matching carve-php. ## Rule - The **content column** gates **only ordered** markers (ordered does not interrupt a paragraph, §10): a below-column ordered marker folds into the item paragraph (`1. a` / ` 1. b` -> `
  • a\n1. b
    • `); an at/above-column one nests. - **Unordered/task** markers interrupt (§10), so they nest at any indent past the base -- the content column does not gate them. - A **task's content column is the bullet width (2)** (the checkbox is content), so a task child at column 2 nests, matching the spec's task attribute/continuation convention. carve-rs previously nested any marker indented past the base, so a 2-space ordered child nested instead of folding. ## Correctness Matches carve-php on the full nesting matrix. Spec corpus + suite pass, clippy/fmt clean. A 400-case list fuzz vs `main` changes only inputs containing an indented ordered marker. Adds tests. Pairs with carve-js#109 and the carve-php (already correct) behavior.

author: danielkortan
body:
Follow-ups to #305, hardening the player-name identity tooling. Found while preparing the "Nicholas Kurtz → Nick Kurtz" fix instructions.

## 1. `POST /api/mlb/roster-fix` purge guard (the big one)

The unrostered branch purged **every** unrostered name. It predates the catalog-seeded pool, so running it today would:
- purge thousands of legitimate bootstrap pool entries (gutting the swap-form player pool until the next boot/4am refresh), and
- because the `rostered` set is a pre-pass snapshot, purge a **rename target written seconds earlier in the same pass** — e.g. mapping `Nicholas Kurtz → Nick Kurtz` would rename him onto Cam's roster and then purge "Nick Kurtz" (still unrostered in the snapshot), stripping the player from the roster and deleting the just-assigned id claim.

Purging now happens in a guarded second pass that skips: catalog-exact fullNames, names with a valid `mlb_ids` claim (the "Max Muncy (LAD)" duplicate keys from #305), and rename targets from the same pass. Genuinely mismatched unrostered names (typo'd legacy entries) are still purged as designed. `roster-audit` similarly stops reporting catalog-exact unrostered names, so the report shows real mismatches instead of ~2k pool entries.

## 2. `period_submissions` coverage

`renamePlayerInSeason`, `purgePlayerFromSeason`, and `extractSeasonPlayerNames` only handled `initial_submissions`. A renamed PP2/QF/SF/Finals player's submission record kept the stale name. All three now cover the period buckets.

## 3. Pool dedupe in `bootstrapPlayerPools`

A name-fix rename landing on a name the bootstrap already added left the player listed twice in the pool array (twice in the swap search). The bootstrap now dedupes both pool arrays in place, order-preserving and idempotent (verified with a mock-catalog harness: dedupe flags `changed: true` once, second run `changed: false`).

## Scoring invariant

No scoring inputs change. The purge guard only **reduces** what roster-fix deletes; submission-bucket coverage keeps derived records consistent with renames the commissioner explicitly applies; pool dedupe is display/availability-only.

Also appends today's name-identity decisions to MEMORY.md (including the "missing team label = possibly unattributed stats" diagnostic tell and the don't-mix-rename-and-swap warning).

`npm test` (84/84), `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` all pass.

Scream, but not be heard.

author: hugo0
body:
## Summary

When an iOS third-party credential provider (1Password) wedges, every passkey assertion during transaction signing throws `NotAllowedError` until the provider is unlocked or the device restarts. Users hitting this mid-send saw the generic **"There was an issue with your request. Please contact support."** — a dead end for a failure that a retry (after unlocking/rebooting) fixes. **45 users hit this in the last 30 days, 40 confirmed iOS** (TASK-20000, Crisp user `ariel`: 4 failed send attempts on 2026-06-06, QR payment succeeded on a later retry).

- `ErrorHandler` now maps the iOS Safari message ("not allowed by the user agent…") to retry/unlock-your-password-manager guidance. Only the *timeout* variant was mapped before.
- iOS `PASSKEY_TROUBLESHOOTING_STEPS.NotAllowedError` now leads with the password-manager unlock hint and ends with device restart (the two fixes that actually work in the field).
- New `passkey_sign_failed` PostHog event (`error_name`, `context`) emitted from the two low-level signing entry points (`useZeroDev.handleSendUserOpEncoded`, `useSignUserOp.signCallsUserOp`) via `capturePasskeySignFailure`, which no-ops for non-WebAuthn errors. Spend-bundle EIP-712 failures already carry `error_kind` on `card_withdraw_failed`, so they're intentionally not double-captured.

## Risks / breaking changes

None expected. Copy + analytics only; no flow logic changed. No backend involvement. The new ErrorHandler branch sits after the existing WebAuthn-timeout matcher and before the generic fallback, so existing mappings are untouched (ordering covered by tests).

## QA

- `npm test` — new tests: verbatim prod error message → new copy; ordering guard for the existing timeout variant; `capturePasskeySignFailure` captures for `NotAllowedError` and ignores non-WebAuthn errors.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `pnpm prettier --check .` all green locally.
- Manual repro of the wedged-provider state isn't feasible in sandbox; the mapped string is the verbatim DOMException message captured in PostHog $exception events from prod.

author: utkarshbhardwaj007
body:
## Summary

Adds the **Web3 Summit** network and makes the active network selectable via a single `ACTIVE_TESTNET_ENV` constant in `src/config.ts`. Switching a release to Summit becomes a one-line PR; a guard test ensures that PR only goes green once Summit is genuinely ready. Also consolidates env-specific values to a single source of truth.

## Why

The CLI duplicated network endpoints between `src/config.ts` and `@parity/polkadot-app-deploy`'s `environments.json`, and several `--env` defaults / user-facing strings hardcoded `paseo-next-v2` / "Paseo". That made a network switch error-prone (two copies could silently diverge; `deploy --env summit` would have been rejected and the default wouldn't have moved).

## What changed

- **`config.ts`** — `ENV_IDS` is the single source for both the `Env` type and `ENV_FLAG_CHOICES` (the `--env` values). Added the `SUMMIT` block (endpoints mirror `environments.json`), a per-env `cdmEnvName`, promoted `faucetUrl` to a live field, removed three dead fields (`identityBackendUrl`, `appViewerOrigin`, `bulletinAuthorizeV2`).
- **`config.test.ts`** (new) — divergence guard: reads polkadot-app-deploy's `environments.json` via its public `loadEnvironments()` and asserts every wired env's endpoints/network/gateway match upstream, and that the default env's CDM meta-registry address is non-empty. This **blocks the Summit flip from merging until it's ready**.
- **`registry.ts` / `contract.ts`** — the CDM meta-registry address is resolved per-env from `@parity/cdm-env` (`getRegistryAddress(cdmEnvName)`), never hardcoded; `cdm.json` (generated by `cdm i`) is left untouched. Clear error when the address is empty.
- **`deploy` / `deploy-all` / `decentralize`** — `--env` now honours `DEFAULT_ENV` and the single-sourced choices, so the switch moves every command and `--env summit` is accepted.
- **`funder.ts`** — faucet URL sourced from config.
- **`connection.ts` / `bulletinTopUp.ts`** — error messages name the active network via `getNetworkLabel()`; documented why `paseo_*` descriptors are reused for all envs (matches `@parity/cdm-env`'s `w3s → paseo` mapping; the deploy engine is descriptor-free).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — deployment-doc checklist for switching to Summit, including the upstream-SDK audit (product-sdk and triangle-js-sdks need no changes; the only pending dependency is `@parity/cdm-env` shipping the `w3s` registry address).

## How to switch to Summit later (one line)

1. Confirm `@parity/cdm-env` ships a non-empty `w3s` registry address (bump if needed).
2. Flip `ACTIVE_TESTNET_ENV` to `"summit"`.
3. `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` — the guard is the gate.

## Out of scope

The `PAS` token symbol remains hardcoded (no source-of-truth field; both networks are 12-decimal so math is unaffected — only the label could be wrong on Summit). Tracked for a follow-up before the actual flip.

## Verification

`pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint:license`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` — all pass (784 tests).

author: bindreams
body:
Closes #496.

## Why

`mock_plugin_path()` ran `cargo build -p mock-plugin` inside every nextest test process and spawned the uplift destination `target/debug/mock-plugin`. On macOS cargo uplifts via `fs::copy` (Gatekeeper workaround, rust-lang/cargo#10196), so `is_same_file` is always false and **every** sibling no-op build re-runs `remove_file` + `fs::copy` on the destination — a recurring ENOENT window that concurrent spawns hit (the PR #483 darwin/arm64 flake; locally reproduced: 994 ENOENT observations across 50 no-op builds when emulating the copy-uplift). The runtime build also violated the archive lane's "no Rust toolchain on test runners" contract and recompiled the fixture from scratch inside tests (~23 s) on all 6 platforms.

## What

- `mock-plugin` is now an ungated, auto-discovered bin of the **garter** package (`src/bin/mock-plugin.rs`) — cargo builds it before garter's tests under every invocation; `package.exclude` keeps the published crates.io crate lib-only (`cargo install garter` stays bin-free).
- Tests locate it via one shared helper (`tests/common/mod.rs`): runtime `CARGO_BIN_EXE_mock-plugin` (nextest-remapped under `--archive-file`) with compile-time `env!` fallback — the `handle-holders`/`tombstone` pattern. No cargo at test runtime, anywhere.
- CI archive lane: archives the fixture as a non-test binary, passes `--features garter/test-utils` explicitly (for `tap_integration`) instead of relying on galoshes' dev-dep edge, and dispatches via `cargo-nextest` so the test jobs are genuinely toolchain-free. `.config/nextest.toml` pins `nextest-version = "0.9.130"` — the floor for runtime `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` injection under archives.
- Clippy lanes (`clippy-hole`, `clippy-ex-galoshes`, prek `cargo-clippy`) gain `--features garter/test-utils`, fixing a pre-existing gap where `tap_integration` was never linted.
- New prek hook `no-cargo-in-tests` forbids `Command::new("cargo")` in test code so the pattern cannot return.
- `crates/mock-plugin` package dissolved; all references updated (build.yaml targets + manifest-test pins, release path filters, NOTICES, CONTRIBUTING, release-notes test fixture).

Also fixes the helper's latent profile bug (the env var always matches the compiled profile; the old code built debug but probed `target/release` under release tests).

## How verified

- TDD: locator switched first → compile error (RED); bin moved in → 109/109 garter+garter-bin tests (GREEN); `cargo nextest list` diff vs main = zero tests lost.
- Archive-lane proof on nextest 0.9.137: archive built exactly as CI ("9 binaries, including 1 non-test binary"; manifest records `garter → mock-plugin bin-exe`), then run from the archive **with the workspace binary renamed away** — 109/109 pass, proving spawns use the runtime-remapped extraction path; no cargo output during the test phase.
- Bare `cargo nextest run -p garter` and plain `cargo test -p garter --no-default-features` pass from a fresh state (no prebuilt fixture) — the plain-cargo workflow that the first iteration regressed is intact.
- `cargo package -p garter` verify-builds green; the package contains nothing under `src/bin/` or `tests/`.
- `cargo xtask run garter-tests` / `garter-bin-tests` / `galoshes-tests`, `cargo nextest run -p xtask`, and `prek run --all-files` all green; the new hook verified to fire on a synthetic violation.

author: mousebrains
body:
## Summary

Full scientific-accuracy review of the package, performed by auditing the chi, scor160, rsi, and perturb/processing subpackages against the ODAS MATLAB Library v4.5.1 (the reference implementation in `odas/`) and the primary literature, then fixing every verified finding. Six commits: four code-fix commits (grouped by subsystem), one documentation overhaul, one lint cleanup.

**Validation:** full suite green (2,313 passed / 10 skipped, up from 2,309 baseline — 4 new regression tests), `ruff check` and `mypy` clean, ATOMIX L2→L4 benchmark agreement verified unchanged or improved on VMP250 Tidal (both variants), MR1000 Minas Passage, and Epsilometer datasets, and the Method-1 chi workflow verified end-to-end on `SN479_0006.p`.

A prior audit round (AUDIT.md, 2026-03) had graded "Mathematical correctness: A — every formula verified." This review found several formula-level errors that integral-only tests could not catch; an addendum was added to AUDIT.md.

---

## 1. Chi (thermal variance dissipation) — `src/odas_tpw/chi/`

### 1.1 Wrong 1-D Kraichnan gradient spectrum shape (critical — default model)

`batchelor.py: kraichnan_grad` implemented

```
S(k) = q·χ/(3·κ_T·kB²) · k · (1 + √(6q)·y) · e^(−√(6q)·y),   y = k/kB
```

which is the **3-D** Kraichnan scalar spectrum of Bogucki et al. (1997, eq. 11) rescaled to the right integral — not the 1-D along-path gradient spectrum a profiler measures. The isotropic transform G₁(k₁) = k₁²∫ₖ₁^∞ E(k)/k dk evaluates **in closed form** for the Kraichnan shape (the exponential-integral terms cancel exactly, via d/dk[−k⁻¹e^(−ak)] = (k⁻² + ak⁻¹)e^(−ak)) to

```
S(k) = q·χ/(κ_T·kB²) · k · e^(−√(6q)·y)
```

— the same expression as Peterson & Fer (2014, eq. 8). The derivation was verified independently, and cross-checked by applying the identical transform to Bogucki eq. 9, which reproduces the Dillon & Caldwell (1980) 1-D Batchelor form exactly.

**Impact:** `kraichnan` is the default `spectrum_model` everywhere. The wrong shape peaks at 1.618·kB/√(6q) instead of kB/√(6q), biasing Method-2 kB low by ~×0.62 (hence ε_T = (2πkB)⁴νκ² low by ~×7) and Method-1 χ high by up to ~3×.

**Why tests missed it:** both forms integrate to χ/(6κ_T), and the only existing test checked the integral. Added `test_peak_location` (pins the shape) and `test_low_k_amplitude` (pins the viscous-convective amplitude) so this class of error cannot recur.

### 1.2 FP07 electronics noise off by speed² (critical)

`fp07.py: gradT_noise` multiplied the noise by speed; `noise_thermchannel` outputs **time-derivative** noise [(K/s)²/Hz] (its `G_HP` factor contains (2πf)²), so converting to a gradient spectrum requires dividing by speed² (dT/dz = (dT/dt)/W) then multiplying by speed (per-Hz → per-cpm): net **divide** by speed. ODAS `gradT_noise_odas.m:341` does `scale_factor ./ speed` before squaring — confirmed line-by-line.

**Impact:** noise floor wrong by speed² at any speed ≠ 1 m/s (≈2× low at 0.7 m/s, ~11× low at glider speeds), corrupting the `spec_obs > 2·noise` validity mask, K_max selection, the model noise floor in all fits, and fom. Fixed in `gradT_noise` and `gradT_noise_batch`; docstring units corrected.

### 1.3 Default iterative chi fit ignored in-band FP07 attenuation (critical)

`chi.py: _iterative_fit` (the default `fit_method`) integrated the observed spectrum over [k_l, k_u] without ever compensating the thermistor response |H|², and its out-of-band corrections used the unattenuated model — so in-band attenuation (half-power at ~19 cpm for τ≈12 ms at 0.7 m/s, vs kB of 50–500 cpm) was never restored → **χ biased low** by tens of percent to ~2×. Method 1 and the MLE path already handled this via `_variance_correction`. Fix: extended `_variance_correction` with a band lower limit and replaced the additive tails with the band-limited model variance ratio (V_total over V_resolved-with-|H|²), equivalent in expectation to Peterson & Fer's response-boosted integration but robust at low SNR.

### 1.4 Other chi fixes

- **MLE path noise subtraction**: `_mle_fit_kB` re-estimated χ from ∫spec_obs without subtracting the noise floor (biased high near the floor); now consistent with the iterative path.
- **Thermistor calibration dropped from the noise model**: `l3_chi.py` filtered out `b`, `T_0`, `beta_2` before calling the noise model, and `chi_io._extract_therm_cal` looked up `"T_0"` although `parse_config` lowercases all keys — so `T_0` was *never* extracted. Both fixed.
- **Method-1 time pairing**: `argmin(|t_eps − t_chi|)` would pair a chi window with an epsilon estimate arbitrarily far away (failed estimates, different window grids). Now rejected beyond one epsilon-window spacing.
- `fom` NetCDF attribute now states explicitly it is the observed/model variance ratio, **not** the MAD-based ATOMIX/Rockland FM.

---

## 2. Epsilon — `src/odas_tpw/scor160/` and `src/odas_tpw/rsi/`

### 2.1 fom vs FM definitional swap in QC (critical)

The QC flag thresholded `fom` (observed/Nasmyth **variance ratio**; good ≈ 1.0, can be < 1) against 1.15 — the ATOMIX limit defined for the **MAD-based Lueck (2022) FM statistic** (good → 0). The code implemented FM correctly but `process_l4` never computed it (`num_ffts=0`), and `compare.py` compared the variance ratio against the benchmark's MAD-based FOM.

**Fix:** `process_l4` now receives `num_ffts`/`n_v`, computes FM, stores it in `L4Data` and the L4 NetCDF (with a precise `comment` attribute), flags on FM when available, and the benchmark comparison uses it. The viewers' Method-1 epsilon filter also now uses FM.

**Evidence this is right:** benchmark FOM comparison went from **negative correlation** (−0.48/−0.76, RMS diff ~0.35) to **+0.75–0.98** (RMS 0.05–0.12) — the benchmark reference FOM is indeed the MAD-based statistic. Epsilon agreement unchanged (100% within factor 2).

### 2.2 Unsorted polynomial roots in the spectral-minimum search

`np.roots` returns eigenvalues in arbitrary order; the code took `roots[0]` where ODAS takes the **lowest** qualifying minimum (`sort(roots(pd1))`, `get_diss_odas.m:590,597`). With two minima above 10 cpm the integration limit could extend into the noise floor, biasing ε high. Now `np.min(roots)`.

### 2.3 Corrupted spectral bins zeroed instead of handled

NaN/Inf bins were replaced with 0, which (a) silently removed variance from the integrals and (b) entered the log-space polynomial fit as log10(1e-30) = −30 outliers, dragging the fitted spectral minimum. Now follows the ODAS convention (`get_diss_odas.m:577-587`): a single interior bad bin is interpolated from neighbours; multiple bad bins invalidate the estimate (NaN, flags=255). The polynomial fit additionally excludes zero bins, and the ISR flyer-removal index mapping was fixed for the case where non-positive ratio bins are present (indices into a compressed array were applied to the uncompressed range).

### 2.4 X_ISR and the ISR method-switch margin — evidence-based decision

Both review agents flagged `X_ISR = 0.01` (ODAS v4.5.1 ships an experimental 0.02: "test pushing this upward") and the hidden `ISR_MARGIN = 1.6` (whose code comment claimed it compensated a 2–4% e₁ offset — arithmetically impossible). I ran the controlled experiments on the local ATOMIX data:

| Configuration | VMP250 agreement (p1/p2) | VMP250_cs agreement | MR1000 per-probe mean log₁₀ error |
|---|---|---|---|
| X_ISR=0.01, margin=1.6 (current) | 96.9% / 100% | 96.9% / 93.8% | ~+0.02 |
| X_ISR=0.02, margin=1.0 (ODAS v4.5.1) | 96.9% / 84.4% | 93.8% / 87.5% | +0.05…+0.08 |
| X_ISR=0.01, margin=1.0 | 96.9% / 84.4% | 93.8% / 87.5% | — |

The margin, not X_ISR, drives the agreement; without it the pipeline selects ISR far more often than the references (37.5% vs 21.9%). **Decision: keep both values**, but the margin is now a named constant (`DEFAULT_ISR_MARGIN`) exposed as an `isr_margin` parameter, with an honest comment documenting the evidence — and X_ISR carries the benchmark rationale.

### 2.5 Silent temperature failures

body:
💡 What: The optimization implemented
Batched consecutive database operations via `Promise.all` in the `/api/chat` route of `server.js`.

🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
The application was making multiple sequential database calls (e.g. `getUserPatterns`, `getUserSessions`, `getRecentUserMessages`, and multiple `saveMessage` and `recordPattern` operations) via Supabase over HTTP. Awaiting each network call sequentially incurs significant artificial latency.

📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement
Significantly reduces endpoint latency by transforming N sequential HTTP roundtrips into batched concurrent requests. Response times for the `/api/chat` endpoint should visibly improve, saving roughly `(N-1) * (network latency)` per request.

🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
Inspect the `/api/chat` response times in your browser's network tab or by using a performance profiling tool before and after this change. The time taken from request start to the LLM fetch block should be drastically reduced.

author: dev-chezgoulet
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of temporal awareness for /ask. Adds parallel fact retrieval to queryContext, appending facts with their temporal metadata (valid_from, valid_until, created_at) to the LLM context. Updates the Synthesize prompt to instruct the LLM to use temporal metadata for time-ordered reasoning.

## Changes

### internal/server/handlers.go
- After chunk search in queryContext, performs a parallel Qdrant search on the **facts collection** with the same query embedding and topK
- New `appendFactContext()` helper that embeds the query, searches facts, and returns a formatted block:
  ```
  ── Facts ──

  [Fact: key | Created: ts | Valid from: ts | Valid until: ts | Score: X.XXX]
  fact value text
  ```
- Guarded by `s.facts != nil` — silent degradation on missing facts collection

### internal/llm/client.go
- Appended to Synthesize prompt: "If facts include temporal metadata (Valid from / Valid until), use it to determine which fact was active at the time of the question. If the question asks about a specific time period, only use facts whose validity range overlaps with that period."

### docs/specs/SPEC-temporal-awareness-complete.md
- New specification document covering the full temporal awareness design

## Why This Matters

Temporal reasoning categories (temporal-order, temporal-reasoning, knowledge-update) are the single biggest accuracy gap at 22-46%. Chunk headers from Phase 1 help document ordering but don't touch facts. This PR closes the gap by making fact temporal metadata visible during synthesis.

## Verification

- gofmt clean (verified locally)
- No Go toolchain in dev container for go vet — CI will validate
- Spec file documents the full data flow and error handling

## Related
- Phase 1: PR #739 (chunk headers + prefer-later-chunks prompt)
- Issue #733 (temporal awareness)
- Issue #691 (benchmark quality)

author: michaeltrefry
body:
Closes [sc-4066](https://app.shortcut.com/trefry/story/4066) (F-078).

`dets.sort_by(|a, b| b.score.partial_cmp(&a.score).unwrap())` in SCRFD NMS panics if any detection score is NaN. Scores come straight off a model readback, so a corrupted checkpoint or numeric blow-up turned into a process panic inside `Scrfd::detect` — crashing every consumer (`FaceAnalysis::analyze`, PuLID, InstantID) instead of returning zero detections.

**Fix:**
- **NMS sort** → `b.score.total_cmp(&a.score)` (no `unwrap`): deterministic IEEE total order, never panics.
- **Decode filter** → also drop non-finite scores (`!score.is_finite() || score < score_thresh`) so a NaN/inf never enters `detections` in the first place. The old `score < score_thresh` let NaN through because NaN comparisons are always false.

**Test:** added a weight-free `nms` unit test — a NaN-scored detection doesn't panic the sort, and the finite scores stay in descending order.

**Validation:** `cargo clippy -p mlx-gen-face --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; tests pass (1 new); `cargo fmt --check` clean.
